tishomingo-oklahoma.s: Tishomingo is a city in Johnston County, south-central Oklahoma, United States, named after the Chickasaw leader Tishomingo. It became the capital of the Chickasaw Nation after the nation's 1856 constitution separated it from the Choctaw, and the granite Chickasaw National…

tupelo-mississippi.s: Tupelo is a city in north-eastern Mississippi, United States, the seat of Lee County. It lies in the heart of the old Chickasaw homeland, and the battles of Ackia and Ogoula Tchetoka between the Chickasaw and the French in 1736 were fought nearby.

tumbuka-people.s: The Tumbuka are a Bantu-speaking people of northern Malawi and neighbouring parts of Zambia and Tanzania. Living in small farming communities, they came under the loose authority of the Chikulamayembe dynasty in the late 18th century and in the mid-19th century were conquered…

treaty-of-adrianople-1829.s: The Treaty of Adrianople, signed on 14 September 1829 at Edirne, ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1828–29. The Ottoman Empire ceded to Russia the mouth of the Danube and much of the eastern Black Sea coast with Akhaltsikhe, and accepted Russian protection over Moldavia and…

tirich-mir.s: Tirich Mir is the highest mountain of the Hindu Kush, rising to 7,708 metres in Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. It dominates the Chitral valley and appears in local legend as the home of fairies.

treaty-of-dancing-rabbit-creek.s: The Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek was signed on 27 September 1830 in Noxubee County, Mississippi, the first removal treaty concluded under the Indian Removal Act. The Choctaw ceded about 11 million acres of their remaining homeland in exchange for land in Indian Territory.

tuskahoma-oklahoma.s: Tuskahoma is a small community in Pushmataha County, south-eastern Oklahoma, United States. From 1884 it was the seat of the Choctaw Nation's government, whose brick council house still stands there, and it remains the nation's historic capital and the site of its annual Labor…

tosa-province.s: Tosa Province was an old province of Japan on the southern, Pacific coast of Shikoku, corresponding to modern Kōchi Prefecture. Ruled by the Chōsokabe clan, who unified it by 1575, it passed after 1600 to Yamauchi Kazutoyo as the Tosa domain.

tralee.s: Tralee is the county town of County Kerry in south-west Ireland, near the head of Tralee Bay. It grew around a castle and a Dominican priory founded by the FitzGeralds in the 13th century and was a seat of the Earls of Desmond until their fall in the 1580s.

thirty-three-orientals.s: The Thirty-Three Orientals were a band of exiles from the Banda Oriental who, led by Juan Antonio Lavalleja, crossed from Buenos Aires province in April 1825 to rise against Brazilian rule. Their landing sparked a revolt across the province, and a congress at Florida declared…

tepich.s: Tepich is a village in Quintana Roo, Mexico, in the east of the Yucatán peninsula. In July 1847 the Maya leader Cecilio Chi attacked it after the execution of Manuel Antonio Ay in Valladolid, an event usually taken as the start of the Caste War of Yucatán.

tihosuco.s: Tihosuco is a town in Quintana Roo, Mexico, in the east of the Yucatán peninsula, which was a colonial parish centre on the frontier of Spanish settlement. Jacinto Pat, one of the leaders of the Caste War of Yucatán, was its Maya headman, and the town was largely abandoned…

tsilhqotin-war.s: The Tsilhqot'in War was a conflict in 1864 between the Tsilhqot'in people of the Chilcotin plateau and the colony of British Columbia. Tsilhqot'in warriors killed members of a road-building crew working for Alfred Waddington, who planned a route from Bute Inlet to the…

tackys-revolt.s: Tacky's Revolt was a rising of enslaved Africans in Jamaica in 1760, led by Tacky, a Coromantee man from the Gold Coast. Beginning in Saint Mary Parish at Easter, it spread to other parts of the island and took months to suppress, with the help of Maroons bound by treaty to…

toubou-people.s: The Toubou are a people of the central Sahara, living mainly in the Tibesti Mountains of northern Chad and in neighbouring parts of Niger and Libya. Speakers of Teda and Dazaga, two Saharan languages, they are traditionally camel and goat herders and oasis farmers, organised…

touro-synagogue.s: The Touro Synagogue in Newport, Rhode Island, is the oldest surviving synagogue building in the United States, dedicated in 1763. Designed by Peter Harrison for the Sephardic congregation Jeshuat Israel, it reflects the religious freedom of the Rhode Island colony.

trinidad-and-tobago-carnival.s: The Trinidad and Tobago Carnival is an annual festival held on the Monday and Tuesday before Ash Wednesday, centred on Port of Spain. It began with masquerade balls of French Creole planters in the late 18th century and was transformed after emancipation in 1838 by formerly…

thomas-jefferson.s: Thomas Jefferson was a Virginian planter, lawyer and statesman, the principal author of the Declaration of Independence in 1776 and the third President of the United States from 1801 to 1809. As president he made the Louisiana Purchase of 1803, doubling the size of the country.

tortuguero.s: Tortuguero is a Classic Maya archaeological site in Tabasco, Mexico, close to the western edge of the Maya lowlands. Its 7th-century rulers, notably Bahlam Ajaw, used the same Baakal emblem glyph as Palenque and waged wars against neighbouring centres, including the conquest…

taos-new-mexico.s: Taos is a town in northern New Mexico beside Taos Pueblo, a multi-storey adobe village inhabited for about a thousand years and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Under Spanish rule its annual trade fairs drew Comanche, Ute and other Plains peoples to exchange horses, captives and…

the-californias.s: The Californias is the name for the Spanish and Mexican territory on the Pacific coast of North America, divided into Baja (Lower) California and Alta (Upper) California. Settled through Jesuit and later Franciscan missions from 1697 and 1769, it formed one of the northern…

tanaro.s: The Tanaro is a river of Piedmont in north-western Italy, rising in the Ligurian Alps and flowing past Alba, Asti and Alessandria before joining the Po. About 276 km long, it is the main right-bank tributary of the upper Po.

torrazzo-of-cremona.s: The Torrazzo is the bell tower of Cremona Cathedral in Lombardy, about 112 metres tall and completed around 1309. One of the tallest medieval brick towers in Europe, it became the symbol of the commune.

treaty-of-tartu-russian-estonian.s: The Treaty of Tartu was signed on 2 February 1920 between the Republic of Estonia and Soviet Russia, ending the Estonian War of Independence. Russia recognised Estonia's independence in perpetuity and agreed a border that gave Estonia Ivangorod and Petseri.

treaty-of-tartu-finnish-russian.s: The Treaty of Tartu was signed on 14 October 1920 between Finland and Soviet Russia, confirming the border between the two states after Finnish independence. Finland gained the Arctic port of Petsamo but gave up its claims to East Karelia, which remained Soviet despite the…

thirteenth-amendment.n: Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution
thirteenth-amendment.s: The Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution abolished slavery and involuntary servitude, except as punishment for crime. Passed by Congress in January 1865 with Abraham Lincoln's support and ratified in December 1865, it freed the remaining enslaved people in…

thomas-hooker.s: Thomas Hooker was an English Puritan minister who emigrated to Massachusetts in 1633 and in 1636 led his congregation to found Hartford on the Connecticut River. A leader of the Connecticut Colony, he preached that authority rests on the free consent of the people, ideas…

tristan-de-luna-y-arellano.s: Tristán de Luna y Arellano was a Spanish conquistador who in 1559 led a large expedition from New Spain to found a colony on Pensacola Bay in present-day Florida. A hurricane soon destroyed most of his ships and supplies, and detachments sent inland in search of food reached…

titterstone-clee-hill.s: Titterstone Clee Hill is a hill in south Shropshire, England, rising to 533 metres. Its summit is enclosed by a large prehistoric hillfort, one of the many fortified hilltops in the land of the Cornovii.

the-wrekin.s: The Wrekin is an isolated hill in east Shropshire, England, rising to 407 metres above the Shropshire plain. Its summit carries a large Iron Age hillfort, thought to have been a chief centre of the Cornovii before the Roman conquest.

tabula-cortonensis.s: The Tabula Cortonensis is an inscribed Etruscan bronze tablet found near Cortona, Italy, and first published in 2000. Dating from around 200 BCE, it carries about 200 words, making it one of the longest Etruscan texts known, and appears to record a sale or lease of land,…

treaty-of-zboriv.s: The Treaty of Zboriv was concluded in August 1649 between the Polish king John II Casimir and the Cossack hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky, after a Polish army had been besieged at Zbarazh and the king's relief force was attacked at Zboriv. It recognised Cossack self-rule in the…

truce-of-andrusovo.s: The Truce of Andrusovo, agreed in January 1667 in a village near Smolensk, ended the Russo-Polish War of 1654–1667. The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth ceded Smolensk and left-bank Ukraine east of the Dnieper to the Tsardom of Russia, which also received Kyiv, nominally for two…

touraine.s: Touraine is a historic province of central France on the middle Loire, centred on the city of Tours. Contested in the 11th century between the counts of Blois and Anjou, it passed to Anjou in 1044 and formed part of the Angevin lands of the Plantagenets until Philip II of…

theobald-ii-count-of-champagne.s: Theobald II, called the Great, was count of Champagne from 1125 and, as Theobald IV, count of Blois and Chartres from 1102. A son of Stephen-Henry and Adela of Normandy and brother of Stephen, King of England, he reunited Blois and Champagne.

theobald-i-of-navarre.s: Theobald I was king of Navarre from 1234 and, as Theobald IV, count of Champagne from his birth in 1201. One of the most admired trouvères, or poets, of his age, he wrote love songs and crusade songs, and he led the Barons' Crusade of 1239–1240 to the Holy Land.

thoros-of-edessa.s: Thoros was the Armenian ruler of Edessa in the late 11th century, a former Byzantine official who held the city after Byzantine power in the region collapsed. In 1098 he invited Baldwin of Boulogne to help defend it and adopted him as son and heir.

thoros-i-prince-of-armenia.s: Thoros I was the Rubenid lord of Armenian Cilicia from about 1100 to 1129. He took castles of the Cilician plain, including Anazarbus, from the Byzantines and cooperated with the crusader states of Antioch and Edessa against the Seljuk Turks.

turbessel.s: Turbessel, today Tell Bashir near the Syrian–Turkish border, was a fortress west of the Euphrates and the second centre of the crusader County of Edessa. Joscelin of Courtenay held it before becoming count, and after Zengi took Edessa in 1144 Joscelin II ruled the remaining…

treaty-of-le-goulet.s: The Treaty of Le Goulet was signed in May 1200 between Philip II of France and John of England, on the Seine in Normandy. Philip recognised John as heir to the Angevin lands in France in return for the county of Évreux, parts of the Vexin and a large relief payment, and John…

thurgau.s: Thurgau is a region and canton of north-eastern Switzerland, lying between Lake Constance and the Thur, with its capital at Frauenfeld. Once a large Alemannic district, it was held largely by the counts of Kyburg and then the Habsburgs until the Swiss Confederates conquered it…

thun.s: Thun is a city in the Swiss canton of Bern, where the Aare leaves Lake Thun below the Bernese Oberland. Its castle keep was built by the dukes of Zähringen around 1200, and the town passed to the counts of Kyburg in 1218 and to Bern in 1384.

tettnang.s: Tettnang is a town in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, near the northern shore of Lake Constance, known for its hop growing. It was the residence of the Tettnang line of the counts of Montfort, who built its baroque New Palace in the 18th century.

tierra-de-campos.s: The Tierra de Campos is a flat, largely treeless region of the northern Meseta in Castile and León, Spain, spreading across the provinces of Palencia, Valladolid, León and Zamora. Resettled by Christian farmers in the 10th century as the frontier moved south, it became one of…

tonnerre.s: Tonnerre is a small town in the Yonne department of Burgundy, on the Armançon river. In the Middle Ages it was the seat of a county that passed by marriage to the counts of Nevers in the 11th century and was later held by the Chalon family.

treaty-of-turin-1860.s: The Treaty of Turin, signed on 24 March 1860, transferred Savoy and the County of Nice from the Kingdom of Sardinia to Napoleon III's France. It was the price for French help against Austria in 1859 and for French acceptance of Sardinia's annexation of the central Italian states.

tremp.s: Tremp is a town in the province of Lleida, Catalonia, capital of the Pallars Jussà district on the Noguera Pallaresa. In the Middle Ages it lay at the heart of the county of Pallars Jussà, in a basin of farmland ringed by castles.

treaty-of-bretigny.s: The Treaty of Brétigny was agreed on 8 May 1360 between Edward III of England and the captive John II of France, ending the first phase of the Hundred Years' War. Edward gave up his claim to the French crown in return for full sovereignty over an enlarged Aquitaine, Calais and…

teresa-countess-of-portugal.s: Teresa was a daughter of Alfonso VI of León and Castile who, with her husband Henry of Burgundy, held the County of Portugal from 1096. After Henry's death in 1112 she ruled alone, styling herself queen, and allied with the Galician Trava family.

tet.s: The Têt is a river of Roussillon in southern France, about 115 km long, rising in the eastern Pyrenees near the Carlit massif and flowing past Prades and Perpignan into the Mediterranean. Its fertile, irrigated plain was the economic heart of the medieval county of Roussillon.

texas.s: Texas is the second-largest state of the United States by area and population, in the south-central part of the country, bordering Mexico along the Rio Grande. A thinly settled province of New Spain from the late 17th century and part of Mexico after 1821, it broke away in…

traben-trarbach.s: Traben-Trarbach is a wine town on the Moselle in Rhineland-Palatinate, formed in 1904 by uniting Traben and Trarbach on opposite banks. Trarbach was the centre of the Rear County of Sponheim, overlooked by the Grevenburg castle, and later a leading Moselle wine-trading town,…

tortosa.s: Tortosa is a city on the lower Ebro in the province of Tarragona, Catalonia, near the river's delta. Under Muslim rule it was a port and shipbuilding centre and the seat of a taifa kingdom, until Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona conquered it in 1148 with Genoese help.

theophylacti.s: The Theophylacti were a Roman noble family that dominated the city and the papacy in the 10th century. Founded by Theophylact I, a senator and papal official, and his wife Theodora, the family included Marozia, her son Alberic II, prince of the Romans, and Pope John XII.

tyrol-castle.s: Tyrol Castle stands above Merano in South Tyrol, Italy, and was built in the early 12th century. As the seat of the counts of Tyrol it gave its name to the county and to the whole region.

treaty-of-boves.s: The Treaty of Boves of 1185 ended the war between Philip II of France and Philip of Alsace, Count of Flanders, over the inheritance of Vermandois. Philip of Alsace kept part of Vermandois for life, while the king gained the Amiénois and much of the county, a major advance for…

tauber.s: The Tauber is a river in southern Germany, about 130 km long, that rises in the Frankenhöhe hills and flows north past Rothenburg ob der Tauber, Bad Mergentheim and Tauberbischofsheim to join the Main at Wertheim. Its valley, known for vineyards, castles and well-preserved…

treaty-of-munsingen.s: The Treaty of Münsingen of 1482 reunited the County of Württemberg, which had been divided in 1442 between the Urach and Stuttgart lines. Agreed between Count Eberhard V the Bearded and his cousin Eberhard VI, it declared the county indivisible under the senior ruler, with…

tocco-family.s: The Tocco were an Italian noble family of the Kingdom of Naples who ruled Cephalonia, Zakynthos and Leucas from 1357 and, under Carlo I Tocco, also Epirus with Ioannina and Arta. Ottoman conquest stripped them of the mainland in the mid-15th century and of the islands in 1479,…

theriso-revolt.s: The Theriso revolt was an uprising in the Cretan State in 1905, led by Eleftherios Venizelos from the village of Theriso near Chania. The rebels demanded union with Greece and opposed the autocratic rule of the high commissioner, Prince George of Greece.

thanjavur.s: Thanjavur (Tanjore) is a city in the Kaveri delta of Tamil Nadu, India. It was the capital of the Chola Empire from the 9th century, when Rajaraja I built the great Brihadisvara Temple, and later of the Nayak and Maratha rulers of Thanjavur, who were notable patrons of music…

tharangambadi.s: Tharangambadi, formerly Tranquebar, is a coastal town in Tamil Nadu, India. The Danish East India Company obtained it in 1620 from the Nayak ruler of Thanjavur and built Fort Dansborg, making it the capital of Danish India until it was sold to Britain in 1845.

tranquebar-mission.s: The Tranquebar Mission was the first Protestant mission in India, founded in 1706 at the Danish colony of Tranquebar by the German Lutherans Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg and Heinrich Plütschau at the request of King Frederick IV of Denmark. It set up schools and a printing press…

tokat.s: Tokat is a city in northern Anatolia, Turkey, in the valley of the Yeşilırmak, near the site of ancient Comana Pontica. It was held by the Danishmendids, then by the Seljuks of Rum and Mongol governors, and was an important stage on the trade routes across Anatolia.

torstenson-war.s: The Torstenson War of 1643–1645 was a conflict between Sweden and Denmark-Norway within the Thirty Years' War, named after the Swedish general Lennart Torstensson, who invaded Jutland from Germany. Swedish forces also attacked Scania, and a Swedish-Dutch fleet destroyed much…

tama-people.s: The Tama are a people of eastern Chad and western Darfur in Sudan, living mainly in the hills around Guéréda. They speak Tama, one of the Taman languages of the Eastern Sudanic family, and are mostly farmers and herders.

tohoku-region.s: The Tōhoku region is the north-eastern part of Honshu, the main island of Japan, made up of the prefectures of Aomori, Iwate, Miyagi, Akita, Yamagata and Fukushima. Largely the old provinces of Mutsu and Dewa, it was long a frontier of the Japanese state and later the base of…

tavoliere-delle-puglie.s: The Tavoliere delle Puglie is a broad plain in northern Apulia around the city of Foggia, the second largest plain in Italy after the Po valley. In antiquity it was the land of the Daunians, and in later centuries it was used mainly as winter pasture for flocks driven down…

taizhou-jiangsu.s: Taizhou is a city in central Jiangsu province, China, on the north bank of the Yangtze. Its coastal plain was long a centre of salt production, and it was among the salt workers of the area that Zhang Shicheng, a salt boatman, began his revolt against the Yuan dynasty in 1353.

toghto.s: Toghto was a Mongol statesman of the Merkit clan who served as chancellor of the Yuan dynasty under Toghon Temür. He sponsored the official histories of the Liao, Jin and Song dynasties and in 1351 launched a huge project to restore the course of the Yellow River, whose forced…

tomislavgrad.s: Tomislavgrad is a town in western Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the Duvno plain. Near it lay Delminium, the stronghold of the Delmatae, and later a Roman town.

tbilisi-state-university.s: Tbilisi State University is the oldest university in Georgia and in the Caucasus, founded in Tbilisi in 1918 by a group of scholars led by the historian Ivane Javakhishvili, whose name it now bears. Established in the first year of the independent Democratic Republic of…

toroodbe.s: The Toroodbe were a class of Muslim clerics and scholars among the Fulbe of West Africa, originally in Futa Toro on the Senegal River. From the late 17th century they led a series of Islamic reform movements, founding states such as Bundu, the Imamate of Futa Toro in 1776 and,…

teda-people.s: The Teda are the northern branch of the Toubou peoples, living in and around the Tibesti mountains of northern Chad and southern Libya and in north-eastern Niger. They speak Tedaga and are traditionally camel herders, date growers and caravan traders.

taleh.s: Taleh (Taleex) is a town in the Sool region of northern Somalia, the main stronghold of the Dervish state of Mohammed Abdullah Hassan. From 1913 the Dervishes built there a complex of massive stone forts and towers.

thomas-preljubovic.s: Thomas Preljubović was a Serbian nobleman who ruled Ioannina in Epirus from about 1367 until 1384, first as governor for the Serbian ruler Symeon Uroš and then as despot. His harsh rule and constant wars with the Albanian clans made him hated by the townspeople, and Greek…

the-hill-of-devi.s: The Hill of Devi is a book by the English novelist E. M. Forster, published in 1953. It is built from his letters home from Dewas Senior, which he visited in 1912–1913 and where in 1921 he served as private secretary to Maharaja Tukoji Rao III.

tribhuwanaraja-mauli-warmadewa.s: Tribhuwanaraja Mauli Warmadewa was a king of Malayu, ruling from Dharmasraya in central Sumatra, in the late 13th century. He is known from the Padang Roco inscription of 1286, which records that King Kertanegara of Singhasari sent him a statue of Amoghapasa.

tylos.s: Tylos was the Greek name for Bahrain in the Hellenistic and Roman periods, first recorded by writers drawing on the voyages of Alexander the Great's officers. The island was known for its pearls and cotton and belonged to trade networks of the Seleucids and later of Characene…

trepca.s: Trepča is a mining area near Mitrovica in northern Kosovo, worked for lead, zinc and silver. In the Middle Ages its silver mines, operated with the help of Saxon miners and Ragusan merchants, were a major source of revenue for Serbian rulers.

trencin.s: Trenčín is a city in western Slovakia on the Váh river, overlooked by one of the largest castles in the country. Known in Hungarian as Trencsén, it was the stronghold of the magnate Matthew Csák, who ruled much of north-western Hungary from it in the early 14th century.

tamils.s: The Tamils are a people of South Asia whose language, Tamil, has a literary tradition of more than two thousand years. Most live in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu and in northern and eastern Sri Lanka, where a Tamil kingdom ruled Jaffna in the late Middle Ages, and a separate…

turov.s: Turov is a small town on the Pripyat River in Gomel region, southern Belarus, and one of the oldest towns in the country. First mentioned in the Primary Chronicle under the year 980, it was the seat of a principality of Kievan Rus' and of a bishopric whose most famous bishop…

theudebald-duke-of-alamannia.s: Theudebald was a duke of the Alemanni in the 730s and 740s, a son of Duke Gotfrid and brother of Lantfrid. He resisted the Carolingian mayors of the palace, driving Saint Pirmin out of Reichenau around 727 and repeatedly rising against Frankish rule.

treaty-of-bruges-1301.s: The Treaty of Bruges of 1301 ended a war between King Philip IV of France and Count Henry III of Bar, who had allied with England. Defeated and held prisoner, Henry was forced to do homage to the French crown for his lands west of the Meuse, which became known as the Barrois…

tassilo-iii-of-bavaria.s: Tassilo III of Bavaria was the last Agilolfing duke of Bavaria, ruling from 748 under Frankish overlordship. He founded monasteries such as Kremsmünster, subdued Carantania around 772 and acted almost as an independent king.

trausnitz-castle.s: Trausnitz Castle stands above the town of Landshut in Bavaria and was founded in 1204 by Duke Louis I of the Wittelsbach family. It was the residence of the dukes of Lower Bavaria and Bavaria-Landshut until 1503, when the Rich Dukes kept their treasure there, and was later…

treaty-of-kalisz-1343.s: The Treaty of Kalisz, concluded in July 1343, ended a long conflict between King Casimir III of Poland and the Teutonic Order. Poland gave up its claims to Pomerelia, the Chełmno Land and the Michałów Land, while the Order returned Kuyavia and the Dobrzyń Land, which it had…

the-glory-of-the-duchy-of-carniola.n: The Glory of the Duchy of Carniola
the-glory-of-the-duchy-of-carniola.s: The Glory of the Duchy of Carniola is an encyclopedic description of Carniola by Johann Weikhard von Valvasor, published in German at Nuremberg in 1689. Its four volumes, with over 500 engravings, cover the land's geography, history, customs and natural wonders, including the…

tomislav-of-croatia.s: Tomislav was the first ruler of Croatia to be styled king, around 925. Originally Duke of Dalmatian Croatia, he fought off Hungarian incursions and united his land with Pannonian Croatia, and he was addressed as king in a papal letter of 925.

trpimir-i.s: Trpimir I was Duke of Croatia from about 845 to 864 and founder of the Trpimirović dynasty. His charter of 852 is the earliest document in which a Croatian ruler calls himself duke of the Croats.

treaty-of-teusina.s: The Treaty of Teusina was signed on 18 May 1595 at Teusina, near Ivangorod, ending the Russo-Swedish War of 1590–1595. Russia recognised Swedish possession of Estonia, including Narva, while Sweden returned the fortress and district of Kexholm to Russia.

torquato-tasso.s: Torquato Tasso was an Italian poet who served at the court of Duke Alfonso II d'Este in Ferrara. His epic Jerusalem Delivered, completed in 1575, tells of the First Crusade and became one of the most widely read poems in Europe.

tempietto-longobardo.s: The Tempietto Longobardo is a small 8th-century chapel in Cividale del Friuli, Italy, part of the former convent of Santa Maria in Valle. Its stucco figures of female saints and its richly decorated arch are among the finest surviving works of early medieval art in Europe.

tuhutum.s: Tuhutum is a Hungarian chieftain named in the Gesta Hungarorum as the conqueror of Transylvania around 900, who defeated the Vlach duke Gelou. The chronicle makes him the ancestor of the gyulas who ruled Transylvania in the 10th century, and so of Sarolt, mother of King…

treaty-of-venlo.s: The Treaty of Venlo was concluded on 7 September 1543 between Emperor Charles V and Duke William of Jülich-Cleves-Berg. After a swift campaign by Charles, William renounced the Duchy of Guelders and the County of Zutphen and promised to keep his lands Catholic.

tbilisi.s: Tbilisi, known until 1936 as Tiflis, is the capital of Georgia, on the Kura river. Founded according to tradition by King Vakhtang I Gorgasali in the 5th century, it was ruled in turn by Persians, Arabs, Georgian kings, Mongols and Safavid Iran.

tum-collegiate-church.s: Tum Collegiate Church, in the village of Tum near Łęczyca in central Poland, is one of the largest surviving Romanesque churches in the country. Built of granite and sandstone, it was consecrated in 1161 on the site of an earlier Benedictine abbey, and it has two west towers…

treaty-of-vilnius-1561.s: The Treaty of Vilnius, or Pacta subiectionis, was concluded on 28 November 1561 between Sigismund II Augustus, king of Poland and grand duke of Lithuania, and the Livonian Order and the Archbishopric of Riga. Facing Russian invasion during the Livonian War, the order was…

truce-of-altmark.s: The Truce of Altmark was a six-year armistice signed on 26 September 1629 at Altmark (Stary Targ) near Malbork, ending the Polish–Swedish War of 1626–1629. Mediated by France, England and Brandenburg, it left Sweden most of Livonia and the right to levy tolls in the Prussian…

the-last-supper-leonardo.s: The Last Supper is a mural painted by Leonardo da Vinci between about 1495 and 1498 in the refectory of the convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, commissioned by Ludovico Sforza. It shows the moment Christ announces that one of the apostles will betray him.

treaty-of-cherasco.s: The Treaty of Cherasco, signed in 1631 at Cherasco in Piedmont, ended the War of the Mantuan Succession. It confirmed the French-backed Charles I Gonzaga-Nevers as Duke of Mantua and Montferrat, while Savoy received part of Montferrat, including Alba and Trino.

treaty-of-saint-clair-sur-epte.s: The Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte, traditionally dated to 911, was an agreement between the West Frankish king Charles the Simple and the Viking leader Rollo. Charles granted Rollo lands around Rouen near the mouth of the Seine in return for defending them against other…

thomas-ii-zaremba.s: Thomas II Zaremba (d. 1292) was Bishop of Wrocław from 1270. He fought a long dispute with Duke Henry IV Probus of Silesia over the rights and property of the Church, during which he was besieged in Racibórz and the duke was excommunicated.

treaty-of-tsarskoye-selo-1773.s: The Treaty of Tsarskoye Selo of 1773 settled the long dispute between Denmark and Russia over the Gottorp lands in Schleswig-Holstein. Grand Duke Paul of Russia, heir of the Holstein-Gottorp dukes, gave up his share of Holstein to Denmark in exchange for the counties of…

tarnowskie-gory.s: Tarnowskie Góry is a town in the Silesian Voivodeship of southern Poland, which grew up as a mining settlement after silver-bearing lead ore was found there at the end of the 15th century. Duke John II the Good of Opole granted it town rights in 1526 and a mining code in 1528,…

teatro-farnese.s: The Teatro Farnese is a wooden theatre inside the Palazzo della Pilotta in Parma, built in 1618 for Duke Ranuccio I Farnese to designs by Giovanni Battista Aleotti. Its permanent proscenium arch makes it one of the earliest theatres of its kind.

treaty-of-grimnitz.s: The Treaty of Grimnitz was concluded on 26 August 1529 at the Grimnitz hunting lodge between Elector Joachim I of Brandenburg and the dukes of Pomerania. Brandenburg gave up its claim to feudal overlordship over Pomerania, and in return the Griffin dukes recognised the…

treaty-of-kepno.s: The Treaty of Kępno was an agreement made on 15 February 1282 between Mestwin II, Duke of Pomerelia, and Przemysł II, Duke of Greater Poland. Mestwin, who had no sons, named Przemysł his heir, and on Mestwin's death in 1294 Pomerelia passed to Przemysł, who was crowned King of…

treaty-of-krakow.s: The Treaty of Kraków of 8 April 1525 ended the Polish–Teutonic War of 1519–1521. Albert of Brandenburg-Ansbach, Grand Master of the Teutonic Order, secularised the order's state in Prussia and turned it into the hereditary Lutheran Duchy of Prussia, a fief of the Polish crown.

treaty-of-wehlau.s: The Treaty of Wehlau was signed on 19 September 1657 between Poland-Lithuania and Frederick William, the Great Elector of Brandenburg, during the Second Northern War. In return for the elector abandoning his alliance with Sweden, King John II Casimir released the Duchy of…

teatro-allantica.s: The Teatro all'Antica is a theatre in Sabbioneta, in Lombardy, designed by Vincenzo Scamozzi for Duke Vespasiano Gonzaga and built in 1588–1590. Inspired by ancient theatres and by Palladio's Teatro Olimpico, it was one of the first free-standing buildings in modern Europe…

turin.s: Turin is a city in north-western Italy on the Po river and the capital of Piedmont. Founded as the Roman colony of Augusta Taurinorum, it became the capital of the dukes of Savoy in 1563 and later of the Kingdom of Sardinia.

therese-of-saxe-hildburghausen.s: Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen was a German princess who married Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria in Munich on 12 October 1810, and was Queen of Bavaria from 1825 to 1848. The horse race held for the wedding became the Oktoberfest, and the meadow where it took place was named…

trzebnica.s: Trzebnica is a town in Lower Silesia, Poland, north of Wrocław. In 1202 Duke Henry the Bearded and his wife Hedwig founded a Cistercian convent of nuns there.

transamund-ii-of-spoleto.s: Transamund II was Lombard Duke of Spoleto from 724 who acted almost as an independent ruler. He allied with Pope Gregory III and the Duke of Benevento against King Liutprand, who deposed him in 739; he regained the duchy in 740 but was finally overthrown in 742 and forced to…

trakai.s: Trakai is a town west of Vilnius in Lithuania, set among lakes. In the fourteenth century it was the seat of Grand Duke Kęstutis and his son Vytautas, when the Peninsula Castle and the Island Castle on Lake Galvė were built.

trakai-voivodeship.s: The Trakai Voivodeship was a province of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania created by the Union of Horodło in 1413 from the former Duchy of Trakai. It stretched from the area west of Vilnius to the south-western borderlands of Lithuania, with Trakai as its seat.

trento.s: Trento is a city on the Adige river in northern Italy and the capital of the province of Trentino. It began as the Roman town of Tridentum, became a Lombard duchy and from 1027 was ruled by prince-bishops within the Holy Roman Empire.

treaty-of-berlin-1742.s: The Treaty of Berlin was signed on 28 July 1742 between Prussia and Austria, confirming the preliminary Treaty of Breslau of June and ending the First Silesian War. Maria Theresa ceded most of Silesia and the County of Glatz to Frederick II of Prussia, keeping only Teschen,…

treaty-of-breslau.s: The Treaty of Breslau was the preliminary peace agreed on 11 June 1742 between Maria Theresa of Austria and Frederick II of Prussia, mediated by Britain, ending the First Silesian War. Austria ceded most of Silesia and the County of Glatz to Prussia.

the-book-of-the-courtier.s: The Book of the Courtier (Il Cortegiano) is a dialogue by the Italian diplomat Baldassare Castiglione, published in Venice in 1528. Set at the court of Duke Guidobaldo da Montefeltro in Urbino in 1507, it describes the ideal courtier and court lady, recommending grace,…

treaty-of-tubingen.s: The Treaty of Tübingen was an agreement of 8 July 1514 between Duke Ulrich of Württemberg and the estates of his duchy, made during the Poor Conrad revolt. The estates took over the duke's debts in return for the right to approve taxes and wars and guarantees of personal…

thaya.s: The Thaya (Czech Dyje) is a river in Austria and the Czech Republic, about 235 kilometres long. Rising in Lower Austria, it flows through southern Moravia past Znojmo and for long stretches forms the Austrian-Czech border.

table-bay.s: Table Bay is a natural bay on the Atlantic coast of South Africa, overlooked by Table Mountain, on whose shore Cape Town stands. Jan van Riebeeck landed there in 1652 to set up a supply station for Dutch East India Company ships, the start of European settlement in southern…

trekboers.s: The Trekboers were semi-nomadic, Dutch-speaking livestock farmers who moved beyond the settled districts of the Cape Colony in the 18th century. They took over grazing land from Khoikhoi and San communities and pushed the frontier east, where they came into conflict with the…

trincomalee.s: Trincomalee is a port city on the north-east coast of Sri Lanka with one of the largest natural deep-water harbours in the world. It is the site of the ancient Hindu Koneswaram temple.

tsonga-people.s: The Tsonga are a Bantu-speaking people of southern Mozambique and north-eastern South Africa, with smaller communities in Zimbabwe and Eswatini; their language is Xitsonga. Their chiefdoms around Delagoa Bay, among them the Tembe, traded ivory and other goods with Portuguese,…

tobago.s: Tobago is a Caribbean island north-east of Trinidad, with which it forms the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago. In the 17th and 18th centuries it was contested by the Dutch, Courlanders, English, French and Spanish and changed hands many times.

tritaea.s: Tritaea was an ancient Greek city in the inland hills of western Achaea in the Peloponnese, one of the twelve cities of the Achaean League. According to Polybius, it was one of the four cities, with Dyme, Patrae and Pharae, that revived the league in 280 BCE.

tablet-of-shamash.s: The Tablet of Shamash is a carved stone tablet found at Sippar in Iraq in 1881 and now in the British Museum. Made in the reign of Nabu-apla-iddina of Babylon in the 9th century BCE, it records how the king restored the cult image of the sun god Shamash after it had been lost.

tsewang-rabtan.s: Tsewang Rabtan was ruler of the Dzungar Khanate from 1697 until his death in 1727. A nephew of Galdan Boshugtu Khan, he restored Dzungar power after Galdan's defeat by the Qing, fought the Qing and Russia, and in 1717 sent an army that took Lhasa.

torf-einarr.s: Torf-Einarr was an Earl of Orkney around 900, a son of Rognvald Eysteinsson of Møre according to the Orkneyinga saga. He won the islands from Danish raiders, and the saga says he got his name from teaching the islanders to cut peat, or turf, for fuel.

theobald-walter.s: Theobald Walter was an Anglo-Norman lord who came to Ireland with Prince John in 1185 and was granted lands in Munster and the hereditary office of butler of Ireland. His brother Hubert Walter was Archbishop of Canterbury.

thomas-butler-10th-earl-of-ormond.s: Thomas Butler, 10th Earl of Ormond, known as Black Tom, was a powerful Irish nobleman raised at the English court and a cousin and favourite of Elizabeth I. He fought his rivals the FitzGeralds of Desmond and commanded the forces that crushed the second Desmond Rebellion.

tamil-nadu.s: Tamil Nadu is a state of south-eastern India, on the Coromandel Coast, with its capital at Chennai. It formed the core of ancient Tamilakam, ruled by the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas, and is known for its great Hindu temples and classical Tamil literature.

tiruchirappalli.s: Tiruchirappalli, also called Trichy and formerly Trichinopoly, is a city on the Kaveri River in Tamil Nadu, India. It includes the early Chola capital of Uraiyur and lies beside the temple island of Srirangam, and its Rock Fort temple stands on a hill in the centre.

tran-quoc-pagoda.s: The Tran Quoc Pagoda in Hanoi is regarded as the oldest Buddhist temple in the city. Tradition says it was founded in the 6th century under Ly Nam De as the Khai Quoc pagoda, on the bank of the Red River.

trieu-quang-phuc.s: Trieu Quang Phuc was a Vietnamese leader who continued Ly Bi's resistance to the Liang dynasty after 546, waging guerrilla war from the Da Trach marshes. After Chinese forces withdrew he ruled the Red River delta as Trieu Viet Vuong.

tamilakam.s: Tamilakam was the ancient Tamil country of southern India, covering roughly modern Tamil Nadu, Kerala and adjacent areas. In the Sangam age it was shared by the three crowned dynasties, the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas, together with many lesser chiefs.

tamil-brahmi.s: Tamil-Brahmi is a variant of the Brahmi script used to write the Tamil language from around the 3rd or 2nd century BCE. It is found in inscriptions in caves used by Jain monks in Tamil Nadu and Kerala and scratched on pottery, including finds in Sri Lanka and at Red Sea ports…

telugu-language.s: Telugu is a Dravidian language of south-eastern India, the main language of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and one of the most widely spoken languages of India. It is written in its own script, derived from Brahmi, and its earliest inscriptions date from the 6th century.

tao-yuanming.s: Tao Yuanming, also called Tao Qian, was a Chinese poet of the Eastern Jin and early Liu Song periods. After brief service as an official he retired around 405 to farm in his home district near Mount Lu, and his plain verse on rural life, wine and chrysanthemums made him the…

treaty-of-san-stefano.s: The Treaty of San Stefano was the preliminary peace signed on 3 March 1878 between Russia and the Ottoman Empire at the end of the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–1878. It recognised the independence of Serbia, Montenegro and Romania and created a large autonomous Bulgaria reaching…

treaty-of-meerssen.s: The Treaty of Meerssen was concluded in August 870 by the Carolingian kings Louis the German and Charles the Bald, who divided between them the Middle Frankish kingdom of Lotharingia after the death of their nephew Lothair II. Louis gained the eastern part, including Aachen,…

tanggu-truce.s: The Tanggu Truce was the ceasefire signed at Tanggu, near Tianjin, on 31 May 1933 between China and Japan after Japanese forces had pushed south of the Great Wall. It created a demilitarised zone in north-eastern Hebei and in effect accepted Japan's control of Manchuria and Rehe.

tongzhou-district.s: Tongzhou District is a district of Beijing, east of the city centre at the northern end of the Grand Canal, where grain shipped from the south was unloaded for the capital. From 1935 it was the seat of the Japanese-backed East Hebei Autonomous Government, and in July 1937 a…

tetum-language.s: Tetum is an Austronesian language of the island of Timor and, with Portuguese, one of the two official languages of Timor-Leste. Its widely spoken form, Tetun Dili, absorbed many Portuguese loanwords during centuries of colonial rule and served as a lingua franca across the…

triphylia.s: Triphylia was a region of the western Peloponnese between the rivers Alpheios and Neda, south of Elis, with towns such as Lepreon and Samikon. Long dominated by Elis, it was detached from Elean control by Sparta after their war of about 402–400 BCE and later joined the…

tsakhurs.s: The Tsakhurs are a people of the eastern Caucasus who speak Tsakhur, a Northeast Caucasian language of the Lezgic group. They live in the highlands of southern Dagestan in Russia and in the Qakh and Zaqatala districts of north-western Azerbaijan.

tabqa-dam.s: The Tabqa Dam, also called the Euphrates Dam, is an earth-fill dam on the Euphrates near the town of al-Thawra (Tabqa) in northern Syria, built with Soviet help between 1968 and 1973. It created Lake Assad and is the country's largest source of hydroelectric power and…

tagdemt.s: Tagdemt is a site near Tiaret in north-western Algeria, beside the remains of the medieval Rustamid capital Tahert. Emir Abdelkader made it his capital in the late 1830s, building a fortress, arsenal and mint there to give his state a base beyond the reach of French columns.

treaty-of-desmichels.s: The Treaty of Desmichels was signed in February 1834 between Emir Abdelkader and General Louis Alexis Desmichels, the French commander at Oran. It established peace in western Algeria and, in its Arabic version, recognised Abdelkader's authority over the interior and his…

treaty-of-tafna.s: The Treaty of Tafna was signed on 30 May 1837 near the Tafna river between Emir Abdelkader and General Thomas-Robert Bugeaud. France recognised Abdelkader's authority over most of western and central Algeria while keeping Oran, Algiers and their hinterlands, which freed French…

third-anglo-afghan-war.s: The Third Anglo-Afghan War was a brief conflict in May 1919, when Emir Amanullah Khan of Afghanistan sent troops across the frontier of British India. The British, using aircraft and superior numbers, checked the advance, but a war-weary Britain agreed to the Treaty of…

tutush-i.s: Tutush I was a Seljuk prince, brother of Sultan Malik-Shah I, who founded the Seljuk Sultanate of Syria. Sent to help Atsiz against the Fatimids, he had him killed in 1079 and took Damascus, later extending his rule over Aleppo and much of Syria.

tetouan.s: Tetouan is a city in northern Morocco, close to the Mediterranean coast below the Rif mountains. It was refounded at the end of the 15th century by Muslim refugees from Granada under Ali al-Mandri and later governed by his daughter-in-law Sayyida al-Hurra.

talal-ibn-rashid.s: Talal ibn Rashid was emir of Jabal Shammar from 1848 to 1868, the son of the dynasty's founder Abdullah ibn Rashid. He consolidated the emirate's hold over northern Najd, encouraged merchants and pilgrims to pass through Ha'il, and undertook building works in the town.

treaty-of-darin.s: The Treaty of Darin was signed on 26 December 1915 on the island of Tarut between Britain, represented by Percy Cox, and Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud. Britain recognised his rule over Najd and al-Hasa and placed his lands under its protection, in return for his promise not to deal…

tijikja.s: Tijikja is a town in central Mauritania, capital of the Tagant region, built around a palm oasis. Founded in the 17th century, it became a main centre of the Emirate of Tagant.

taga-castle.s: Taga Castle was a fortified government centre founded in 724 in present-day Tagajō, Miyagi Prefecture. It served as the seat of the governor of Mutsu Province and of the Chinjufu, the court's military command against the Emishi, until Isawa Castle took over in the early 9th…

theodore-ii-laskaris.s: Theodore II Laskaris was emperor of Nicaea from 1254 to 1258, the son of John III Doukas Vatatzes and grandson of Theodore I. A pupil of Nikephoros Blemmydes, he was a scholar and writer of theological and philosophical works.

theodore-i-laskaris.s: Theodore I Laskaris was the founder of the Empire of Nicaea, ruling from 1205 and as crowned emperor from 1208 until 1221. Son-in-law of the emperor Alexios III Angelos, he gathered Byzantine refugees in Bithynia after the Fourth Crusade took Constantinople in 1204.

temple-of-artemis.s: The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, the Artemision, was a great sanctuary of the goddess and one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world. The marble temple of the 6th century BCE, partly paid for by King Croesus of Lydia, was burned by Herostratus in 356 BCE and rebuilt on an…

tell-harmal.s: Tell Harmal is an archaeological site in Baghdad, Iraq, the remains of the ancient town of Shaduppum, an administrative centre of the kingdom of Eshnunna in the early second millennium BCE. Excavated by Iraqi archaeologists from 1945, it yielded the tablets of the Laws of…

tishpak.s: Tishpak was the city god of Eshnunna in the Diyala region of Mesopotamia, replacing the earlier god Ninazu in the later third millennium BCE. A warrior god associated with the snake-dragon mushhushshu, he was regarded as the true king of the city, and its rulers styled…

tarrafal-camp.s: The Tarrafal camp was a prison camp on the island of Santiago in Cape Verde, opened in 1936 by Portugal's Estado Novo for political prisoners. Harsh conditions and disease killed dozens of inmates, earning it the name camp of slow death.

trondur-i-gotu.s: Tróndur í Gøtu was a Faroese chieftain known from the Færeyinga saga, which describes him as a cunning pagan leader based at Gøta on Eysturoy. He opposed Sigmundur Brestisson, who around 999 brought Christianity to the islands for King Olaf Tryggvason, and accepted baptism…

tinganes.s: Tinganes is a small rocky peninsula in the harbour of Tórshavn, the capital of the Faroe Islands. From the Viking Age it was the meeting place of the Alting, the islands' assembly, and it is regarded as one of the oldest parliamentary meeting places in the world.

torshavn.s: Tórshavn is the capital and largest town of the Faroe Islands, on the east coast of the island of Streymoy. Its name means Thor's harbour.

the-hague.s: The Hague is a city in the western Netherlands and the seat of the Dutch government, parliament and monarchy, although Amsterdam is the constitutional capital. It grew around the Binnenhof, the castle begun by the counts of Holland in the 13th century, and from the 16th…

taunggyi.s: Taunggyi is the capital of Shan State in eastern Myanmar, set on the Shan Plateau at about 1,400 metres above sea level, near Inle Lake. Under British rule it was the seat of the superintendent and then commissioner of the Federated Shan States, and it grew into the main…

tampere.s: Tampere is a city in southern Finland on the Tammerkoski rapids between two large lakes. Founded in 1779, it used the water power of the rapids to become the country's leading industrial town, with textile mills such as Finlayson, and was a centre of the labour movement.

texas-revolution.s: The Texas Revolution was the rebellion of American settlers and some Tejanos in the Mexican province of Texas against the centralist government of Antonio López de Santa Anna. Fighting began in October 1835; Santa Anna won at the Alamo in March 1836, but Sam Houston defeated…

tarlac-city.s: Tarlac City is the capital of Tarlac province in central Luzon, Philippines. In 1899, as American forces advanced during the Philippine–American War, Emilio Aguinaldo made Tarlac the seat of the First Philippine Republic for several months before it fell in November 1899 and…

treaty-of-batum.s: The Treaty of Batum was signed on 4 June 1918 between the Ottoman Empire and the new republics of Armenia, Georgia and Azerbaijan after the collapse of the Transcaucasian Federation. It forced Armenia to cede large territories, leaving it a small landlocked state of about…

toghon-taishi.s: Toghon Taishi was a leader of the Oirats of western Mongolia in the early 15th century. Succeeding his father Bakhamu, he united the Oirat groups, defeated the eastern Mongols and in the 1430s became master of the steppe, ruling through a Chinggisid puppet khan, Toghtoa Bukha,…

tell-el-muqdam.s: Tell el-Muqdam is an archaeological site in the central Nile Delta of Egypt, the ancient town of Taremu, which the Greeks called Leontopolis. It was a centre of the cult of the lion god Mahes.

temimino.s: The Temiminó were a Tupi-speaking Indigenous people of the coast of south-eastern Brazil, around Guanabara Bay and Espírito Santo, enemies of the Tupinambá allied with the French. Under their leader Arariboia they allied with the Portuguese and helped Estácio de Sá and Mem de…

theuderic-ii.s: Theuderic II was the Merovingian king of Burgundy from 595 and of Austrasia from 612 until his death in 613, a son of Childebert II. Much of his reign was dominated by his grandmother Brunhild, and he fought his brother Theudebert II, whom he defeated and had killed in 612.

trave.s: The Trave is a river in Schleswig-Holstein, northern Germany, which flows past Bad Segeberg and Lübeck to the Baltic Sea at Travemünde. Lübeck was refounded in 1159 on a hill between the Trave and the Wakenitz, and the river gave the city the access to the sea that made it the…

treaty-of-riechenberg.s: The Treaty of Riechenberg was the settlement of 1552 by which the imperial city of Goslar submitted to Duke Henry the Younger of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel after years of conflict over the Rammelsberg. The city lost control of the mines and its forests to the duke, which began its…

treaty-of-chambord.s: The Treaty of Chambord was an alliance concluded in January 1552 between King Henry II of France and German Protestant princes led by Maurice of Saxony against Emperor Charles V. In return for French money, the princes allowed Henry to occupy the imperial cities of Metz, Toul…

the-sorrows-of-young-werther.s: The Sorrows of Young Werther is an epistolary novel by Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, published in 1774, about a young man's hopeless love for a woman engaged to another, ending in his suicide. It drew on Goethe's stay in Wetzlar in 1772, caused a sensation across Europe and is a…

tomas-herrera.s: Tomás Herrera was a Panamanian soldier and politician who fought in the wars of independence under Simón Bolívar. In 1840 he became head of the short-lived State of the Isthmus, which seceded from New Granada until 1841.

treaty-of-saigon-1862.s: The Treaty of Saigon, signed on 5 June 1862, ended the first phase of the French conquest of southern Vietnam. Emperor Tự Đức of the Nguyễn dynasty ceded the three eastern provinces of Biên Hòa, Gia Định and Định Tường, with Saigon and the islands of Poulo Condore, to France,…

tuileries-palace.s: The Tuileries Palace was a royal and imperial residence in Paris, begun in 1564 for Catherine de' Medici beside the Louvre. Louis XVI was brought there from Versailles in 1789, and its storming on 10 August 1792 brought down the monarchy.

timucua.s: The Timucua were a Native American people of northern Florida and south-eastern Georgia, divided into many chiefdoms that spoke dialects of the Timucua language. They met French Huguenots at Fort Caroline in 1564 and from the late 16th century were drawn into the Spanish…

treaty-of-hue-1883.s: The Treaty of Huế of 25 August 1883, known as the Harmand Treaty after the French negotiator Jules Harmand, was imposed on the Nguyễn court after French forces stormed the forts guarding Huế. It made Annam and Tonkin French protectorates, annexed Bình Thuận province to…

thanh-thai.s: Thành Thái was emperor of Vietnam of the Nguyễn dynasty from 1889 to 1907. He showed sympathy for reform and resentment of French control, and the French deposed him in 1907 on grounds of insanity, replacing him with his young son Duy Tân.

treaty-of-neuberg.s: The Treaty of Neuberg was an agreement of 9 September 1379, signed at Neuberg Abbey in Styria, by which the Habsburg brothers Albert III and Leopold III divided their lands. Albert kept the Duchy of Austria proper, founding the Albertine line, while Leopold received Styria,…

tolistobogii.s: The Tolistobogii were one of the three Celtic tribes of Galatia in central Anatolia, alongside the Tectosages and the Trocmi. They crossed into Asia Minor in 278 BCE and settled the western part of Galatia around Gordion and Pessinus.

trocmi.s: The Trocmi were one of the three Celtic tribes of Galatia in central Anatolia, with the Tolistobogii and the Tectosages. After crossing into Asia Minor in 278 BCE they settled the eastern part of Galatia, beyond the Halys river around Tavium.

tetricus-i.s: Tetricus I was the last emperor of the breakaway Gallic Empire, ruling from 271 to 274. A senator and governor of Aquitania, he was proclaimed after the murder of Victorinus.

trer-ceiri.s: Tre'r Ceiri is an Iron Age hillfort on the eastern summit of Yr Eifl on the Llŷn peninsula in north-west Wales. Its stone rampart encloses the remains of about 150 stone huts, many still standing to shoulder height.

treaty-of-nymphaeum-1261.s: The Treaty of Nymphaeum was concluded in March 1261 between the Nicaean emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos and the Republic of Genoa. Genoa promised naval help against the Latin Empire of Constantinople and Venice, and in return received tax-free trade, quarters in Byzantine…

tripartite-convention-1899.s: The Tripartite Convention of 1899 partitioned the Samoan Islands between Germany and the United States. Signed by Germany, Britain and the United States after the Second Samoan Civil War, it gave Germany the western islands of Upolu and Savaiʻi and the United States the…

theodor-leutwein.s: Theodor Leutwein was a German officer who led the colony of South West Africa from 1894, as governor from 1898 to 1905. He ruled largely through treaties with African leaders, playing them against each other, while settlers took land and cattle.

togoville.s: Togoville is a town on the northern shore of Lake Togo in southern Togo. On 5 July 1884 the German envoy Gustav Nachtigal signed a protection treaty there with the local chief Mlapa III, which founded the German colony of Togoland and gave the country its name.

thaj.s: Thaj is an archaeological site in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia, inland from the Gulf port of Jubail. It was a large walled city of the Hellenistic period, from about the 4th century BCE to the early centuries CE, and has yielded inscriptions, coins and a rich girl's…

thracian-tomb-of-sveshtari.s: The Thracian Tomb of Sveshtari is a royal tomb of the early 3rd century BCE near the village of Sveshtari in north-eastern Bulgaria. Its burial chamber has ten female figures carved in high relief, half human and half plant, supporting the roof, and a painted scene of a…

thracians.s: The Thracians were an ancient Indo-European people of south-eastern Europe, living in the lands of modern Bulgaria, northern Greece, European Turkey and parts of Romania. Divided into many tribes, among them the Odrysians, Getae and Bessi, they traded with the Greek colonies…

tiruvannamalai.s: Tiruvannamalai is a temple town in northern Tamil Nadu, India, at the foot of the sacred hill of Arunachala. Its Annamalaiyar temple, dedicated to Shiva as the element of fire, is one of the largest in India and was enlarged by the Cholas, Hoysalas, Vijayanagara and Nayaka…

trunajaya.s: Trunajaya was a Madurese prince who led a great rebellion against the Mataram Sultanate of Java from 1674. Allied with Makassarese fighters, he took and sacked the Mataram court at Plered in 1677, and Amangkurat I died while fleeing.

taedong-river.s: The Taedong is a river of North Korea that flows about 450 kilometres south-west from the northern mountains through Pyongyang to the Yellow Sea at Nampo. Its basin was the heartland of late Gojoseon, of the Chinese commandery of Lelang and later of Goguryeo, whose capital…

tripitaka-koreana.s: The Tripitaka Koreana is a complete Buddhist canon carved on 81,258 wooden printing blocks by the Goryeo court between 1236 and 1251, in the hope of divine protection against the Mongol invasions. It replaced an earlier set burned by the Mongols in 1232.

tumaparisi-kallonna.s: Tumapa'risi' Kallonna was king of Gowa in South Sulawesi in the first half of the sixteenth century. According to the Makassarese chronicles he joined Gowa with neighbouring Tallo in a twin kingdom and conquered or subdued many nearby polities, beginning the rise that made…

treaty-of-fredrikshamn.s: The Treaty of Fredrikshamn was signed on 17 September 1809 at Fredrikshamn (Hamina) between Sweden and Russia, ending the Finnish War. Sweden ceded all of Finland, together with the Åland Islands and the part of Lapland east of the Torne river, to Russia, which made them the…

turku.s: Turku, Swedish Åbo, is a city on the south-west coast of Finland at the mouth of the Aura river. Founded in the thirteenth century around its cathedral and castle, it was the chief city of Finland under Swedish rule and the seat of its university from 1640.

tomas-regalado.s: Tomás Regalado was a Salvadoran general who seized power in November 1898 and was president of El Salvador until 1903. His coup withdrew El Salvador from the Greater Republic of Central America, which then dissolved.

treaty-of-fort-laramie-1868.s: The Treaty of Fort Laramie of 1868 was an agreement between the United States and bands of the Lakota, Yanktonai Dakota and Arapaho that ended Red Cloud's War. It set aside the Great Sioux Reservation, including the Black Hills, for the Lakota and closed the army forts on the…

telemark.s: Telemark is a traditional region and county of southern Norway, stretching from the Skagerrak coast to the mountain plateaus of the interior. Its inland districts were known for iron, whetstones, stave churches and rich folk traditions, and the region gave its name to telemark…

trun.s: Trun, in German Truns, is a village in the Surselva region of Graubünden, Switzerland. According to tradition, in 1424 the Grey League was renewed there under a maple tree by the abbot of Disentis, local lords and the communes.

tholing-monastery.s: Tholing Monastery is a Buddhist monastery in Zanda County in the west of the Tibet Autonomous Region, founded in 996 by Yeshe-Ö, king of Guge, with the translator Rinchen Zangpo. It was the leading religious centre of the kingdom of Guge and a base of the later diffusion of…

tsaparang.s: Tsaparang is the ruined capital of the kingdom of Guge, built on a ridge above the Sutlej valley in Zanda County, western Tibet. Its palaces, temples and cave dwellings rise up an eroded hillside, and its temples hold fine murals of the 15th and 16th centuries.

tirigan.s: Tirigan was the last Gutian king listed in the Sumerian King List, said to have reigned for only forty days. Around 2119 BCE Utu-hengal of Uruk defeated his army; Tirigan fled to the town of Dubrum, where he was seized and handed over, ending Gutian rule in southern Mesopotamia.

tore-hund.s: Tore Hund was a powerful chieftain of Bjarkøy in Hålogaland, northern Norway, in the early 11th century, who traded with the Bjarmians of the White Sea. An opponent of King Olaf II, he fought in the peasant army that defeated and killed Olaf at the Battle of Stiklestad in…

treaty-of-stralsund-1370.s: The Treaty of Stralsund was the peace signed in 1370 between the Hanseatic League and the Kingdom of Denmark, ending the war that the Danish king Valdemar IV had provoked by seizing Visby in 1361. Denmark confirmed the League's trading privileges and handed over fortresses on…

tabinshwehti.s: Tabinshwehti was king of the First Toungoo Empire of Burma from 1530 to 1550. Starting from the small kingdom of Toungoo, he conquered the Mon kingdom of Hanthawaddy, taking Pegu in 1539 and Martaban in 1541, and Prome in 1542, with the help of Portuguese mercenaries and…

talal-of-jordan.s: Talal of Jordan (Talal bin Abdullah) was King of Jordan from July 1951, after the assassination of his father Abdullah I, until August 1952. During his short reign he approved the constitution of 1952, which made the government responsible to parliament.

tayfur-sokmen.s: Tayfur Sökmen was a Turkish politician who served as head of state of the Hatay State, the short-lived republic formed from the Sanjak of Alexandretta, from 1938 until its annexation by Turkey in 1939. He had long campaigned for the region's union with Turkey and later sat as…

tongwan.s: Tongwan was the capital of the Xia state of the Sixteen Kingdoms, built by Helian Bobo between 413 and 418 in the Ordos region, in today's Jingbian County in northern Shaanxi. Its walls of rammed earth mixed with lime were famous for their hardness.

thessaloniki.s: Thessaloniki is the second-largest city of Greece and the main port of Macedonia, at the head of the Thermaic Gulf. Founded around 315 BCE by Cassander, it was a leading city of the Roman and Byzantine empires and, under Ottoman rule from 1430, home to a large Sephardic Jewish…

tokharistan.s: Tokharistan was the medieval name for former Bactria, the lands on both sides of the upper Amu Darya in northern Afghanistan and southern Uzbekistan and Tajikistan. It was ruled by the Hephthalites and then, from the 7th century, by Turkic yabghus under Western Turkic…

tables-of-heraclea.s: The Tables of Heraclea are bronze tablets found in 1732 near Heraclea in Lucania, southern Italy. One side carries Greek texts of the 4th century BCE recording surveys of the sacred lands of Dionysus and Athena Polias; the other carries a Latin law of the 1st century BCE on…

teaching-for-merikare.s: The Teaching for Merikare is an ancient Egyptian wisdom text in which a king of the Herakleopolitan dynasty instructs his son Merikare on kingship, justice and the defence of the Delta frontier. Set in the First Intermediate Period, it survives in copies of the New Kingdom and…

thermae-himeraeae.s: Thermae Himeraeae, modern Termini Imerese, was a town on the north coast of Sicily, east of Palermo, founded by the Carthaginians in 407 BCE near hot springs, with survivors of Himera, which they had destroyed two years earlier. It later became a Roman town and was the…

trilochanapala-shahi-dynasty.s: Trilochanapala was a king of the Hindu Shahi dynasty from about 1010, son of Anandapala. After Mahmud of Ghazni took his stronghold of Nandana in the Salt Range around 1014, he fought on with help from Kashmir and later in the eastern Punjab, until he was killed in 1021.

tsugaru-tamenobu.s: Tsugaru Tamenobu, born Ōura Tamenobu, was a Japanese warlord who seized the Tsugaru region of northern Honshu from his overlords, the Nanbu, in the 1570s and 1580s. Recognised by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1590, he took the name Tsugaru and sided with Tokugawa Ieyasu at Sekigahara.

tsugaru-nobuhira.s: Tsugaru Nobuhira was the second lord of the Hirosaki domain in northern Honshu, the son of Tsugaru Tamenobu. He completed Hirosaki Castle in 1611 and laid out the castle town around it.

tiefu.s: The Tiefu were a people of the Ordos region of northern China in the 4th and 5th centuries, of mixed Xiongnu and Xianbei descent; the name was used for offspring of Xiongnu fathers and Xianbei mothers. Their chiefs of the Liu family led them against the Tuoba Xianbei, and Liu…

tajura.s: Tajura is a coastal town in Libya, just east of Tripoli. In the mid-16th century it served as a base for the Ottoman corsair Turgut Reis and other opponents of the Knights Hospitaller, who then held Tripoli.

tunanmarca.s: Tunanmarca was a walled hilltop town of the Xauxa people above the Yanamarca valley, near the Mantaro valley in central Peru. Built in the 14th century, during a period of endemic warfare before the Inca conquest, it held thousands of circular stone houses grouped in compounds.

tamaulipas.s: Tamaulipas is a state of north-eastern Mexico on the Gulf of Mexico, bordering Texas along the Rio Grande, with Ciudad Victoria as its capital. Colonised from 1748 as the Spanish province of Nuevo Santander, it became a state of independent Mexico in 1824.

tibor-szamuely.s: Tibor Szamuely was a Hungarian communist leader of the Hungarian Soviet Republic of 1919, in which he served as a deputy people's commissar for military affairs. He organised the repression of counter-revolutionary uprisings and was associated with the terror squad known as…

tisza-party.s: The Tisza Party, named after Hungary's second river and formally the Respect and Freedom Party, is a Hungarian centre-right political party. Founded in 2020, it was taken over in 2024 by Péter Magyar, a former Fidesz insider, and rapidly became the main opposition to Viktor…

treaty-of-margus.s: The Treaty of Margus was an agreement made, traditionally in 435, between the Eastern Roman Empire and the Hun kings Bleda and Attila at Margus on the Danube, in modern Serbia. Rome doubled its annual tribute to 700 pounds of gold, opened markets to the Huns and agreed to…

tisza.s: The Tisza is one of the main rivers of central Europe, rising in the Carpathians of western Ukraine and flowing for about 960 kilometres through Hungary to join the Danube in Serbia. Its broad plain was home to the Iazyges, Gepids and Avars and was settled by the Hungarians in…

tawergha.s: Tawergha is a town in north-western Libya, south of Misrata, on the route along the coast of the Gulf of Sirte. In 761 an Abbasid army defeated and killed the Ibadi imam Abu al-Khattab nearby.

treaty-of-lisbon-1668.s: The Treaty of Lisbon was signed on 13 February 1668 between Portugal and Spain with English mediation. By it Spain recognised the independence of Portugal and the rule of the House of Braganza, ending the Portuguese Restoration War that had begun in 1640.

thingvellir.s: Þingvellir is a site in south-western Iceland where the Althing, the island's general assembly, met in the open air from around 930 until 1798. It lies in a rift valley marking the boundary between the North American and Eurasian plates.

thetford.s: Thetford is a market town in Norfolk, England, on the Little Ouse river. An important centre of the Iceni in the Iron Age, it later became a major Anglo-Saxon town and, briefly, the seat of the bishop of East Anglia.

tatar-assr.s: The Tatar Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic was an autonomous republic within the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic, created in May 1920 with Kazan as its capital. It replaced earlier plans for a larger Tatar-Bashkir state and covered only part of the Volga Tatar…

tihama.s: Tihamah is the hot coastal plain along the Red Sea in western Arabia, stretching from the Gulf of Aqaba to the Bab el-Mandeb strait. Its southern part, in Saudi Arabia and Yemen, holds ports such as Jizan and Hodeidah and was farmed and traded across the sea for centuries.

treaty-of-wad-ras.s: The Treaty of Wad Ras was signed at Tetouan on 26 April 1860, ending the Hispano-Moroccan War. Morocco agreed to enlarge the territory of Ceuta, pay Spain a large indemnity and cede a territory on the Atlantic coast at Santa Cruz de Mar Pequeña, later identified with Ifni.

tamaroa.s: The Tamaroa were a people of the Illinois Confederation who lived on the Mississippi near the mouth of the Illinois river in the late 17th century. From 1699 French priests ran a mission among them and their Cahokia neighbours.

treaty-of-schonbrunn.s: The Treaty of Schönbrunn was signed at Schönbrunn Palace in Vienna on 14 October 1809, ending the War of the Fifth Coalition between France and Austria. Austria ceded Salzburg to Bavaria, West Galicia to the Duchy of Warsaw, and Carniola, Trieste and other lands to France,…

trieste.s: Trieste is a port city at the head of the Adriatic in north-eastern Italy. Under Habsburg rule from 1382, it was made a free port in 1719 and grew into the main seaport of the Austrian Empire.

takeda-clan.s: The Takeda were a Japanese samurai clan descended from the Minamoto that ruled Kai Province from the 12th century. Under Takeda Shingen in the 16th century they became one of the strongest Sengoku daimyo, conquering Shinano and parts of Suruga and Tōtōmi and fighting Uesugi…

tokaido.s: The Tōkaidō was the main road of Japan linking Edo with Kyoto along the Pacific coast, about 500 kilometres long. The name, meaning eastern sea route, also described the coastal provinces it crossed.

totomi-province.s: Tōtōmi Province was an old province of Japan in the western part of present-day Shizuoka Prefecture, around Lake Hamana. Long ruled by the Imagawa clan, it was contested after 1560 between Takeda Shingen and Tokugawa Ieyasu, who took most of it and moved his base to Hamamatsu…

timbo.s: Timbo is a town in the Futa Jallon highlands of central Guinea. In the 18th century it became the capital of the Imamate of Futa Jallon, the seat of the almamy, the elected Muslim ruler, and a centre of Islamic learning.

tanuf.s: Tanuf is a village in the interior of Oman, at the foot of the Jebel Akhdar near Nizwa. In 1913 Ibadi scholars and tribal leaders elected Salim ibn Rashid al-Kharusi as imam there, reviving the Imamate of Oman.

titlis.s: Titlis is a mountain of the Uri Alps in central Switzerland, rising to 3,238 metres on the border of the cantons of Obwalden and Bern. It overlooks the valley and abbey of Engelberg, founded below it in 1120.

theophanu-abbess-of-essen.s: Theophanu was abbess of Essen from 1039 until her death in 1058. A granddaughter of Emperor Otto II through his daughter Matilda and Ezzo, Count Palatine of Lotharingia, she enlarged the abbey church with a new westwork and crypt and enriched its treasury, notably with the…

thur.s: The Thur is a river of north-eastern Switzerland, about 135 kilometres long and a left tributary of the Rhine. It rises in the upper Toggenburg below the Säntis massif and flows through the cantons of St. Gallen and Thurgau, to which it gives its name, before joining the Rhine…

thorn-netherlands.s: Thorn is a small town in the province of Limburg in the south-eastern Netherlands, near the Meuse. From about 990 until 1794 it was ruled by the princess-abbesses of Thorn Abbey, a foundation for noble ladies, as a tiny imperial territory.

torun.s: Toruń is a city on the Vistula in northern Poland. Founded by the Teutonic Order in 1233 under the German name Thorn, it became a prosperous Hanseatic town.

treaties-of-rome-1941.s: The Treaties of Rome were agreements signed on 18 May 1941 between Fascist Italy and the newly created Independent State of Croatia. Croatia ceded much of Dalmatia, including Split and most Adriatic islands, to Italy, agreed to limits on its forces along the Adriatic and…

thomas-the-apostle.s: Thomas the Apostle was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus, remembered in the Gospel of John for doubting the resurrection until he saw Jesus. Tradition holds that he preached in Parthia and India and was martyred near Chennai, and the Saint Thomas Christians of Kerala trace…

takht-i-bahi.s: Takht-i-Bahi is a Buddhist monastic complex on a hilltop near Mardan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, founded in the 1st century CE and used until about the 7th century. Its courts, stupas and meditation cells are among the best preserved in ancient Gandhara.

thomasites.s: The Thomasites were American teachers sent to the Philippines in the early years of United States rule, named after the transport ship USAT Thomas, which brought over five hundred of them in 1901. They set up a public school system teaching in English and trained Filipino…

tydings-mcduffie-act.s: The Tydings–McDuffie Act, or Philippine Independence Act, was a United States law of 1934 providing for Philippine independence after a ten-year transition. It created the Commonwealth of the Philippines, with its own constitution and elected president, in 1935, while the…

taoiseach.s: The Taoiseach is the head of government of Ireland, nominated by Dáil Éireann and appointed by the President. The office was created by the Constitution of 1937, replacing the President of the Executive Council of the Irish Free State, and Éamon de Valera was the first to hold…

tadodaho.s: Tadodaho, in Haudenosaunee tradition, was a fearsome Onondaga chief, said to have snakes in his hair, who was the last to accept the Great Law of Peace of the Great Peacemaker and Hiawatha. His acceptance completed the Iroquois Confederacy.

treaty-of-hudaybiyyah.s: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was a truce agreed in March 628 at al-Hudaybiyyah, near Mecca, between Muhammad and the Quraysh of Mecca. It established a ten-year truce and allowed the Muslims to make the pilgrimage the following year.

treaty-of-wuchale.s: The Treaty of Wuchale was signed on 2 May 1889 between Menelik II of Ethiopia and Italy. It recognised Italian control of the Eritrean highlands, but its Italian and Amharic texts differed over Article 17, which Italy read as making Ethiopia an Italian protectorate.

treaty-of-san-francisco.s: The Treaty of San Francisco was signed on 8 September 1951 by Japan and 48 Allied nations, formally ending the state of war of the Second World War. It took effect on 28 April 1952, ending the Allied occupation and restoring Japan's sovereignty, and Japan gave up its claims to…

trelawny-town.s: Trelawny Town was the principal town of the Leeward Maroons in the Cockpit Country of western Jamaica, renamed after Governor Edward Trelawny, who signed the peace treaty of 1739 with Cudjoe. After the Second Maroon War of 1795 to 1796 its people were deported to Nova Scotia,…

tomoyuki-yamashita.s: Tomoyuki Yamashita was a Japanese general who commanded the Twenty-Fifth Army in the conquest of Malaya and Singapore in 1941 and 1942, earning the nickname the Tiger of Malaya. He later defended the Philippines in 1944 and 1945.

tayy.s: The Tayy are a large Arab tribe originating in the mountains of Aja and Salma in northern Arabia. They moved into Syria and Iraq in early Islamic times, and the poet Hatim al-Tai was one of them.

treaty-of-ganghwa.s: The Treaty of Ganghwa was signed between Japan and Joseon Korea in February 1876, after a Japanese naval clash near Ganghwa Island in 1875. Modelled on the unequal treaties imposed on Japan, it opened Busan and later two other ports to Japanese trade, gave Japanese residents…

tharros.s: Tharros is an ancient city on the Sinis peninsula of western Sardinia, founded by the Phoenicians around the 8th century BCE and later held by Carthage and Rome. It was the first capital of the Judicate of Arborea, but was abandoned around 1070 for Oristano.

talagunda-inscription.s: The Talagunda inscription is a Sanskrit verse inscription on a stone pillar at Talagunda in Shimoga district, Karnataka, India, carved in the 5th century under the Kadamba king Shantivarma. It tells how Mayurasharma, a Brahmin insulted by a Pallava guard at Kanchipuram, took…

tambdi-surla-mahadeva-temple.s: The Tambdi Surla Mahadeva Temple is a small Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva in the forested east of Goa, India. Built of basalt in the 12th or 13th century, in the period of the Kadamba dynasty of Goa, it is the best-preserved temple of that era in the region.

tell-nebi-mend.s: Tell Nebi Mend is an archaeological mound on the Orontes river south-west of Homs in western Syria, identified with the Bronze Age city of Kadesh. Kadesh controlled the route through the Homs gap and was fought over by Egypt and the Hittites, most famously in the Battle of…

togashi-masachika.s: Togashi Masachika was the military governor of Kaga province in Japan. He won control of the province with the help of True Pure Land believers but then turned against them.

tirukkural.s: The Tirukkural is a classic Tamil work of 1,330 couplets on ethics, attributed to the poet Thiruvalluvar. Divided into three books on virtue, wealth and love, it gives practical guidance on personal conduct, kingship and household life.

tailapa-iii.s: Taila III was a king of the Western Chalukya Empire in the Deccan, reigning from 1151. His reign saw the empire break apart: the Kakatiya chief Prola II defeated him, and his Kalachuri commander Bijjala II seized the capital Kalyani around 1156 and later proclaimed himself…

torghut.s: The Torghut are an Oirat Mongol tribe. In the early 17th century, under Kho Orluk, many of them migrated from Dzungaria across the Kazakh steppe to the lower Volga, where they founded the Kalmyk Khanate.

tezpur.s: Tezpur is a town on the north bank of the Brahmaputra in Assam, India. Nearby lay Haruppeshvara, the capital of the Mlechchha dynasty of Kamarupa, and the area holds early remains such as the carved stone doorframe of Da Parbatia.

taraz.s: Taraz is a city in southern Kazakhstan on the Talas River, one of the oldest towns of Central Asia. Known in the Middle Ages as Talas, it was a trading town of the Silk Road, a seat of Turkic rulers such as the Turgesh and later the Kara-Khanids, and lay near the site of the…

treaty-of-kurekchay.s: The Treaty of Kurekchay was signed on 14 May 1805 between Ibrahim Khalil Khan of the Karabakh Khanate and the Russian commander Pavel Tsitsianov. The khan accepted Russian suzerainty, with his family keeping internal rule in return for tribute and a Russian garrison.

turtkul.s: Turtkul is a town on the right bank of the Amu Darya in Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan. Founded as the Russian fort of Petro-Aleksandrovsk after the conquest of Khiva in 1873, it was the capital of the Karakalpak autonomous region until 1939, when erosion by the river and the…

thrace.s: Thrace is a historical region of south-eastern Europe, bounded by the Balkan Mountains, the Black Sea, the Aegean and the Sea of Marmara, and now divided between Bulgaria, Greece and European Turkey. It was home to the Thracian peoples and the Odrysian kingdom before becoming…

treaty-of-noteborg.s: The Treaty of Nöteborg was a peace concluded in 1323 at the fortress of Nöteborg (Orekhovets) at the source of the Neva between Sweden and the Novgorod Republic. It drew the first agreed border across Karelia, leaving the western part with Sweden and the east with Novgorod.

tirhut.s: Tirhut is a historical region of northern Bihar in India, between the Ganges and the Himalayan foothills, largely corresponding to Mithila. It was ruled by the Karnat dynasty from the late 11th century and then by the Oiniwar dynasty under the Delhi Sultanate.
