tajiks.s: The Tajiks are a Persian-speaking people of Central Asia, living mainly in Tajikistan, Afghanistan and Uzbekistan. They descend largely from the Iranian population of Bactria and Sogdiana, and cities such as Bukhara and Samarkand were centres of their culture.

tarim-yemen.s: Tarim is a town in the Wadi Hadramawt in eastern Yemen, long the religious centre of the valley. It is the seat of Ba 'Alawi sayyid families and of Shafi'i Sufi scholarship, with many mosques and the Dar al-Mustafa school.

turkistan-city.s: Turkistan is a city in southern Kazakhstan, near the Syr Darya, known in the Middle Ages as Yasi. It grew around the shrine of the Sufi Ahmad Yasawi, whose mausoleum was built by Timur.

tengiz-field.s: The Tengiz Field is a giant oil field near the north-eastern shore of the Caspian Sea in western Kazakhstan, discovered in 1979. Since 1993 it has been developed by Tengizchevroil, a joint venture led by Chevron, and it is the largest source of Kazakhstan's oil output.

tarki.s: Tarki is a historic Kumyk settlement on the Caspian coast of Dagestan, now a district of the city of Makhachkala. From the 17th century until 1867 it was the seat of the shamkhals of Tarki, who controlled the coastal plain on the route between Russia and Persia.

tamanrasset.s: Tamanrasset is the main town of the Ahaggar region in southern Algeria, in the central Sahara. It grew from a Tuareg settlement and a French military post of the early 20th century, where Charles de Foucauld lived from 1905.

tassili-najjer.s: Tassili n'Ajjer is a sandstone plateau in south-eastern Algeria, near the Libyan border, in the central Sahara. It is famous for thousands of prehistoric rock paintings and engravings showing wild animals, herds and people from a time when the Sahara was green.

timia.s: Timia is an oasis village in the central Aïr Mountains of Niger. It is a centre of the Kel Ewey Tuareg, known for its gardens of fruit trees watered from wells and for the ruins of a French fort above the valley.

tahoua.s: Tahoua is a town in south-western Niger, capital of the Tahoua Region. It lies in the Ader, on the frontier between the Hausa farming lands and the pastures of Tuareg confederations such as the Iwellemmeden Kel Dinnik and the Kel Gres.

tai-khun-people.s: The Tai Khün are a Tai people centred on Kengtung in the eastern Shan State of Myanmar, with smaller communities in northern Thailand and Yunnan. Their language, script and Theravada Buddhist traditions are closely related to those of Lan Na.

theog.s: Theog is a town in Shimla district of Himachal Pradesh, India, in the hills north-east of Shimla. It was the seat of a small hill chiefship that was a feudatory of Keonthal under British rule, and it joined Himachal Pradesh in 1948.

tuul-river.s: The Tuul is a river of central Mongolia that rises in the Khentii Mountains and flows west through Ulaanbaatar to join the Orkhon. Its valley was the homeland of the Keraites in the 12th century, and later of the Tüsheet Khans.

tayichiud.s: The Tayichiud were a Mongol clan closely related to the Borjigin and part of the Khamag Mongol confederation of the 12th century. After the death of Yesügei they abandoned his widow and children and later held the young Temüjin, the future Genghis Khan, captive until he escaped.

tatarstan.s: Tatarstan is a republic of the Russian Federation on the middle Volga and lower Kama, with its capital at Kazan. Its territory was the core of Volga Bulgaria and later of the Khanate of Kazan, conquered by Russia in 1552.

tsogt-taij.s: Tsogt Taij, known in other sources as Choghtu Khong Tayiji, was a Khalkha Mongol prince and poet who supported the Karma Kagyu school against the Gelug in the religious wars of Tibet. He moved to the Kokonor region in the 1630s but was defeated and killed in 1637 by Güshi Khan…

tecun-uman.s: Tecun Uman was a K'iche' Maya leader who, according to tradition, was killed fighting the Spanish under Pedro de Alvarado near Quetzaltenango in 1524, in single combat with Alvarado himself. Spanish letters do not name him, and his story comes from later K'iche' documents.

tokugawa-iemochi.s: Tokugawa Iemochi was the fourteenth Tokugawa shogun, from 1858 until his death. Born Tokugawa Yoshitomi, lord of the Kii domain, he was chosen as shogun with the backing of Ii Naosuke over Tokugawa Yoshinobu.

tengrism.s: Tengrism is the modern name for the traditional religion of the Turkic and Mongol peoples of the Eurasian steppe, centred on Tengri, the god of the sky, together with the earth, spirits of nature and ancestors, and shamans who mediated with them. Rulers such as the Göktürk…

tem-binoka.s: Tem Binoka was the ruler of the Kingdom of Abemama in the Gilbert Islands from the 1870s until his death in 1891. He ruled as an autocrat, controlling land, labour and the copra trade and dealing directly with European ships.

terek-river.s: The Terek is a river of the North Caucasus, about 620 kilometres long, which rises on the slopes of Mount Kazbek in Georgia, flows through the Darial Gorge and past Vladikavkaz, and enters the Caspian Sea in Dagestan. Its valley was settled by Alans, Kabardians and, from the…

teispids.s: Teispids is the name historians give to the early Persian royal line descended from Teispes, which ruled Anshan in Fars in the 7th and 6th centuries BCE. Its kings, including Cyrus I and Cambyses I, used the title king of Anshan, and Cyrus the Great came from this family.

tiridates-i-of-armenia.s: Tiridates I was king of Armenia in the mid-1st century CE and founder of the Arsacid dynasty of Armenia. A brother of the Parthian king Vologases I, he was placed on the Armenian throne by his brother, provoking war with Rome.

tigranocerta.s: Tigranocerta was a city founded in the early 1st century BCE by Tigranes the Great as the new capital of his Armenian empire, in the upper Tigris region of present-day south-eastern Turkey. He populated it with people deported from Cappadocia, Cilicia and other conquered lands.

the-bafut-beagles.s: The Bafut Beagles is a 1954 book by the British naturalist Gerald Durrell, describing his animal-collecting expedition to the Cameroon Grassfields in 1949. Much of it is set at the court of the Fon of Bafut, Achirimbi II, whose hospitality and personality the book made widely…

tikar-people.s: The Tikar are a people of the Tikar plain in central Cameroon. Many of the ruling dynasties of the Cameroon Grassfields, including those of Bamum, Nso and Bafut, trace their origins to Tikar princes or princesses who left their homeland and founded new kingdoms, so that Tikar…

touba.s: Touba is a city in central Senegal, founded in 1887 by the Sufi leader Amadou Bamba in the former kingdom of Baol. It is the holy city of the Mouride brotherhood and the site of its Great Mosque, inaugurated in 1963, where Bamba is buried.

tete.s: Tete is a city on the south bank of the Zambezi in north-western Mozambique and the capital of Tete Province. The Portuguese established a trading post there in the 16th century, and with Sena it became a base for the ivory, gold and slave trade with the interior and for the…

tanoa-visawaqa.s: Tanoa Visawaqa was the Vunivalu, or war king, of Bau in Fiji from the late 1820s until his death in 1852. Driven into exile by a revolt in the 1830s, he was restored with the help of his son Seru Epenisa Cakobau and extended Bau's dominance over much of eastern Fiji through…

thimphu.s: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan, in the valley of the Wang Chhu in the west of the country. It grew around Tashichho Dzong, the fortress-monastery that houses the throne room, government offices and the central monk body, and was made the permanent capital…

treaty-of-punakha.s: The Treaty of Punakha was signed in January 1910 between Bhutan and British India. Britain doubled Bhutan's annual subsidy and promised not to interfere in its internal affairs, while Bhutan agreed to be guided by Britain in its external relations.

treaty-of-angers-851.s: The Treaty of Angers was agreed in 851 between the West Frankish king Charles the Bald and the Breton ruler Erispoe after the Breton victory at Jengland. Charles recognised Erispoe as king and granted him the counties of Rennes and Nantes and the Pays de Retz in return for his…

treaty-of-neuilly-sur-seine.s: The Treaty of Neuilly-sur-Seine was the peace treaty between the Allied powers and Bulgaria after the First World War, signed on 27 November 1919. Bulgaria ceded Western Thrace, losing its access to the Aegean, and several border districts to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and…

treaty-of-kiganda.s: The Treaty of Kiganda was the agreement of June 1903 by which Mwami Mwezi IV Gisabo of Burundi submitted to German authority after years of resistance and a German punitive campaign. In return the Germans recognised him as ruler, and Burundi was then governed through indirect…

torwa-dynasty.s: The Torwa dynasty ruled the kingdom of Butua on the south-western plateau of present-day Zimbabwe from the mid-15th century, after the decline of Great Zimbabwe. Its capital, Khami, near modern Bulawayo, is a World Heritage Site with terraced and decorated stone walling.

thirunavaya.s: Thirunavaya is a village in Malappuram district, Kerala, on the north bank of the Bharathappuzha river. It is known for its Navamukunda temple and as the venue of the Mamankam, the great twelve-yearly festival presided over by the Zamorins of Calicut until 1755, at which rival…

tiberius.s: Tiberius was the second Roman emperor, ruling from 14 to 37 CE as the stepson and adopted heir of Augustus. Before his accession he was Rome's leading general, campaigning in Pannonia, Illyricum and Germany and crushing the Great Illyrian Revolt of 6–9 CE.

t-e-lawrence.s: T. E. Lawrence was a British archaeologist, army officer and writer. Before the First World War he worked on the British Museum excavations at Carchemish from 1911 to 1914, partly alongside Leonard Woolley.

tacaynamo.s: Tacaynamo is the legendary founder of the ruling dynasty of Chimor on the north coast of Peru. According to a tradition recorded by the Spanish, he arrived by sea on a raft of logs, settled in the Moche valley and founded the dynasty at Chan Chan, the Chimú capital.

tumbes.s: Tumbes is a city in far northern Peru, near the border with Ecuador, and capital of the Tumbes Region. In the 15th century it marked the northern limit of the kingdom of Chimor and then became an Inca outpost.

tarsus.s: Tarsus is a city in southern Turkey, in the Cilician plain on the Berdan (ancient Cydnus) river near the Mediterranean. An ancient city, it was the capital of the kingdom of Cilicia and later of the Roman province of Cilicia, and it was the birthplace of the apostle Paul.

the-mounth.s: The Mounth is the range of hills forming the eastern end of the Grampian Mountains in Scotland, running from the Cairngorms towards the coast near Stonehaven. It separates Angus and the Mearns from Deeside and Aberdeenshire, and its passes were key routes north.

thrissur.s: Thrissur is a city in central Kerala, India, built around the Vadakkunnathan Temple on a hill at its centre. Rebuilt and enlarged by Sakthan Thampuran, ruler of Cochin from 1790 to 1805, it became a commercial hub and is known as the cultural capital of Kerala.

theodore-von-neuhoff.s: Theodore von Neuhoff was a Westphalian adventurer who was crowned king of Corsica in April 1736 by islanders in revolt against Genoa. He landed with arms and money obtained abroad, set up a court, created knighthoods and minted coins, but left the island within eight months to…

trpimirovic-dynasty.s: The Trpimirović dynasty ruled Croatia, first as dukes and from about 925 as kings, from the mid-9th century to the late 11th century. Named after Duke Trpimir I, it included Tomislav, the first king, and Petar Krešimir IV.

trajans-column.s: Trajan's Column is a Roman triumphal column in Trajan's Forum in Rome, dedicated in 113 CE. Its spiral frieze, about 190 metres long, shows the emperor's two Dacian Wars of 101–102 and 105–106 CE in more than 2,500 figures and is a major source for the Roman army and the Dacians.

treaty-of-rapallo-1920.s: The Treaty of Rapallo was signed on 12 November 1920 by Italy and the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes to settle their border after the First World War. Italy received Istria, Zara (Zadar) and several islands, while the rest of Dalmatia went to the Yugoslav kingdom, and…

trelleborg-slagelse.s: Trelleborg is a Viking Age ring fortress near Slagelse on Zealand, Denmark, built around 980 under King Harald Bluetooth. Its circular rampart, divided into four quarters with uniform longhouses, follows the same plan as Fyrkat, Aggersborg and the other Danish ring forts.

tenpa-tsering.s: Tenpa Tsering was king of Derge in Kham, eastern Tibet, in the early 18th century. In 1729 he founded the Derge Parkhang, the printing house whose woodblocks for the Kangyur and other Buddhist texts are still in use.

tintagel.s: Tintagel is a headland and village on the north coast of Cornwall, England. Excavations have found large quantities of imported Mediterranean pottery and glass of the 5th and 6th centuries, showing that it was a high-status site, probably a royal centre of Dumnonia.

tang-e-sarvak.s: Tang-e Sarvak is a valley in the Zagros mountains of Khuzestan, south-western Iran, known for rock reliefs carved on large boulders in the Parthian period. The reliefs show rulers and nobles of Elymais in Parthian dress, banqueting, hunting and receiving homage, with Aramaic…

tharyps.s: Tharyps was king of the Molossians of Epirus in the late 5th century BCE. Educated at Athens, he is credited by ancient writers with introducing Greek customs, letters and institutions to his kingdom, and he was an ancestor of the later Aeacid kings, including Pyrrhus.

thesprotians.s: The Thesprotians were one of the three main tribal groups of ancient Epirus, with the Molossians and Chaonians, living in the south-west of the region along the Ionian coast. Homer mentions their land, and the oracle of the dead on the Acheron lay in their territory.

treaty-of-aranjuez-1801.s: The Treaty of Aranjuez of 21 March 1801 was an agreement between France and Spain confirming the secret Treaty of San Ildefonso of 1800. Duke Ferdinand of Parma renounced his duchy, and his son Louis received Tuscany as the new Kingdom of Etruria, in return for Spain's…

tanah-lot.s: Tanah Lot is a Hindu sea temple on a rock just off the south-west coast of Bali, Indonesia, cut off from the shore at high tide. Tradition credits its foundation to the 16th-century priest Dang Hyang Nirartha, and it is one of the island's chain of sea temples dedicated to the…

the-knight-in-the-panthers-skin.n: The Knight in the Panther's Skin
the-knight-in-the-panthers-skin.s: The Knight in the Panther's Skin is a Georgian epic poem written by Shota Rustaveli around 1200 and dedicated to Queen Tamar. It tells of the knights Avtandil and Tariel and their quest for Tariel's lost beloved, Nestan-Darejan, celebrating friendship, loyalty and love.

tefnakht.s: Tefnakht was a Libyan chief of Sais in the western Nile Delta who, in the later 8th century BCE, led a coalition of Delta and Middle Egyptian rulers and pushed south. The Kushite king Piye defeated the coalition around 728 BCE, and Tefnakht submitted by oath without meeting…

thoth.s: Thoth was the ancient Egyptian god of writing, wisdom, the moon and reckoning, shown as an ibis-headed man or as a baboon. He was believed to have invented hieroglyphs, kept the records of the gods and written down the verdict when the hearts of the dead were weighed.

troodos-mountains.s: The Troodos Mountains are the largest mountain range of Cyprus, in the west and centre of the island, rising to Mount Olympus at 1,952 metres. Their geology, a slice of ancient ocean floor, made them rich in copper, which was mined from the Bronze Age and made Cyprus a centre…

trabzon.s: Trabzon, historically Trebizond, is a port on the Black Sea coast of north-eastern Turkey. Founded as the Greek colony of Trapezus, it was the capital of the Empire of Trebizond from 1204 until the Ottoman conquest of 1461, and a major outlet for the caravan trade with Persia.

teimuraz-i-of-kakheti.s: Teimuraz I was king of Kakheti in eastern Georgia from 1605, with interruptions, and later also of Kartli, as well as a noted poet. His long resistance to Shah Abbas I of Iran led to the devastation of Kakheti in 1614–1617, when many thousands of people were killed or…

tosali.s: Tosali was an ancient city of Kalinga in eastern India, near modern Bhubaneswar. Under the Maurya Empire it was the seat of a provincial viceroy, a royal prince, and Ashoka's separate rock edicts at nearby Dhauli are addressed to its officials.

temple-of-the-tooth.s: The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, or Sri Dalada Maligawa, is a Buddhist temple in the royal palace complex at Kandy, Sri Lanka, that houses the relic of the Buddha's tooth. Possession of the relic was long seen as conferring the right to rule the island, and the kings of…

tel-dan.s: Tel Dan is an archaeological mound in northern Israel at the foot of Mount Hermon, beside one of the sources of the Jordan. It was the Canaanite city of Laish, mentioned in Egyptian texts and the Mari letters, which the Bible says the tribe of Dan conquered and renamed.

treaty-of-jeddah-1927.s: The Treaty of Jeddah, signed on 20 May 1927 between Britain and Ibn Saud, recognised the full independence of his Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd and its dependencies, replacing the Treaty of Darin of 1915, which had made Nejd a British protectorate. Ibn Saud in turn recognised…

treaty-of-jeddah-2000.s: The Treaty of Jeddah, signed on 12 June 2000, settled the land and sea border between Saudi Arabia and Yemen, ending a dispute dating back to their war of 1934 and the Treaty of Taif. It confirmed the line agreed at Taif in the west and drew a new boundary across the desert…

terqa.s: Terqa was an ancient city on the middle Euphrates in eastern Syria, at the site of Tell Ashara. A centre of the cult of the god Dagan, it belonged to the kingdom of Mari and after Mari's fall became the capital of the Kingdom of Hana in the 2nd millennium BCE.

treaty-of-georgievsk.s: The Treaty of Georgievsk was signed on 24 July 1783 between the Russian Empire and Erekle II of Kartli-Kakheti. Erekle renounced Persian overlordship and accepted a Russian protectorate, while Russia guaranteed his kingdom's territory and the Bagrationi dynasty.

toprak-kala.s: Toprak-Kala is an ancient fortified city in Karakalpakstan, north-western Uzbekistan, that served as a royal seat of the kings of Khwarazm in the 2nd and 3rd centuries CE. Excavated by Soviet archaeologists under Sergei Tolstov, its high palace contained halls with wall…

thotagamuwe-sri-rahula-thera.s: Thotagamuwe Sri Rahula Thera was a Sinhala Buddhist monk and poet of the Kingdom of Kotte in Sri Lanka and the leading literary figure of the reign of Parakramabahu VI. His works include the messenger poems Selalihini Sandeshaya and Paravi Sandeshaya and the long poem…

thiksey-monastery.s: Thiksey Monastery is a Gelug Buddhist monastery on a hilltop about 19 km east of Leh in Ladakh, India. Founded in the 15th century, its tiers of white buildings rising up the hill resemble the Potala Palace in Lhasa.

treaty-of-tingmosgang.s: The Treaty of Tingmosgang was concluded in 1684 between Ladakh and Tibet at the end of the Tibet–Ladakh–Mughal War of 1679–84. It fixed the frontier between the two near Demchok, left western Tibet, including Guge, to Lhasa, and set up regular trade and tribute missions…

tzath-i.s: Tzath I was king of Lazica in western Georgia in the early 6th century. In 522 he went to Constantinople, rejecting Sasanian overlordship, and was baptised and crowned by Emperor Justin I, who gave him a Roman noblewoman as his wife.

tomrair-mac-ailchi.s: Tomrair mac Ailchi was a Viking leader who established a permanent Norse fleet base at Limerick in 922. From there his forces raided widely along the River Shannon and its lakes, and the Limerick Norse became rivals of the Vikings of Dublin, who defeated them in 937.

treniota.s: Treniota was a Lithuanian duke and nephew of King Mindaugas who led resistance to the Livonian Order in the 1260s and encouraged the uprisings that followed the Battle of Durbe. In 1263 he and Daumantas murdered Mindaugas, and Treniota seized power as grand duke.

teutberga.s: Teutberga was queen of Lotharingia as the wife of Lothair II, whom she married in 855. Childless, she became the object of Lothair's long campaign to divorce her and marry his mistress Waldrada, which included accusations of incest against her.

treaty-of-prum.s: The Treaty of Prüm was the arrangement of September 855 by which the dying Emperor Lothair I divided Middle Francia among his three sons at the abbey of Prüm in the Eifel. Louis II received Italy with the imperial title, Lothair II the northern lands that became Lotharingia,…

tell-el-farkha.s: Tell el-Farkha is an archaeological site in the eastern Nile Delta of Egypt, excavated by a Polish expedition since 1998. Occupied from the Buto-Maadi period in the 4th millennium BCE into the Old Kingdom, it has yielded early breweries, an administrative-cultic centre and…

temenos.s: Temenos was, in Greek myth, a great-great-grandson of Heracles who led the return of the Heracleidae into the Peloponnese and received Argos as his share. The kings of Macedon, the Argeads, claimed descent from him, which allowed Alexander I to be accepted as a Greek at the…

tharu-people.s: The Tharu are an indigenous people of the Terai lowlands along the border of Nepal and India. Long resistant to malaria, they farmed the forested plains when few others lived there, and they speak Indo-Aryan Tharu languages.

tau-american-samoa.s: Taʻu is the largest and easternmost of the Manuʻa Islands in American Samoa, a volcanic island rising to Lata Mountain, the highest point in the territory. It was the residence of the Tuʻi Manuʻa, the paramount chief of Manuʻa.

tagaloa.s: Tagaloa, also Tangaloa, is the supreme creator god of Samoan and Tongan tradition, cognate with Tangaroa elsewhere in Polynesia. In Samoan myth he created the islands from rocks in the ocean and peopled them, and the title of Tuʻi Manuʻa was said to descend from him.

tui-manua-elisala.s: Tuʻi Manuʻa Elisala was the paramount chief of the Manuʻa Islands at the eastern end of Samoa at the turn of the 20th century. After the Tripartite Convention of 1899 assigned eastern Samoa to the United States, he signed the deed of cession of Manuʻa on 16 July 1904.

tangier.s: Tangier is a port city in northern Morocco on the Strait of Gibraltar. As Tingis it was a Phoenician and Mauretanian town and the capital of the Roman province of Mauretania Tingitana.

tarik-sulayman.s: Tarik Sulayman was a chief of Macabebe in Pampanga, in the Philippines, who led a coalition fleet against the Spanish at Manila in 1571. Spanish accounts describe him only as the young chief of Macabebe.

tamworth.s: Tamworth is a market town in Staffordshire, England, on the River Tame. It was the principal royal seat of the kings of Mercia from the 8th century, and Offa had a palace there.

taichung.s: Taichung is a city in central-western Taiwan and one of its largest municipalities. In the 17th century the plains of the area were home to indigenous peoples such as the Pazeh and Papora.

thubchen-monastery.s: Thubchen Monastery is a 15th-century Buddhist assembly hall in Lo Manthang, capital of the former Kingdom of Lo in Mustang, Nepal. Its great hall, supported by tall wooden columns, has wall paintings of Buddhas and deities that are among the finest in the Tibetan cultural world.

treasury-of-atreus.s: The Treasury of Atreus is a monumental tholos tomb at Mycenae in southern Greece, built around 1250 BCE. Its corbelled stone dome, over 13 metres high, was the largest in the world for more than a thousand years.

teesta-river.s: The Teesta is a river that rises in the Himalayas of Sikkim and flows south through West Bengal into Bangladesh, where it joins the Brahmaputra (Jamuna). About 414 km long, it marked the eastern limit of Gorkha expansion in the late 18th century and the western edge of the…

treaty-of-sugauli.s: The Treaty of Sugauli ended the Anglo-Nepalese War between the Kingdom of Nepal and the British East India Company. Signed in December 1815 and ratified in March 1816, it forced Nepal to give up Sikkim, Kumaon, Garhwal and much of the Terai, about a third of its territory, and…

toffa-i.s: Toffa I was king of Porto-Novo, on the coast of present-day Benin, from 1874 until his death in 1908. Threatened by Dahomey and by British Lagos, he renewed the French protectorate over his kingdom in 1882 and supported the French in their war against Dahomey in 1890–94.

timna-yemen.s: Timna was the capital of the ancient kingdom of Qataban in Yemen, at the site now called Hajar Kuhlan in Wadi Bayhan. Lying at the start of the incense caravan route to the north, it had temples, a walled city with gates and a stele inscribed with a market law regulating trade…

turfan.s: Turfan, or Turpan, is an oasis city in eastern Xinjiang, China, in the Turfan Depression, one of the lowest and hottest places in Asia. Watered by underground karez channels, it was a major stop on the Silk Road, home to the kingdom of Gaochang and from the 9th century to the…

tahaa.s: Tahaʻa is an island in the Leeward Islands of French Polynesia, sharing a single lagoon with neighbouring Raiatea. In the 18th century it was ruled with Raiatea by the Tamatoa chiefs and was conquered by warriors from Bora Bora.

taputapuatea.s: Taputapuatea is a marae complex at Opoa on the island of Raiatea in French Polynesia, the most important religious centre of eastern Polynesia in the centuries before European contact. Dedicated to the god ʻOro, it drew chiefs and priests from across the Society Islands and…

teraupoo.s: Teraupoʻo was a chief of Raiatea in French Polynesia who led armed resistance against French annexation of the island, proclaimed in 1888. His followers held out in the interior for nearly a decade, until a French expedition put down the rising and captured him in 1897,…

tupaia.s: Tupaia was a Polynesian priest and navigator from Raiatea who joined James Cook's expedition on the Endeavour at Tahiti in 1769. He drew a chart of the islands known to Tahitians, guided Cook through the Society Islands and acted as interpreter with the Māori in New Zealand.

taliesin.s: Taliesin was a Welsh poet of the late 6th century, one of the earliest named poets of the British language. A group of praise poems in the Book of Taliesin, addressed to Urien of Rheged and his son Owain, are thought by many scholars to be his genuine work.

tissamaharama.s: Tissamaharama is a town in Hambantota District in southern Sri Lanka, identified with Mahagama, the capital of the ancient kingdom of Ruhuna. The chronicles say it was founded by Mahanaga in the 3rd century BCE, and excavations have revealed an early urban settlement.

tissa-wewa.s: Tissa Wewa is an ancient irrigation reservoir at Tissamaharama in southern Sri Lanka. Built in the early centuries of the kingdom of Ruhuna, it watered the rice fields of the dry south-east and is still in use.

treaty-of-berlin-1889.s: The Treaty of Berlin of 1889 was an agreement between Germany, Britain and the United States on the future of Samoa, made after the crisis at Apia earlier that year. It recognised Samoa as a neutral and independent kingdom, restored Malietoa Laupepa as king and placed its…

tupua-tamasese-titimaea.s: Tupua Tamasese Titimaea was a Samoan paramount chief who was installed as king with German backing in 1887, after Germany deposed and exiled Malietoa Laupepa. His rule provoked a rising led by Mataʻafa Iosefo, and the resulting crisis brought German, American and British…

tioman-island.s: Tioman Island is a mountainous island in the South China Sea off the east coast of Pahang, Malaysia. Its fresh water and sheltered anchorages made it a landmark and watering stop for ships sailing between China and the Strait of Malacca for many centuries.

tumlong.s: Tumlong was the capital of the kingdom of Sikkim from 1793 to 1894, in northern Sikkim, India. The court moved there from Rabdentse after attacks from Nepal, and the Treaty of Tumlong of 1861, which placed Sikkim under strong British influence, was signed there.

tvrda.s: Tvrđa is the 18th-century fortress and old town of Osijek in eastern Croatia. Built by the Habsburgs from 1712 on the site of the Ottoman town, it was laid out as a star-shaped Baroque fortress with barracks, churches and administrative buildings.

topasses.s: The Topasses were a Portuguese-speaking Catholic community of mixed Portuguese, Indian and Southeast Asian descent who dominated much of Timor from the 17th century. Led by the rival Hornay and da Costa families from their base at Lifau, they controlled the sandalwood trade…

the-weald.s: The Weald is an area of south-east England between the North and South Downs, covering parts of Kent, Sussex, Surrey and Hampshire. In Anglo-Saxon times it was a great forest, Andredesweald, that separated the South Saxons from their neighbours and was used mainly for seasonal…

tatev-monastery.s: Tatev Monastery is a 9th-century Armenian monastery on a basalt promontory above the Vorotan gorge in Syunik Province, southern Armenia. Seat of the bishops of Syunik, it owned many villages and in the 14th and 15th centuries became a leading centre of learning, associated…

taprobane.s: Taprobane was the ancient Greek and Roman name for Sri Lanka, derived from Tambapanni, the name of the first Sinhalese settlement. Greek writers learned of the island after the campaigns of Alexander the Great, and it was described by Megasthenes, Pliny the Elder and Ptolemy,…

thurisind.s: Thurisind was king of the Gepids from about 548 to about 560. His reign was dominated by war with the neighbouring Lombards under Audoin, in which Byzantium supported each side in turn; his son Turismod was killed by Audoin's son Alboin in battle around 551.

tynwald.s: Tynwald is the parliament of the Isle of Man, which descends from the Norse assembly, or thing, of the Kingdom of Mann and the Isles and claims a continuous existence of more than a thousand years. Each year on 5 July it holds an open-air sitting at Tynwald Hill in St John's,…

treaty-of-perth.s: The Treaty of Perth of 2 July 1266 ended the conflict between Norway and Scotland over the western islands. Magnus VI of Norway ceded the Hebrides and the Isle of Man to Alexander III of Scotland in return for 4,000 marks and an annual payment of 100 marks, while Norway kept…

theodelinda.s: Theodelinda was a Bavarian princess who became queen of the Lombards by marrying King Authari in 589 and, after his death, King Agilulf. A Catholic who corresponded with Pope Gregory the Great, she encouraged the Lombards to move from Arian to Catholic Christianity.

the-fens.s: The Fens are a low-lying region of former marshland around the Wash in eastern England, in Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire and Norfolk. In the Middle Ages they were a land of islands and waterways with great abbeys such as Ely, Peterborough and Crowland.

tiaret.s: Tiaret is a city on the high plateaus of north-western Algeria. Nearby stood Tahert, founded in the 8th century by Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam as the capital of the Ibadi Rustamid imamate, a centre of trade and learning until the Fatimids destroyed it in 909.

theodoric-ii-king-of-the-visigoths.n: Theodoric II, King of the Visigoths
theodoric-ii-king-of-the-visigoths.s: Theodoric II was king of the Visigoths from 453 to 466, after murdering his brother Thorismund. Ruling from Toulouse as a Roman ally, he helped make Avitus emperor in 455 and in 456 crushed the Suebi in Hispania, killing their king Rechiar.

tullyhogue-fort.s: Tullyhogue Fort is a hilltop enclosure near Cookstown in County Tyrone, Northern Ireland, the inauguration place of the O'Neill kings of Tír Eoghain. New kings were installed there on a stone chair, with the O'Cahans and O'Hagans playing ceremonial roles.

tupou-vi.s: Tupou VI is king of Tonga, who succeeded his brother George Tupou V in March 2012 and was crowned in 2015. Before his accession he served as prime minister from 2000 to 2006 and as Tonga's high commissioner to Australia.

toro-agreement.s: The Toro Agreement of 1900 was concluded between the British commissioner Sir Harry Johnston and the king and chiefs of Toro. It defined Toro's status as a kingdom within the Uganda Protectorate, fixed its boundaries and taxes, and allotted land to the king and chiefs.

tainan.s: Tainan is a city in south-western Taiwan and the island's oldest city. The Dutch built Fort Zeelandia and Fort Provintia there in the 1620s and 1650s, and after Koxinga expelled them in 1662 it became the capital of the Zheng kingdom of Tungning.

tale-of-aqhat.s: The Tale of Aqhat is an epic poem from Ugarit, written in alphabetic cuneiform on clay tablets of the 14th or 13th century BCE copied by the scribe Ilimilku. It tells of the hero Aqhat, son of the righteous king Danel, who is killed after refusing to give his bow to the…

tushpa.s: Tushpa was the capital of the kingdom of Urartu, built on a long limestone rock above the eastern shore of Lake Van in present-day Turkey. King Sarduri I fortified it around 840 BCE, and his successors carved their annals and tombs into the rock.

talietumu.s: Talietumu is the ruin of a fortified settlement in the south of Wallis Island, built by Tongan invaders who conquered the island in the 15th century. Its basalt walls, raised platforms and ramps enclosed the residence of the Tongan chiefs who ruled Uvea.

tripartite-pact.s: The Tripartite Pact was signed in Berlin on 27 September 1940 by Germany, Italy and Japan, who pledged to assist one another if attacked by a power not yet in the war, chiefly aimed at the United States. Hungary, Romania, Slovakia and Bulgaria joined, and Yugoslavia signed on…

tawhiao.s: Tāwhiao was the second Māori King, succeeding his father Pōtatau Te Wherowhero in 1860. During the invasion of the Waikato in 1863–1864 his people lost their lands, and he withdrew into the King Country, where he led his followers for nearly twenty years.

turangawaewae.s: Tūrangawaewae is a marae in Ngāruawāhia, New Zealand, the official residence of the Māori monarch and the centre of the King movement. It was established in the 1920s on the bank of the Waikato river under the leadership of Te Puea Hērangi.

teshub.s: Teshub was the Hurrian god of storms and the sky, the head of the Hurrian pantheon, with his consort Hebat. Worshipped across northern Mesopotamia, Syria and Anatolia, he was identified with the Hittite storm god and became the chief god of the Hittite state religion.

takasugi-shinsaku.s: Takasugi Shinsaku was a samurai of the Chōshū domain and a leader of the movement to overthrow the Tokugawa shogunate. A student of Yoshida Shōin, he founded the Kiheitai in 1863, a militia that admitted commoners as well as samurai.

tarabai.s: Tarabai was a Maratha queen, the widow of Chhatrapati Rajaram. After his death in 1700 she ruled as regent for her young son Shivaji II and led the Maratha resistance against the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.

treaty-of-warna.s: The Treaty of Warna was concluded in 1731 between Shahu, the Maratha king at Satara, and his cousin Sambhaji II of Kolhapur, ending their long rivalry over the Maratha throne. Sambhaji accepted Shahu's sovereignty over most of the Maratha lands, while Kolhapur kept a separate…

temne-people.s: The Temne are a West African people of northern and central Sierra Leone, one of the country's two largest ethnic groups alongside the Mende. They speak a Mel language, and before colonial rule they were organised in chiefdoms such as Koya on the Sierra Leone estuary, whose…

taraba-state.s: Taraba State is a state in north-eastern Nigeria, created in 1991 from part of Gongola State, with its capital at Jalingo. Named after the Taraba River, it lies along the Benue and the Cameroon border and includes the Mambilla Plateau.

tulip-revolution.s: The Tulip Revolution was a wave of protests in Kyrgyzstan in March 2005 that overthrew President Askar Akayev. Triggered by disputed parliamentary elections, it began in the south, in Jalal-Abad and Osh, and culminated in the storming of the presidential offices in Bishkek on…

tordera-river.s: The Tordera is a river of Catalonia, Spain, about 60 kilometres long, rising in the Montseny massif and reaching the Mediterranean between Malgrat de Mar and Blanes. Its lower course marks the boundary between the comarques of the Maresme and La Selva, and its valley is an…

tarafa.s: Tarafa ibn al-Abd was a pre-Islamic Arabian poet of the Bakr tribe, active in the mid-6th century, whose ode is one of the Mu'allaqat, the celebrated long poems of early Arabic literature. He spent time at the Lakhmid court of al-Hira under King Amr ibn Hind, and tradition…

tenggarong.s: Tenggarong is a town in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, on the Mahakam River upstream from Samarinda, and the seat of Kutai Kartanegara Regency. The sultans of Kutai Kartanegara moved their capital there in 1782, and their former palace, built in 1936, now houses the Mulawarman…

treaty-of-portsmouth.s: The Treaty of Portsmouth ended the Russo-Japanese War. It was signed on 5 September 1905 at Portsmouth, New Hampshire, after talks mediated by US President Theodore Roosevelt.

triple-intervention.s: The Triple Intervention was the diplomatic intervention of Russia, Germany and France on 23 April 1895, six days after the Treaty of Shimonoseki ended the First Sino-Japanese War. The three powers pressed Japan to give back the Liaodong peninsula, which China had ceded to it,…

the-prince-of-homburg.s: The Prince of Homburg is a play by Heinrich von Kleist, completed around 1810 and first performed in 1821. It is loosely based on Frederick II of Hesse-Homburg, who commanded the cavalry at the Battle of Fehrbellin in 1675.

tiengen.s: Tiengen is a historic town on the Wutach river near the Swiss border in Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It was the seat of the counts of Sulz and later the Schwarzenbergs as landgraves of the Klettgau, whose castle still stands above the old town.

telaga-said.s: Telaga Said is an oil field in Langkat Regency, North Sumatra, Indonesia, the first commercially productive oil field in the Dutch East Indies. Oil was struck there in 1885 by the Dutch planter Aeilko Jans Zijlker, who obtained a concession from the Sultan of Langkat.

tilokarat.s: Tilokarat was king of Lan Na, in what is now northern Thailand, from 1441 to 1487, and its most powerful ruler. He waged long wars against Ayutthaya, extended Lan Na's power over Nan and Phrae, and was a great patron of Theravada Buddhism.

titus-quinctius-flamininus.s: Titus Quinctius Flamininus was a Roman general and politician who defeated Philip V of Macedon at Cynoscephalae in 197 BCE, ending the Second Macedonian War. At the Isthmian Games of 196 BCE he proclaimed the freedom of the Greek cities from Macedonian rule, and Roman forces…

tran-nghe-tong.s: Trần Nghệ Tông was emperor of Vietnam of the Tran dynasty from 1370 to 1372 and then ruled as retired emperor until his death. He trusted his relative Ho Quy Ly with great power, a decision that allowed Ho Quy Ly to depose the Tran and found the Ho dynasty in 1400.

tabasco.s: Tabasco is a state in south-eastern Mexico on the Gulf of Mexico, with its capital at Villahermosa. Its low, wet plains are crossed by the Grijalva and Usumacinta rivers.

tonala-river.s: The Tonalá River is a river of south-eastern Mexico that forms part of the border between the states of Veracruz and Tabasco before flowing into the Gulf of Mexico. Its lower course runs through coastal marshes, where the Olmec centre of La Venta stood on an island of higher…

taif-agreement.s: The Taif Agreement was negotiated by Lebanese members of parliament at Taif in Saudi Arabia and signed in October 1989 to end the Lebanese Civil War. It shared parliamentary seats equally between Christians and Muslims, reduced the powers of the Maronite president in favour of…

toul.s: Toul is a town on the Moselle in Lorraine, north-eastern France, the Roman Tullum, chief town of the Gallic Leuci. A bishopric from late Roman times, it became a free city whose bishops ruled a small prince-bishopric in the Holy Roman Empire.

tongtai-temple.s: Tongtai Temple was a Buddhist monastery in Jiankang (modern Nanjing), founded by Emperor Wu of Liang in 527 beside his palace. The emperor gave himself to the temple as a servant several times, and his ministers had to pay huge ransoms to the monastery to bring him back.

true-whig-party.s: The True Whig Party is a Liberian political party founded in 1869. It held power without interruption from 1878 to 1980, making Liberia in effect a one-party state dominated by the Americo-Liberian elite under presidents such as Charles D. B. King, William Tubman and William…

theoderich-von-treyden.s: Theoderich von Treyden was a Cistercian monk and missionary in Livonia and the first abbot of Dünamünde near Riga. With Bishop Albert of Riga he founded the Livonian Brothers of the Sword in 1202.

teruel.s: Teruel is a city in Aragon, eastern Spain, the capital of the province of the same name. Founded as a Christian frontier town by Alfonso II of Aragon in 1171, it preserves fine Mudéjar towers and churches, a World Heritage Site.

theodore-i-palaiologos.s: Theodore I Palaiologos was the Byzantine Despot of the Morea from 1383 to 1407, a son of Emperor John V. He strengthened Byzantine rule in the Peloponnese, settled Albanian colonists there and fought the Ottomans, the Navarrese and Venice.

trim-county-meath.s: Trim is a town on the River Boyne in County Meath, Ireland. Hugh de Lacy made it the centre of his Lordship of Meath after 1172, and Trim Castle, begun by him and completed by his son Walter, is the largest Anglo-Norman castle in Ireland.

tolfa.s: Tolfa is a hill town in the Tolfa Mountains of Lazio, north-west of Rome. The discovery of rich alum deposits there in the early 1460s gave the Papal States a lucrative monopoly of a mineral vital to the European cloth industry, replacing supplies lost when the Ottomans took…

tempio-malatestiano.s: The Tempio Malatestiano is the cathedral of Rimini, originally the Gothic church of San Francesco. From about 1450 Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta had it remodelled by Leon Battista Alberti, who designed an unfinished classical façade inspired by Roman triumphal arches, as a…

treaty-of-westminster-ardtornish.s: The Treaty of Westminster-Ardtornish was a secret agreement made in 1462 between Edward IV of England, John MacDonald II, Lord of the Isles, and the exiled James Douglas, 9th Earl of Douglas. Scotland was to be conquered and divided, the Lord of the Isles and his kinsmen…

tinos.s: Tinos is an island of the Cyclades in the Aegean Sea, Greece. Taken around 1207 by the Venetian Ghisi family and ruled directly by Venice from 1390, it held out longer than any other Venetian possession in the Aegean, until the Ottomans took it in 1715.

tibnin.s: Tibnin is a town in southern Lebanon, in the hills east of Tyre. Around 1105 Hugh of Saint-Omer built the crusader castle of Toron there, which became the centre of a lordship of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

tollensians.s: The Tollensians (Tollenser) were a West Slavic tribe of the Lutician federation, named after the Tollense river and lake in modern Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Germany. Together with the Redarii they formed the core of the federation, and in 1057 they fought the Circipanians and…

tlos.s: Tlos was one of the oldest and largest cities of ancient Lycia, on a hill above the Xanthos valley in south-western Turkey, generally identified with the Dalawa of Hittite texts. It was one of the six leading members of the Lycian League.

theobald-bourke-1st-viscount-mayo.s: Theobald Bourke, known as Tibbot na Long ('of the ships'), was the son of Grace O'Malley and Richard an Iarainn Bourke, said to have been born at sea. He grew up as a Mayo lord and at first fought the English, but sided with the Crown during the Nine Years' War, including at…

thirumalai-nayak-palace.s: The Thirumalai Nayak Palace is a 17th-century palace in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, built around 1636 for Tirumala Nayak, ruler of the Madurai Nayak kingdom. Built in a blend of Dravidian and Islamic styles, it is known for its huge columns, domes and stucco work.

tun-perak.s: Tun Perak was bendahara (chief minister) of the Malacca Sultanate from about 1456 to 1498, serving four sultans. He led the defence against Siamese invasions and guided the expansion that brought much of the Malay Peninsula and eastern Sumatra under Malacca.

thermidorian-reaction.s: The Thermidorian Reaction was the turn in the French Revolution that began on 9 Thermidor Year II (27 July 1794), when the National Convention arrested Maximilien Robespierre and his allies; they were guillotined the next day and in the days that followed. The Convention then…

treaty-of-salatiga.s: The Treaty of Salatiga, signed in March 1757 in Salatiga, Central Java, ended the long rebellion of Raden Mas Said against the Dutch East India Company and the courts of Surakarta and Yogyakarta. He received lands carved from Surakarta's territory and the title Mangkunegara I,…

tutul-xiu.s: The Tutul Xiu were a Maya ruling lineage of northern Yucatán, associated with Uxmal and, after the fall of Mayapán in the mid-15th century, with the town of Maní. Their rulers, the halach uinic, governed a province of many towns.

tulln.s: Tulln is a town on the Danube in Lower Austria, on the site of the Roman fort of Comagena. It was a residence of the Babenberg margraves before they moved to Klosterneuburg and Vienna, and in the Nibelungenlied it is the place where Kriemhild meets Etzel.

thomas-iii-of-saluzzo.s: Thomas III was Marquis of Saluzzo from 1396 to 1416. Captured in 1394 during wars with the princes of Savoy-Achaea, he spent his imprisonment in Turin writing Le Chevalier errant, an allegorical romance in French.

treaty-of-lyon-1601.s: The Treaty of Lyon, signed on 17 January 1601, ended the war between Henry IV of France and Charles Emmanuel I, Duke of Savoy. Savoy kept the Marquisate of Saluzzo, which it had seized in 1588, and in exchange gave France Bresse, Bugey, Valromey and the Pays de Gex.

tabula-rapinensis.s: The Tabula Rapinensis is a small bronze tablet found at Rapino in Abruzzo, central Italy, inscribed in the Italic dialect of the Marrucini in the Latin alphabet, probably in the 3rd century BCE. It records a sacred regulation of the community of Teate, apparently about the…

tafna.s: The Tafna is a river in north-western Algeria that flows into the Mediterranean near Rachgoun. In antiquity the Numidian royal city of Siga stood near its mouth.

tehran.s: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran, lying at the southern foot of the Alborz mountains. Once a village near the ancient city of Rey, it grew under the Safavids and was made the capital by Agha Mohammad Khan, founder of the Qajar dynasty, in 1786.

treaty-of-giyanti.s: The Treaty of Giyanti, signed on 13 February 1755, divided the Mataram Sultanate of Java into two realms, Surakarta and Yogyakarta. Brokered by the Dutch East India Company, it ended the Third Javanese War of Succession by recognising Pakubuwana III at Surakarta and the rebel…

tata-steel.s: Tata Steel, founded in 1907 as the Tata Iron and Steel Company, is an Indian steel maker and one of the oldest industrial companies of the subcontinent. Planned by Jamsetji Tata and launched by his son Dorabji, it built India's first large integrated steel works at Jamshedpur,…

takaungu.s: Takaungu is a small coastal town in Kilifi County, Kenya, north of Mombasa. After the Busaidi of Oman took Mombasa in 1837, a branch of the Mazrui family settled there and ruled it as a semi-independent town.

takht-e-soleyman.s: Takht-e Soleyman is an archaeological site in West Azerbaijan province, north-western Iran, built around a spring-fed lake on a hilltop. It held the main Sasanian sanctuary of the sacred fire Adur Gushnasp, which Heraclius sacked in 624, and in the thirteenth century the…

thersilion.s: The Thersilion was the great assembly hall of the Arcadian League at Megalopolis in the Peloponnese, built in the 360s BCE. A roofed square hall with rows of columns arranged so that the audience could see the speaker, it could hold several thousand delegates.

theagenes-of-megara.s: Theagenes was tyrant of Megara in Greece in the second half of the seventh century BCE. According to Aristotle he won power by championing the poor against the rich, slaughtering the flocks of wealthy landowners.

theognis-of-megara.s: Theognis of Megara was a Greek elegiac poet of the sixth century BCE. A collection of about 1,400 lines survives under his name, though much of it is by other poets.

timoleon.s: Timoleon was a Corinthian statesman and general sent to Sicily in 344 BCE to help Syracuse. He drove out the tyrant Dionysius II, defeated a large Carthaginian army at the Crimissus river around 339 BCE and overthrew tyrants in other Greek cities.

tarhunazi.s: Tarhunazi was the last king of Melid, a Neo-Hittite kingdom at Arslantepe near Malatya in eastern Turkey. In 712 BCE the Assyrian king Sargon II deposed him, took him captive and made Melid an Assyrian province, giving part of its territory to the neighbouring kingdom of Kummuh.

tsiribihina-river.s: The Tsiribihina is a river in western Madagascar that flows west from the central highlands to the Mozambique Channel near Belo-sur-Tsiribihina. It formed the northern edge of the heartland of the Sakalava kingdom of Menabe, and its gorges are today a well-known route for…

toera.s: Toera was the last king of the Sakalava kingdom of Menabe in western Madagascar. After France conquered Madagascar in 1895 he refused to submit to French rule, and he was killed in 1897 when French troops attacked his capital at Ambiky.

turan-malik.s: Turan Malik was the wife of the Mengujekid ruler Ahmad Shah of Divriği in eastern Anatolia and a daughter of Fakhr al-Din Bahramshah of Erzincan. In 1228–1229 she founded the hospital of the Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği, whose richly carved portal is among the…

tavole-palatine.s: The Tavole Palatine are the remains of a Doric temple of Hera built in the late 6th century BCE outside the Greek colony of Metapontum, near modern Metaponto in Basilicata, southern Italy. Fifteen columns still stand, ten on one side and five on the other, with parts of their…

thermaic-gulf.s: The Thermaic Gulf is an inlet of the north-western Aegean Sea, bordered by Pieria, Macedonia and the Chalcidice peninsula, with Thessaloniki at its head. It takes its name from the ancient town of Therma, on whose site Thessaloniki was founded in 315 BCE.

tizoc.s: Tizoc was the seventh ruler, or tlatoani, of the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan, reigning from 1481 to 1486. His reign brought few conquests, and his campaign against the mountain lordship of Metztitlan ended in failure and heavy losses.

tale-of-sinuhe.s: The Tale of Sinuhe is an ancient Egyptian literary work of the Twelfth Dynasty, often regarded as the finest piece of Middle Egyptian literature. It tells of the courtier Sinuhe, who flees to the Levant on hearing of the death of Amenemhat I, prospers there among foreign…

tafilalt.s: Tafilalt is the largest oasis of Morocco, in the Ziz valley on the edge of the Sahara in the south-east of the country. Its date palms supported the medieval city of Sijilmasa, founded in 757, which became a great northern terminus of the trans-Saharan gold trade.

terceira.s: Terceira is an island of the Azores in the Atlantic, whose main town, Angra do Heroísmo, is a World Heritage Site. During the Portuguese Liberal Wars it was the only part of the kingdom held by supporters of Maria II, who repelled a Miguelist landing at the Battle of Praia in…

thales-of-miletus.s: Thales of Miletus was a Greek thinker of the 6th century BCE, traditionally regarded as the first philosopher and the first of the Seven Sages. He held that water was the origin of all things, seeking natural rather than mythological explanations of the world.

thrasybulus-of-miletus.s: Thrasybulus was the tyrant of Miletus in the late 7th and early 6th centuries BCE. Herodotus relates that during a long Lydian war he deceived King Alyattes by heaping up grain and holding feasts while the Lydian envoy was in the city, convincing him that Miletus could not be…

tawagalawa-letter.s: The Tawagalawa letter is a fragmentary Hittite diplomatic letter of the 13th century BCE, usually attributed to Hattusili III and addressed to the king of Ahhiyawa, whom it calls 'brother'. It complains about the raids of the renegade Piyamaradu, who used Millawanda (Miletus)…

tarkasnawa.s: Tarkasnawa was a king of Mira, a western Anatolian vassal kingdom of the Hittites, in the late 13th century BCE. He is named on the Karabel relief near Izmir, whose reading in 1998 confirmed that Mira reached towards the Aegean, and on a silver seal, the 'Tarkondemos' seal,…

tengu-party-rebellion.s: The Tengu Party Rebellion was a rising of radical loyalist samurai of the Mito domain in 1864, during the last years of the Tokugawa shogunate. Inspired by the Mito school's call to revere the emperor and expel the barbarians, the Tengu faction raised forces at Mount Tsukuba…

trujillo-peru.s: Trujillo is the chief city of northern Peru and capital of the La Libertad region, near the Pacific coast in the Moche valley. It was founded by the Spanish in 1534 and named after Francisco Pizarro's home town in Spain, and it was the first major Peruvian city to declare…

tyendinaga-mohawk-territory.s: Tyendinaga Mohawk Territory is a Mohawk reserve on the Bay of Quinte in south-eastern Ontario, Canada. It was founded in 1784 by Mohawks loyal to Britain who had lost their homes in the Mohawk valley of New York during the American Revolution, led by John Deseronto.

therouanne.s: Thérouanne is a village in the Pas-de-Calais in northern France, on the site of Tarvenna, the Roman capital of the Morini. It became the seat of a large bishopric in the early Middle Ages and grew into a fortified town on the border between France and the Habsburg Netherlands.

tsugaru-clan.s: The Tsugaru were a Japanese daimyo family who ruled the Hirosaki domain at the northern tip of Honshu throughout the Edo period. Its founder, Ōura Tamenobu, was a vassal of the Nanbu who broke away around 1590 and won recognition from Toyotomi Hideyoshi, taking the name Tsugaru.

treaty-of-managua.s: The Treaty of Managua was signed in January 1860 between Great Britain and Nicaragua. Britain gave up its protectorate over the Mosquito Coast and recognised Nicaraguan sovereignty, while the Miskito received a self-governing reserve around Bluefields.

tanyus-shahin.s: Tanyus Shahin was a Maronite muleteer and blacksmith of Keserwan in Mount Lebanon who led the peasant revolt of 1858 to 1859 against the Khazen sheikhs. The rebels expelled the lords, seized their property and set up a peasant government under his leadership.

tsitsa-river.s: The Tsitsa is a river of the Eastern Cape in South Africa, a tributary of the Mzimvubu, known for the high Tsitsa Falls near Tsolo. Its valley was part of the heartland of the Mpondomise people before the colonial period.

tsolo.s: Tsolo is a small town in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa, near the Tsitsa River north of Mthatha. It lies in the former heartland of the Mpondomise kingdom and became a magistracy after Cape annexation.

tallapoosa-river.s: The Tallapoosa is a river of Georgia and Alabama in the United States, which joins the Coosa to form the Alabama River. Many of the Upper Towns of the Muscogee stood on its banks, and Andrew Jackson's defeat of the Red Sticks at Horseshoe Bend in 1814 took place in one of its…

tacfarinas.s: Tacfarinas was a Numidian of the Musulamii who had served in the Roman auxiliary army and from 17 CE led a revolt against Rome in North Africa. Using guerrilla tactics, he drew in the Gaetuli and Moorish groups and resisted several Roman commanders for seven years.

tebessa.s: Tébessa, the ancient Theveste, is a city in north-eastern Algeria near the Tunisian border. It was a town of the Musulamii and became the base of the Third Augustan legion in the 1st century CE before the legion moved to Lambaesis.

therapne.s: Therapne was an ancient site on the hills east of the Eurotas, opposite Sparta in Laconia. It held the Menelaion, a shrine where Menelaus and Helen were worshipped from the 8th century BCE.

treasury-of-minyas.s: The Treasury of Minyas is a Mycenaean tholos tomb at Orchomenos in Boeotia, Greece, named after the legendary king Minyas. Dating from the 13th century BCE, it is one of the largest tholos tombs in Greece, comparable to the Treasury of Atreus at Mycenae.

troad.s: The Troad is the historical name of the Biga Peninsula in north-western Anatolia, now in Turkey, bounded by the Dardanelles and the Aegean Sea. It was the land of Troy, and from the early first millennium BCE Aeolian Greek cities such as Mytilene founded settlements on its coast.

themistocles.s: Themistocles was an Athenian statesman and general who persuaded Athens to build a large fleet with the silver of Laurion. He led the Greek fleet to victory over the Persians at Salamis in 480 BCE and had the walls of Athens rebuilt.

treaty-of-deogaon.s: The Treaty of Deogaon was signed on 17 December 1803 between the British East India Company and Raghuji II Bhonsle of Nagpur after his defeats at Assaye and Argaon in the Second Anglo-Maratha War. Raghuji ceded Cuttack and the coast of Orissa and his lands in western Berar,…

tata-tonga.s: Tata-tonga was a Uyghur official who served as keeper of the seal to Tayang Khan of the Naimans in the early 13th century. Captured by Temüjin's forces around 1204, he entered Mongol service and, according to the Yuan dynastic history, taught the Mongol princes to write their…

taif.s: Taif is a city in the Hejaz mountains of western Saudi Arabia, south-east of Mecca, at an altitude of about 1,800 metres. In the time of Muhammad it was the home of the Thaqif tribe and resisted a Muslim siege in 630 before submitting.

taksin.s: Taksin was a Siamese general of Chinese descent who rallied resistance after the Burmese destroyed Ayutthaya in 1767 and was crowned king at Thonburi. In a series of campaigns he drove out the Burmese and reunified Siam, bringing rival regimes such as Phitsanulok, Phimai and…

taromai.s: Taromai was the last king of Nanzan, the southern of the three kingdoms that divided Okinawa Island in the 14th and early 15th centuries. In 1429 Shō Hashi, ruler of Chuzan, conquered Nanzan and defeated him, completing the unification of Okinawa as the Ryukyu Kingdom.

taihe-nanzhao.s: Taihe was the first capital of the kingdom of Nanzhao, built under Piluoge in the 730s on the western shore of Erhai Lake, south of modern Dali in Yunnan, China. It served as the royal seat until 779, when the capital moved to Yangjumie.

tarikh-i-sistan.s: The Tarikh-i Sistan is an anonymous Persian chronicle of the province of Sistan in eastern Iran and south-western Afghanistan, written in stages from the 11th to the 14th century. It traces the region's history from legendary times, including the hero Rustam, through the Arab…

tsemes-bay.s: Tsemes Bay is an inlet of the Black Sea on the coast of Krasnodar Krai in southern Russia, on which the port city of Novorossiysk stands. In the early 19th century its shores belonged to the Natukhaj Circassians, and the Ottomans held the fortress of Sudjuk-Kale there.

taormina.s: Taormina is a hilltop town on the east coast of Sicily, Italy, above the bay of Naxos and facing Mount Etna. Founded as Tauromenium in the 4th century BCE, with settlers including refugees from nearby Naxos, it prospered under Greek and Roman rule and is known for its ancient…

theocles.s: Theocles was the leader of the Greek colonists from Chalcis in Euboea who founded Naxos around 734 BCE, according to Thucydides the first Greek colony in Sicily. Thucydides also records that a few years later he led settlers from Naxos to found Leontini.

teumman.s: Teumman was king of Elam from about 664 to 653 BCE. Hostile to Assyria, he demanded the return of rival Elamite princes who had fled to Ashurbanipal's court and attacked Assyrian territory.

tsouharissen.s: Tsouharissen was the principal war chief of the Neutral Confederacy in present-day southern Ontario in the 1640s, known from the Jesuit Relations. He led large campaigns against Algonquian peoples to the west, including the Mascouten, and the missionaries described him as the…

trois-rivieres.s: Trois-Rivières is a city in Quebec, Canada, where the Saint-Maurice river meets the St Lawrence, halfway between Quebec City and Montreal. Founded in 1634 by Laviolette on Samuel de Champlain's orders, it was the second permanent French settlement on the St Lawrence and a…

tanna.s: Tanna is an island in the Tafea province of southern Vanuatu, known for the active volcano Mount Yasur. Captain James Cook landed there in 1774.

tinicum-island.s: Tinicum Island is an area on the Delaware River in Delaware County, Pennsylvania, south-west of Philadelphia. In 1643 Governor Johan Printz made it the seat of New Sweden, building Fort New Gothenburg and his residence, the Printzhof, there; it was the first permanent European…

thuan-hoa.s: Thuan Hoa was the name of a frontier region of central Vietnam, roughly the modern provinces of Quang Tri and Thua Thien Hue, formed from Cham territory ceded to Dai Viet in 1306. In 1558 Nguyen Hoang became its governor, and it became the base from which the Nguyen lords…

teutomatus.s: Teutomatus was a king of the Nitiobroges, a Gaulish people on the Garonne, and the son of Ollovico, a friend of the Roman people. In 52 BCE he joined Vercingetorix's revolt, bringing cavalry, including mercenaries raised in Aquitania.

tumkur.s: Tumkur, officially Tumakuru, is a city in southern Karnataka, India, about 70 km north-west of Bengaluru and the headquarters of Tumkur district. The surrounding area formed part of Nolambavadi, ruled by the Nolamba dynasty in the 9th and 10th centuries, and later came under…

the-troubles.s: The Troubles were the conflict in Northern Ireland from the late 1960s to 1998 between mainly Catholic nationalists and republicans seeking a united Ireland and mainly Protestant unionists and loyalists, with the British Army and police also involved. Beginning with clashes…

tiantishan-grottoes.s: The Tiantishan Grottoes are Buddhist cave temples near Wuwei in Gansu province, north-western China. They were begun in the early 5th century under the Northern Liang ruler Juqu Mengxun and are among the earliest Buddhist cave temples in China.

tumbuka-language.s: Tumbuka, or Chitumbuka, is a Bantu language spoken in northern Malawi and eastern Zambia. In the 19th century the Ngoni of Mbelwa, who had conquered the Tumbuka, gradually adopted it in place of their own Nguni language.

tamale.s: Tamale is the capital of the Northern Region of Ghana and the largest city of northern Ghana. It became the administrative centre of the British Northern Territories of the Gold Coast in 1907, replacing Gambaga, and grew as a market and route centre.

tumu-crisis.s: The Tumu Crisis was the defeat and capture of the Ming emperor Zhengtong by the Oirat Mongols under Esen at Tumu fortress, north-west of Beijing, in September 1449. The emperor had led a large army against the Oirat under the influence of the eunuch Wang Zhen, who was killed.

tsiomeko.s: Tsiomeko was a queen of the Sakalava kingdom of Boina in north-western Madagascar. Driven from the mainland by the expanding Merina kingdom, she and her followers took refuge on the island of Nosy Be, and in 1840 she accepted French protection, which led to France's annexation…

tepehuan-revolt.s: The Tepehuán Revolt was a rising of the Tepehuán people of Nueva Vizcaya, in northern Mexico, against Spanish rule that broke out in November 1616. Led by a prophet who promised to drive out the Spaniards, the rebels killed settlers and Jesuit and Franciscan missionaries and…

tampico.s: Tampico is a port city in the Mexican state of Tamaulipas, near the mouth of the Pánuco River on the Gulf of Mexico. Refounded in 1823, it was the scene in 1829 of Santa Anna's defeat of the Spanish expedition under Isidro Barradas, the last Spanish attempt to reconquer Mexico.

tsoede.s: Tsoede, also called Edegi, is the legendary founder of the Nupe Kingdom in the middle Niger valley of present-day Nigeria. Nupe tradition makes him a son of an Attah of Igala by a Nupe mother, who travelled up the Niger, united the Nupe chiefdoms in the early 16th century and…

teres-i.s: Teres I was the founder of the Odrysian kingdom of Thrace in the 5th century BCE. After the Persian withdrawal from Europe following 479 BCE he united Thracian tribes of the Hebrus valley under Odrysian rule, and Thucydides names him as the first to make the kingdom great.

thucydides.s: Thucydides was an Athenian general and historian, author of the History of the Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta. Exiled after failing to save Amphipolis in 424 BCE, he wrote a contemporary account of the war down to 411 BCE, based on his own observation and inquiry.

toluids.s: The Toluids were the descendants of Tolui, the youngest son of Genghis Khan. In 1251 the Toluid prince Möngke became Great Khan, displacing the line of Ögedei, and his brothers Kublai and Hulagu founded the Yuan dynasty in China and the Ilkhanate in Iran. Ögedeid resistance…

taejo-of-goguryeo.s: Taejo was the sixth king of Goguryeo, the ancient Korean kingdom, whose traditional reign of 53 to 146 CE is implausibly long. Under him Goguryeo became a more centralised kingdom, subjugated the Okjeo and Dongye peoples on the east coast and raided the Han Chinese…

teucer.s: Teucer is a hero of Greek mythology, son of Telamon of Salamis and half-brother of Ajax the Great, celebrated as an archer in the Iliad. Banished by his father after returning from Troy without Ajax, he was said to have founded the city of Salamis in Cyprus.

tagsatzung.s: The Tagsatzung, or Federal Diet, was the assembly of envoys of the cantons of the Old Swiss Confederacy and its successors until 1848. Delegates met in turn in various towns, bound by instructions from their cantons, and decisions needed the members' agreement, so its powers…

troy.s: Troy, known to the Greeks as Ilion, was an ancient city at Hisarlik in north-western Anatolia, near the entrance to the Dardanelles. Inhabited from about 3000 BCE into the Roman period, it is famous as the setting of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad, and its layers were…

tikamgarh.s: Tikamgarh is a town in the Bundelkhand region of Madhya Pradesh, India. Formerly called Tehri, it became the capital of the Bundela state of Orchha in 1783 and remained so until the state joined India after independence.

tabare-vazquez.s: Tabaré Vázquez was a Uruguayan oncologist and politician of the Broad Front, the first left-wing president of Uruguay. As mayor of Montevideo from 1990 to 1995 he built the coalition's base, and he served as president in 2005–2010 and 2015–2020.

tupamaros.s: The Tupamaros, formally the National Liberation Movement, were a Marxist urban guerrilla group in Uruguay active from the 1960s. Known for robberies, kidnappings and propaganda actions, they were crushed by the armed forces in 1972, shortly before the military seized power in…

teia.s: Teia was the last king of the Ostrogoths in Italy, elected after Totila's death at Taginae in 552. He gathered the remaining Gothic forces and marched south to protect the Gothic treasure at Cumae, but was trapped near Vesuvius by the Byzantine army of Narses.

totila.s: Totila, also called Baduila, was king of the Ostrogoths from 541 to 552. He revived the Gothic cause after Belisarius' first conquest, retaking most of Italy, capturing Rome twice and freeing slaves and tenants to join his army.

tensho-embassy.s: The Tenshō embassy was a mission of four young Japanese Christian nobles sent to Europe in the name of the Kyushu lords Ōtomo Sōrin, Ōmura Sumitada and Arima Harunobu. Organised by the Jesuit Alessandro Valignano, it left Nagasaki in 1582, was received by Philip II of Spain…

tuman-bay-ii.s: Tuman bay II was the last sultan of the Mamluk Sultanate, chosen in Cairo in 1516 after Sultan Qansuh al-Ghawri was killed at Marj Dabiq. He resisted the Ottoman invasion but was defeated at Ridaniya in January 1517 and fought on in guerrilla actions.

testour.s: Testour is a town in northern Tunisia on the Medjerda River, west of Tunis. It was founded in the early 17th century by Morisco refugees expelled from Spain, and its Great Mosque has a minaret in Aragonese Mudéjar style with a clock that runs backwards.

taj-ul-alam-safiatuddin-syah.s: Taj ul-Alam Safiatuddin Syah was sultana of Aceh from 1641 to 1675, the daughter of Iskandar Muda and widow of Iskandar Thani. The first of four women who ruled Aceh in succession until 1699, she governed with a council of nobles, patronised scholars and writers, and kept the…

teuku-umar.s: Teuku Umar was an Acehnese commander in the Aceh War against the Dutch. In 1893 he went over to the Dutch with his followers and received arms and money, then in 1896 returned to the resistance with the weapons, a deception that embarrassed the colonial government.

teungku-chik-di-tiro.s: Teungku Chik di Tiro, born Muhammad Saman, was an Acehnese religious scholar who led resistance to the Dutch in the Aceh War from the early 1880s. Proclaiming the struggle a holy war, he rallied village fighters and recovered much of the countryside, confining the Dutch to…

the-golden-ass.s: The Golden Ass, whose Latin title is Metamorphoses, is a novel by Apuleius written in the 2nd century CE in Roman North Africa. It tells how Lucius, turned into a donkey by a magic mishap, passes through many adventures before being restored by the goddess Isis.

thuburbo-maius.s: Thuburbo Maius was a Roman town in northern Tunisia, about 60 kilometres south-west of Carthage. Originally a Punic and Berber settlement, it became a municipium under Hadrian and a colony under Commodus.

talatal-ghar.s: The Talatal Ghar is a royal palace of the Ahom kingdom at Rangpur, near Sivasagar in Assam. Begun by Rudra Singha in the early eighteenth century and enlarged by later kings, notably Rajeswar Singha, it is the largest Ahom monument: a multi-storeyed brick building whose upper…

treaty-of-asurar-ali.s: The Treaty of Asurar Ali was a peace agreement concluded in 1639 between the Ahom kingdom of Assam and the Mughal Empire after more than twenty years of war over Kamrup. Negotiated by the Ahom official Momai Tamuli Borbarua and the Mughal commander Allah Yar Khan, it fixed the…

treaty-of-ghilajharighat.s: The Treaty of Ghilajharighat was signed in January 1663 between the Ahom king Jayadhwaj Singha and the Mughal governor of Bengal, Mir Jumla, after the Mughal occupation of the Ahom capital Garhgaon. The Ahoms ceded western territories including Guwahati, agreed to pay a heavy…

tristao-da-cunha.s: Tristão da Cunha was a Portuguese navigator and naval commander. In 1506 he led a large fleet to India, sighting on the way the South Atlantic islands later named Tristan da Cunha after him.

tashfin-ibn-ali.s: Tashfin ibn Ali was emir of the Almoravid Empire from 1143 to 1145, son of Ali ibn Yusuf. Earlier governor in al-Andalus, where he campaigned against the Christian kingdoms, he came to the throne as the Almohads under Abd al-Mu'min were overrunning Morocco.

theodora-megale-komnene.s: Despina Khatun was the name borne by Theodora Komnene, daughter of Emperor John IV of Trebizond, who married the Aq Qoyunlu ruler Uzun Hasan around 1458 as part of an alliance against the Ottoman Empire. She kept her Orthodox Christian faith at his court, and her family ties…

tur-ali-beg.s: Tur Ali Beg was an early leader of the Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen tribes of the Bayandur clan, who pastured around Diyarbakır and the upper Tigris in the first half of the fourteenth century. He led raids on the Empire of Trebizond in the 1340s, and his son Qutlu Beg later turned this…

tehuelche.s: The Tehuelche are indigenous peoples of Patagonia in southern Argentina and Chile, traditionally hunters of guanaco and rhea who adopted the horse in the eighteenth century. Their lands were overrun by the Argentine army during the Conquest of the Desert in the 1870s and…

treaty-of-asuncion.s: The Treaty of Asunción was signed on 26 March 1991 by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay in the Paraguayan capital. It created Mercosur, the Southern Common Market, committing the four states to free movement of goods and a common external tariff, and it built on earlier…

treaty-of-the-triple-alliance.s: The Treaty of the Triple Alliance was signed in secret on 1 May 1865 in Buenos Aires by Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay after Paraguay invaded Argentine territory. The allies pledged to fight until the regime of Francisco Solano López was removed and set out the territory…

thirty-tyrants.s: The Thirty Tyrants were the oligarchy of thirty men installed in Athens with Spartan backing after its defeat in the Peloponnesian War in 404 BCE. Led by Critias, they executed some 1,500 people and seized property, until democratic exiles under Thrasybulus defeated them at…

tyrol.s: Tyrol is a historical region in the eastern Alps, centred on the valleys of the Inn, Adige and Eisack and the Brenner Pass. A Habsburg land from 1363, it was ceded to Bavaria by the Peace of Pressburg in 1805, provoking Andreas Hofer's rising of 1809, and was returned to…

treaty-of-accession-1972.s: The Treaty of Accession 1972 was the agreement signed in Brussels on 22 January 1972 under which the United Kingdom, Ireland and Denmark joined the European Economic Community on 1 January 1973. Norway also signed but did not join after a referendum.

toka-leya.s: The Toka-Leya are a Bantu people of southern Zambia living around Livingstone and the Victoria Falls, made up of the closely related Toka and Leya. In the nineteenth century they paid tribute to the Lozi kingdom of Barotseland.

tanda-bengal.s: Tanda was a city on the Ganges in Bengal, near Gaur in present-day Malda district, West Bengal. Sulaiman Khan Karrani made it the capital of the Bengal Sultanate in the 1560s, and it remained the seat of Mughal Bengal until Rajmahal replaced it in 1595.

taj-bawdi.s: The Taj Bawdi is a large stepwell in Bijapur, built around 1620 by Malik Sandal in honour of Taj Sultana, queen of Ibrahim Adil Shah II. Entered through a great arched gateway flanked by octagonal towers, its deep tank stored water for the city's population.

tolmides.s: Tolmides was an Athenian general of the mid-fifth century BCE. Around 456–455 BCE he led a naval expedition around the Peloponnese, burning the Spartan dockyards at Gytheion, and he settled Athenian colonists in several places.

trophonius.s: Trophonius was a Greek hero worshipped at Lebadea in Boeotia, where his underground oracle was one of the most famous in Greece. According to legend he and his brother Agamedes built the temple of Apollo at Delphi.

tauri.s: The Tauri were an ancient people of the mountainous southern coast of Crimea, which the Greeks called Taurica after them. Greek writers described them as pirates who sacrificed shipwrecked strangers to a maiden goddess, the setting of the myth of Iphigenia among the Taurians.

tajarib-al-umam.s: Tajarib al-umam, 'Experiences of the Nations', is a universal history written in Arabic by the Persian scholar Miskawayh, who served as librarian to Buyid rulers and viziers. Running from the Flood to 980, it is especially valuable as an eyewitness source for the Buyid period.

temple-of-the-obelisks.s: The Temple of the Obelisks is a Middle Bronze Age sanctuary at Byblos in Lebanon, named after the many standing stones erected in its courtyard. Hundreds of offerings were found buried there, including bronze figurines of gods, some covered in gold leaf, weapons and jewellery.

topkapi-palace.s: Topkapı Palace in Istanbul was the main residence and administrative centre of the Ottoman sultans for about four centuries. Begun by Mehmed II after the conquest of Constantinople, it occupies the tip of the historic peninsula, on the site of the acropolis of ancient Byzantium.

toda-of-pamplona.s: Toda of Pamplona was queen consort of Sancho I Garcés of Pamplona and regent for their son García Sánchez I. Through her network of marriages she was linked to most of the royal houses of Christian Spain, and she was aunt of the caliph Abd al-Rahman III.

treaty-of-washington-1871.s: The Treaty of Washington of 1871 settled disputes between Britain and the United States after the American Civil War. It referred the Alabama claims over Confederate raiders built in Britain to an international tribunal at Geneva, opened fisheries and navigation rights and…

toggenburg-war.s: The Second War of Villmergen was a religious war of 1712 in the Old Swiss Confederacy, arising from a dispute in the Toggenburg between its Protestant subjects and the Prince-Abbot of St. Gallen. Zürich and Bern defeated the Catholic cantons at Villmergen on 25 July 1712, and…

treaty-of-aarau-1712.s: The Treaty of Aarau, concluded in August 1712, ended the Second War of Villmergen between the Protestant cantons of Zürich and Bern and the Catholic cantons. It gave Zürich and Bern control of the common lordships in the Aargau and the leading role in governing the others,…

tabula-contrebiensis.s: The Tabula Contrebiensis is a bronze tablet of 87 BCE found in 1979 at Botorrita, the ancient Contrebia Belaisca, near Zaragoza. Written in Latin, it records a dispute between two neighbouring communities over land and a water channel, decided by the senate of Contrebia under…

titus-didius.s: Titus Didius was a Roman general, consul in 98 BCE and then governor of Hispania Citerior, where he campaigned against the Celtiberians for several years. He forced the people of Termes to leave their hilltop for an unfortified site and celebrated a triumph in 93 BCE.

turiaso.s: Turiaso was a Celtiberian and later Roman town on the site of modern Tarazona in the province of Zaragoza, Spain, at the foot of the Moncayo range. It minted coins in the Celtiberian period and became a Roman municipium under Augustus.

theopompus.s: Theopompus of Chios was a Greek historian and rhetorician, said to have studied under Isocrates. He wrote the Hellenica, continuing Thucydides from 411 to 394 BCE, and the Philippica, a vast history centred on Philip II of Macedon with many digressions.

temryuk-idarov.s: Temryuk Idarov was the leading prince of Kabarda in the mid-sixteenth century. Facing the Crimean Khanate and rival princes, he sought an alliance with Muscovy, sending envoys to Ivan IV in 1557, and in 1561 his daughter Maria married the tsar.

tenterfield-oration.s: The Tenterfield Oration was a speech given on 24 October 1889 at the School of Arts in Tenterfield, New South Wales, by the colony's premier Sir Henry Parkes. Citing a report on colonial defence, he called for the federation of the Australian colonies under one government and…
