tobruk.s: Tobruk is a port city in Cyrenaica in eastern Libya. In the Second World War its harbour made it a key objective in the North African campaign: an Allied garrison, largely the Australian 9th Division, held it against German and Italian forces under Rommel through the siege of…

torres-strait-islanders.s: Torres Strait Islanders are the Indigenous Melanesian peoples of the islands of the Torres Strait between Cape York in Queensland and New Guinea, with cultures distinct from those of Aboriginal Australians. Annexed to Queensland in the 1870s, the islands are part of Australia.

tetela-people.s: The Tetela are a Bantu people of the Sankuru and Maniema regions of the central Democratic Republic of the Congo. Many served as soldiers in the Force Publique of the Congo Free State, and Tetela troops mutinied in 1895 at Luluabourg and in 1897 during Francis Dhanis's…

the-crime-of-the-congo.s: The Crime of the Congo is a book of 1909 by Arthur Conan Doyle, written in support of the Congo Reform Association. Drawing on reports by Roger Casement, missionaries and the Belgian commission of inquiry, it set out the evidence of forced labour, killing and mutilation in the…

tervuren.s: Tervuren is a town in Flemish Brabant, Belgium, east of Brussels. The colonial section of the Brussels International Exposition of 1897 was held there, and it became the home of the Royal Museum for Central Africa, opened in its present building in 1910 and funded in part from…

treaty-of-madrid-1526.s: The Treaty of Madrid was signed on 14 January 1526 by Francis I of France, then a prisoner of Emperor Charles V after his defeat at Pavia. Francis renounced his claims in Italy and his suzerainty over Flanders and Artois, ceded Burgundy and sent his two sons to Spain as hostages.

thierry-of-alsace.s: Thierry of Alsace was count of Flanders from 1128 to 1168. A grandson of Count Robert I through his mother, he was backed by the Flemish towns against William Clito after the murder of Charles the Good and became count when Clito died in 1128.

treaty-of-athis-sur-orge.s: The Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge was concluded in June 1305 between Philip IV of France and Flanders after the French victory at Mons-en-Pévèle. It restored Count Robert of Béthune but imposed a heavy indemnity, acts of penance and the demolition of town fortifications.

treaty-of-rastatt.s: The Treaty of Rastatt was signed on 7 March 1714 by France and Emperor Charles VI, ending their war in the War of the Spanish Succession; the Empire as a whole made peace at Baden later that year. Completing the Utrecht settlement, it gave Austria the Spanish Netherlands,…

treaty-of-delft.s: The Treaty of Delft, concluded on 3 July 1428, ended the main phase of the war between Jacqueline of Bavaria and Philip the Good, duke of Burgundy, over Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland. Jacqueline kept her titles, but Philip became her heir and governor, and she promised not to…

treaty-of-the-pyrenees.s: The Treaty of the Pyrenees was signed on 7 November 1659 on Pheasant Island in the Bidasoa river, ending the Franco-Spanish War that had begun in 1635. Spain ceded Roussillon and northern Cerdanya, Artois and a string of towns in Flanders, Hainaut and Luxembourg to France, and…

treaty-of-lorris.s: The Treaty of Lorris was concluded in January 1243 between Louis IX of France and Raymond VII of Toulouse after the failure of Raymond's revolt in alliance with Henry III of England and the Lusignans. Raymond submitted to the king and confirmed the terms of the Treaty of Paris…

the-fountain-of-bakhchisaray.s: The Fountain of Bakhchisaray is a narrative poem by Alexander Pushkin, written in 1821–1823 and published in 1824. Inspired by his visit to the Khan's Palace at Bakhchysarai and its fountain, it tells of the khan Giray, his jealous wife Zarema and the captive Polish princess…

treaty-of-constantinople-1700.s: The Treaty of Constantinople of July 1700 ended the war of 1686–1700 between Russia and the Ottoman Empire. Russia kept Azov, taken by Peter the Great in 1696, and Muscovy was released from paying the annual 'gifts' to the Crimean khans.

treaty-of-constantinople-1832.s: The Treaty of Constantinople was signed in July 1832 by Britain, France, Russia and the Ottoman Empire, completing the recognition of the independent Kingdom of Greece. It fixed Greece's northern frontier on a line from the Gulf of Arta to the Gulf of Volos, and the Ottomans…

tuqa-timur.s: Tuqa-Timur was a son of Jochi, eldest son of Genghis Khan, who received lands in the western part of the Mongol steppe in the thirteenth century. Several later Chinggisid dynasties claimed descent from him, among them the Giray khans of Crimea, the khans of Kazan and…

treaty-of-almizra.s: The Treaty of Almizra was agreed in 1244 between James I of Aragon and the Castilian heir Alfonso, the future Alfonso X. It fixed the frontier between their conquests in the south-east of the Iberian peninsula, leaving the Kingdom of Valencia to Aragon and Murcia to Castile,…

teresa-of-avila.s: Teresa of Ávila was a Spanish Carmelite nun and mystic who reformed her order, founding the Discalced Carmelites with John of the Cross from 1562. Her writings, including her Life and The Interior Castle, are classics of Spanish prose and Christian mysticism.

treaty-of-benavente.s: The Treaty of Benavente of 1230 settled the succession of the Kingdom of León after the death of Alfonso IX. His daughters Sancha and Dulce renounced their claims in favour of their half-brother Ferdinand III of Castile in return for pensions.

treaty-of-alcacovas.s: The Treaty of Alcáçovas, signed on 4 September 1479, ended the War of the Castilian Succession between Castile and Portugal. Afonso V of Portugal gave up his claim and that of Joanna la Beltraneja, recognising Isabella I as queen of Castile.

tomas-bata.s: Tomáš Baťa was a Czech industrialist who founded the Bata shoe company in Zlín in 1894. Using mass production methods, he made it one of the largest shoe makers in the world, with factories and company towns abroad, and he rebuilt Zlín as a modern industrial town.

taj-al-din-yildiz.s: Taj al-Din Yildiz was a Turkic slave commander of the Ghurid sultan Muhammad of Ghor who seized Ghazni after his master's death in 1206. Driven out by the Khwarazmians, he invaded northern India to claim the Ghurid lands there, but was defeated by Iltutmish at Tarain in 1216…

themis.s: Themis was the Greek goddess of divine law, order and custom, a Titan and daughter of Gaia and Uranus. By Zeus she was mother of the Horai and, in some accounts, the Fates.

treaty-of-knared.s: The Treaty of Knäred, signed on 20 January 1613, ended the Kalmar War between Denmark-Norway and Sweden. Sweden gave up its claims in the far north of Norway and agreed to pay a ransom of one million riksdaler for the return of Älvsborg, its only port on the North Sea, which…

treaty-of-lubeck.s: The Treaty of Lübeck of 1629 ended Christian IV of Denmark's intervention in the Thirty Years' War. Defeated by the imperial armies of Tilly and Wallenstein, which had occupied Jutland, Christian recovered his lands without paying an indemnity but promised to stay out of the…

treaty-of-kiel.s: The Treaty of Kiel was signed on 14 January 1814 by Frederick VI of Denmark-Norway, defeated as an ally of Napoleon, with Sweden and Britain. Denmark ceded Norway to the king of Sweden but kept Iceland, the Faroe Islands and Greenland, receiving Swedish Pomerania in return.

treaty-of-frederiksborg.s: The Treaty of Frederiksborg, signed in 1720, ended the Great Northern War between Denmark-Norway and Sweden. Denmark returned its conquests in Swedish Pomerania, while Sweden paid an indemnity, gave up its exemption from the Sound Toll and stopped supporting the Duke of…

tarut-island.s: Tarut Island lies in the Persian Gulf off Qatif in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia. Occupied since prehistoric times, it has yielded finds of the third millennium BCE linked to Dilmun and Mesopotamia, including stone vessels and statues, and it was probably part of the…

tassilo-i-of-bavaria.s: Tassilo I was duke of Bavaria from about 591 to about 610, installed by the Frankish king Childebert II. A member of the Agilolfing family and probably the brother of the Lombard queen Theodelinda, he fought the Slavs and Avars on the eastern frontier of the duchy in the Alps.

tegernsee-abbey.s: Tegernsee Abbey was a Benedictine monastery on the Tegernsee lake in Upper Bavaria, founded in the mid-eighth century by members of a leading Bavarian noble family. It became one of the richest and most learned abbeys of Bavaria, with a celebrated scriptorium, and the early…

tienen.s: Tienen is a town in Flemish Brabant, Belgium, east of Leuven. In the Middle Ages it was one of the cloth-making towns of the Duchy of Brabant, and since the nineteenth century it has been known as the centre of the Belgian sugar-beet industry.

treaty-of-le-verger.s: The Treaty of Le Verger, also called the Treaty of Sablé, was signed in August 1488 between Charles VIII of France and Duke Francis II of Brittany after the Breton defeat at Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier. Francis had to dismiss his foreign troops, hand over several towns as pledges…

treguier.s: Tréguier is a small town in the Côtes-d'Armor department of northern Brittany, where the Jaudy and Guindy rivers meet. It was a bishop's seat from the early Middle Ages until 1790, and its Gothic cathedral holds the tomb of Saint Yves, who was born nearby.

the-miseries-and-misfortunes-of-war.n: The Miseries and Misfortunes of War
the-miseries-and-misfortunes-of-war.s: The Miseries and Misfortunes of War is a series of eighteen etchings by Jacques Callot, published in Paris in 1633. It shows soldiers of the Thirty Years' War plundering, burning and killing civilians, and then being punished by hanging and other executions.

treaty-of-nuremberg-1542.s: The Treaty of Nuremberg, concluded in August 1542 between Duke Antoine of Lorraine and Emperor Charles V, defined the duchy's relationship with the Holy Roman Empire. It recognised Lorraine as a free and non-incorporable duchy, owing only limited contributions to the Empire…

treaty-of-vincennes-1661.s: The Treaty of Vincennes, signed in February 1661 between Louis XIV of France and Duke Charles IV of Lorraine, returned to Charles the duchy that France had occupied for most of the period since 1633. Its terms were harsh: the fortifications of Nancy were to be demolished and…

treaty-of-aix-la-chapelle-1748.s: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, signed in October 1748, ended the War of the Austrian Succession. Most conquests were returned: France gave back the Austrian Netherlands and Britain returned Louisbourg, while Maria Theresa's succession was recognised but Prussia kept Silesia.

transpadane-republic.s: The Transpadane Republic was a sister republic of revolutionary France set up in Lombardy, north of the Po, after Napoleon Bonaparte conquered the Austrian Duchy of Milan in 1796. With Milan as its capital, its new institutions replaced the old Austrian administration.

tortona.s: Tortona is a town on the Scrivia in Piedmont, north-western Italy, the Roman Dertona. Frederick Barbarossa destroyed it in 1155 after a siege.

teatro-regio-parma.s: The Teatro Regio is an opera house in Parma built for Duchess Marie Louise by the architect Nicola Bettoli and opened in 1829 with an opera by Vincenzo Bellini. Known for its demanding audiences, it is closely associated with the music of Giuseppe Verdi and hosts the annual…

trebbia.s: The Trebbia is a river of northern Italy, about 120 km long, that rises in the Ligurian Apennines and flows north to join the Po near Piacenza. Hannibal defeated the Romans on its banks in 218 BCE, and in June 1799 a Russian and Austrian army under Alexander Suvorov defeated…

treaty-of-landin.s: The Treaty of Landin was concluded in 1250 between Barnim I, duke of Pomerania, and the margraves of Brandenburg, John I and Otto III. By it Barnim ceded the Uckermark, a region north of Berlin long contested between the two powers, to Brandenburg.

treaty-of-pyritz.s: The Treaty of Pyritz, concluded in 1493 at Pyrzyce, settled the long dispute between the Duchy of Pomerania under Bogislaw X and the Margraviate of Brandenburg over Brandenburg's claim to overlordship. Brandenburg gave up the claim in return for the right to inherit Pomerania…

treaty-of-stettin-1570.s: The Treaty of Stettin, signed on 13 December 1570, ended the Northern Seven Years' War between Sweden and Denmark-Norway, allied with Lübeck. Neither side made lasting territorial gains: Denmark gave up its claims to Sweden, Sweden renounced its claims to Norway and other…

treaty-of-stettin-1653.s: The Treaty of Stettin of May 1653 between Sweden and Brandenburg fixed the border in Pomerania after the Peace of Westphalia had divided the former duchy. Sweden kept Western Pomerania with Stettin and the mouth of the Oder, while Brandenburg finally took over Farther…

trzebiatow.s: Trzebiatów, German Treptow an der Rega, is a town on the Rega in the West Pomeranian Voivodeship of north-western Poland. In December 1534 a diet of the Pomeranian estates held there adopted the Lutheran Reformation, and Johannes Bugenhagen, formerly rector of the town's…

treaty-of-nonsuch.s: The Treaty of Nonsuch was signed on 10 August 1585 at Nonsuch Palace in Surrey between Elizabeth I of England and the Dutch rebels. Elizabeth agreed to send several thousand soldiers under the Earl of Leicester and received the towns of Brielle and Flushing as security for her…

triple-alliance-1668.s: The Triple Alliance of 1668 was a league of England, the Dutch Republic and Sweden, formed in January 1668 to halt Louis XIV's conquests in the Spanish Netherlands during the War of Devolution. Negotiated by Sir William Temple and Johan de Witt, it pushed France to accept the…

triple-alliance-1882.s: The Triple Alliance was a secret defensive alliance between Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy, concluded on 20 May 1882 and renewed several times. Italy joined after France seized Tunisia in 1881, ending its diplomatic isolation.

tobolsk.s: Tobolsk is a city in western Siberia, Russia, at the confluence of the Tobol and Irtysh rivers. Founded by Cossacks in 1587, soon after Yermak's campaign against the Khanate of Sibir, it was the administrative capital of Siberia in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries and…

tsering-dondub.s: Tsering Dondub was a Dzungar commander under Tsewang Rabtan. In 1717 he led an army across the Tibetan plateau, killed the Khoshut ruler Lha-bzang Khan and sacked Lhasa, and in 1718 his forces destroyed a Qing relief army near the Salween River.

tsewang-dorji-namjal.s: Tsewang Dorji Namjal was khan of the Dzungars from 1745 to 1750, succeeding his father Galdan Tseren while still a youth. His erratic rule alienated the nobility, and in 1750 he was overthrown and blinded by his half-brother Lama Dorji.

treaty-of-pavia-1329.s: The Treaty of Pavia of 4 August 1329 divided the lands of the house of Wittelsbach. Emperor Louis IV the Bavarian kept Upper Bavaria, while the Rhenish Palatinate and the Upper Palatinate went to his nephews Rudolf II and Rupert I, sons of his brother Rudolf I.

treaty-of-dresden-1745.s: The Peace of Dresden, signed on 25 December 1745 after the Prussian victory at Kesselsdorf, ended the Second Silesian War between Prussia on one side and Austria and Saxony on the other. Austria confirmed Prussia's possession of Silesia, Frederick II recognised Francis I as…

treaty-of-posen.s: The Treaty of Posen, signed on 11 December 1806 at Posen (Poznań), made peace between Napoleon and Elector Frederick Augustus III of Saxony, who had fought on the Prussian side at Jena. Saxony joined the Confederation of the Rhine, its ruler took the title of king as Frederick…

treaty-of-altranstadt-1706.s: The Treaty of Altranstädt of 24 September 1706, made near Leipzig during the Great Northern War, ended Saxon participation in the war after Charles XII of Sweden invaded Saxony. Augustus the Strong renounced the Polish crown in favour of Stanisław Leszczyński, broke his…

theophilos-emperor.s: Theophilos was Byzantine emperor from 829 to 842, of the Amorian dynasty, and the last emperor to support iconoclasm. He fought the Abbasids, who sacked Amorion in 838, and sought allies against them, exchanging embassies with the Umayyad emir Abd al-Rahman II of Córdoba.

tarifa.s: Tarifa is a town at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula in the province of Cádiz, Spain, facing Morocco across the Strait of Gibraltar. Named after the Berber commander Tarif ibn Malik, who landed there in 710, it was captured by Sancho IV of Castile in 1292 and famously…

treaty-of-granada-1491.s: The Treaty of Granada, signed on 25 November 1491, set the terms for the surrender of the Emirate of Granada by Muhammad XII (Boabdil) to Ferdinand and Isabella. The city was handed over on 2 January 1492, ending Muslim rule in the Iberian Peninsula.

tales-of-the-alhambra.s: Tales of the Alhambra is a collection of essays, sketches and legends by the American writer Washington Irving, published in 1832 after he had lived in the Alhambra palace in Granada in 1829. Mixing descriptions of the palace and its inhabitants with Moorish legends, it made…

tomioka-silk-mill.s: The Tomioka Silk Mill in Gunma Prefecture, Japan, was a model factory founded by the Meiji government in 1872 with French machinery and engineers, led by Paul Brunat, to modernise silk reeling. It trained women workers from across Japan, who spread the new methods to other mills.

third-syrian-war.s: The Third Syrian War (246–241 BCE), also called the Laodicean War, was fought between Ptolemy III of Egypt and the Seleucid king Seleucus II. Ptolemy invaded the Seleucid empire to support his sister Berenice, widow of Antiochus II, who was murdered with her son.

tangra.s: Tangra was the supreme sky god of the early Bulgars, a form of the god Tengri worshipped by many Turkic and Mongol peoples of the Eurasian steppe. Bulgar khans invoked him in inscriptions as the source of their rule.

tervel.s: Tervel was khan of Bulgaria from about 700 to about 721, the son and successor of Asparuh. In 705 he helped the deposed emperor Justinian II regain the Byzantine throne, receiving the title of caesar and a territory south of the Balkan mountains.

treaty-of-gottorp.s: The Treaty of Gottorp, concluded in 1768, settled Hamburg's long dispute with Denmark, whose kings as dukes of Holstein had claimed sovereignty over the city. Denmark recognised Hamburg as a free imperial city in return for financial concessions by the city.

town-musicians-of-bremen.s: The Town Musicians of Bremen is a German folk tale published by the Brothers Grimm in 1819. It tells of a donkey, a dog, a cat and a rooster who, too old to be useful to their masters, set out for Bremen to become musicians and on the way drive robbers from a house.

the-battle-of-algiers-film.s: The Battle of Algiers is a 1966 film directed by Gillo Pontecorvo, recreating the struggle between the FLN and French paratroopers in Algiers in 1956–1957. Shot in black and white in the Casbah with mostly non-professional actors, it won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film…

the-wretched-of-the-earth.s: The Wretched of the Earth is a book by the Martinique-born psychiatrist and writer Frantz Fanon, published in French in 1961 shortly before his death, with a preface by Jean-Paul Sartre. Drawing on the Algerian War of Independence, in which Fanon supported the National…

trans-indochinese-railway.s: The Trans-Indochinese Railway is the metre-gauge line of about 1,700 kilometres running along the coast of Vietnam between Hanoi and Saigon, now Ho Chi Minh City. Begun under Governor-General Paul Doumer in the 1890s and built in sections, it was completed in 1936.

thiaroye-massacre.s: The Thiaroye massacre took place on 1 December 1944 at the Thiaroye military camp near Dakar, when French troops fired on West African tirailleurs, recently released prisoners of war returned from France, who were protesting over unpaid wages and allowances. The official toll…

thies.s: Thiès is a city in western Senegal, about seventy kilometres east of Dakar and one of the country's largest cities. It grew as a junction of the Dakar–Saint-Louis railway and the Dakar–Niger line, with major railway workshops, and was the centre of the great railway strike of…

tabaqat-wad-dayfallah.s: The Tabaqat of Wad Dayfallah is a biographical dictionary of the Muslim holy men, scholars and poets of the Funj Sultanate, compiled by Muhammad al-Nur ibn Dayfallah and completed in the early nineteenth century. Its more than 250 biographies are the chief source for the…

thyssen.s: Thyssen was a German steel and industrial company founded in 1871 by August Thyssen at Mülheim in the Ruhr. It grew into one of the largest integrated coal, iron and steel concerns in Germany before the First World War, rivalling Krupp.

treaty-of-frankfurt-1871.s: The Treaty of Frankfurt, signed on 10 May 1871, ended the Franco-Prussian War. France ceded Alsace and most of Lorraine to the new German Empire and agreed to pay an indemnity of five billion francs, with German troops occupying part of France until it was paid.

turnip-winter.s: The Turnip Winter was the severe food crisis in Germany in the winter of 1916–1917, during the First World War, when a failed potato harvest and the British naval blockade left many civilians depending on turnips, normally used as animal fodder. Hunger, disease and…

tarikh-al-hind.s: The Tarikh al-Hind, also known as Al-Biruni's India, is a study of Indian religion, philosophy, literature, astronomy, geography and customs written in Arabic by the scholar al-Biruni around 1030, while he served the Ghaznavid court. Based on Sanskrit sources and conversations…

taehak.s: The Taehak was the national Confucian academy of the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo, founded in 372 under King Sosurim. It taught the Chinese classics and history to the sons of the aristocracy and is regarded as the first formal educational institution in Korea.

taspar-qaghan.s: Taspar Qaghan was ruler of the First Turkic Khaganate from 572 to 581, a son of the founder Bumin and successor of his brother Muqan. He extracted large tributes of silk from the rival Northern Zhou and Northern Qi dynasties of China, whose rulers he reportedly called his two…

tana-azov.s: Tana was an Italian trading colony at the mouth of the Don, on the site of modern Azov in southern Russia. Under licence from the khans of the Golden Horde, Venetian and Genoese merchants traded there from the 1330s in grain, furs, fish, slaves and goods from Central Asia.

tokhta.s: Tokhta was khan of the Golden Horde from 1291 to 1312, a son of Mengu-Timur. He came to power with the support of the general Nogai, who had dominated the western steppe, but turned against him and defeated and killed him around 1299-1300, restoring the unity of the khanate.

technical-university-of-darmstadt.s: The Technical University of Darmstadt is a German university of technology in Darmstadt, Hesse. It grew from a higher trade school founded in 1836 and became a technical university in 1877.

time-of-troubles.s: The Time of Troubles was a period of political crisis, famine, civil war and foreign intervention in Russia between the end of the Rurik dynasty in 1598 and the election of Michael Romanov as tsar in 1613. Pretenders claiming to be Ivan IV's dead son Dmitry won wide support,…

traidenis.s: Traidenis was grand duke of Lithuania from about 1269 to 1282, a pagan ruler who restored the power of the state after the turmoil following the death of Mindaugas. He fought the Livonian Order and the princes of Galicia-Volhynia, and supported the Semigallians and Prussians…

treaty-of-london-1867.s: The Treaty of London of 11 May 1867 settled the Luxembourg Crisis between France and Prussia. Signed by the great powers, it declared the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg perpetually neutral under their collective guarantee, confirmed its union with the House of Orange-Nassau,…

treaty-of-london-1915.s: The Treaty of London was a secret agreement signed on 26 April 1915 by Italy, Britain, France and Russia. Italy left the Triple Alliance and promised to enter the First World War on the Entente side within a month, in return for Trentino, South Tyrol, Trieste, Istria, part of…

theognostus-metropolitan-of-kiev.s: Theognostus was a Greek churchman appointed by Constantinople as Metropolitan of Kiev and All Rus', an office he held from 1328 until his death in 1353. Succeeding Peter, he made Moscow his permanent residence, cooperated closely with Ivan I and his son Simeon, and secured the…

third-rome.s: The Third Rome is the idea that Moscow succeeded Rome and Constantinople as the centre of true Christianity and the last Christian empire. It was formulated in the early sixteenth century in letters of the monk Philotheus of Pskov, against the background of the fall of…

trinity-lavra-of-st-sergius.s: The Trinity Lavra of St. Sergius is the most important monastery of the Russian Orthodox Church, at Sergiyev Posad north-east of Moscow. Founded by Sergius of Radonezh around the 1340s, it became a great landowner and a centre of learning and art, for which Andrei Rublev…

treaty-of-vienna-1738.s: The Treaty of Vienna of 1738 ended the War of the Polish Succession. Augustus III was recognised as king of Poland, while his rival Stanisław Leszczyński received the Duchy of Lorraine, to pass to France after his death.

treaty-of-belgrade.s: The Treaty of Belgrade, signed in September 1739, ended the war of 1735–1739 in which Austria and Russia fought the Ottoman Empire. After a badly managed campaign, Austria returned Belgrade, northern Serbia and Oltenia, which it had gained at Passarowitz in 1718.

treaty-of-hubertusburg.s: The Treaty of Hubertusburg was signed on 15 February 1763 at a Saxon hunting lodge by Prussia, Austria and Saxony, ending the Seven Years' War in Central Europe. It restored the pre-war borders, leaving Silesia with Prussia, while Frederick II promised his vote to Maria…

the-last-judgment-memling.s: The Last Judgment is a triptych painted by Hans Memling in Bruges for Angelo Tani, an agent of the Medici bank. In 1473, on its way to Florence, the ship carrying it was captured by the Danzig privateer Paul Beneke, and the altarpiece was given to St Mary's Church in Danzig.

treaty-of-copenhagen-1441.s: The Treaty of Copenhagen of 1441 ended the naval war of 1438–1441 between the Wendish towns of the Hanseatic League, led by Lübeck, and Holland and Zeeland. It confirmed Dutch access to the Baltic trade, a turning point in the rise of Dutch shipping at the expense of the Hansa.

treaty-of-vordingborg.s: The Treaty of Vordingborg of 1435 ended the war between Eric of Pomerania, king of the Kalmar Union, and the Wendish towns of the Hanseatic League that had begun in 1426. The towns kept their trading privileges in Denmark and their exemption from the Sound Dues, and the costly…

tubba.s: Tubba' was the name by which Arab and Islamic tradition remembered the kings of Himyar in ancient Yemen. The Qur'an mentions the people of Tubba' as a people destroyed for their sins, and later legend made the Tubba' kings great conquerors who campaigned as far as Persia and…

tarazona.s: Tarazona is a town in the province of Zaragoza in Aragon, Spain, near the Moncayo massif, known in Roman times as Turiaso. It was an episcopal see from late antiquity, taken from the Muslims by Alfonso I of Aragon in 1119.

theodoric-ii.s: Theodoric II was king of the Visigoths from 453 to 466, having taken power by killing his brother Thorismund. An ally of Rome, he backed the elevation of Avitus as emperor in 455 and in 456 destroyed the Suebic army near Astorga, later executing its king Rechiar.

tower-of-hercules.s: The Tower of Hercules is a Roman lighthouse at A Coruña in Galicia, north-western Spain, built in the late 1st or early 2nd century CE. Restored in the 1790s, it is the oldest Roman lighthouse still in use.

theogony.s: The Theogony is a Greek poem by Hesiod, composed around 700 BCE, that tells the origin and genealogy of the gods. Its central story, in which Ouranos is overthrown by Kronos and Kronos by Zeus, closely parallels the Hurro-Hittite Kumarbi cycle, a sign that Near Eastern myths…

talakad.s: Talakad is a town on the Kaveri river in Mysore district, Karnataka, once the capital of the Western Ganga dynasty. The Cholas took it around 1004, and its capture by the Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana in 1116 drove them from southern Karnataka; he took the title Talakadugonda,…

tupac-amaru-ii.s: Túpac Amaru II, born José Gabriel Condorcanqui, was a kuraka of the Cusco region who claimed descent from the last Inca ruler, Túpac Amaru. In November 1780 he led a great rebellion against Spanish colonial abuses that spread across the southern Andes.

tuscarora-people.s: The Tuscarora are an Iroquoian people originally from the coastal plain of North Carolina. After their defeat by colonists in the Tuscarora War of 1711–1713, most moved north and around 1722 were adopted into the Iroquois Confederacy under Oneida sponsorship, which then became…

treaty-of-canandaigua.s: The Treaty of Canandaigua was signed on 11 November 1794 at Canandaigua, New York, between the United States, represented by Timothy Pickering, and the Six Nations of the Iroquois. It established peace and friendship, recognised the lands of the Seneca and other nations in New…

treaty-of-fort-stanwix-1784.s: The Treaty of Fort Stanwix of 1784 was signed on 22 October 1784 at Fort Stanwix, New York, between the United States and representatives of the Six Nations after the American Revolution. American commissioners, holding hostages, forced the Iroquois to give up claims to lands…

treaty-of-paris-1229.s: The Treaty of Paris of April 1229, also called the Treaty of Meaux-Paris, ended the Albigensian Crusade. Count Raymond VII of Toulouse did public penance in Paris and ceded his eastern lands in Languedoc to the French crown, keeping a reduced county for life.

treaty-of-paris-1856.s: The Treaty of Paris, signed on 30 March 1856 at the Congress of Paris, ended the Crimean War between Russia and the alliance of the Ottoman Empire, France, Britain and Sardinia. It neutralised the Black Sea, closing it to warships, guaranteed the integrity of the Ottoman…

treaty-of-paris-1857.s: The Treaty of Paris of 4 March 1857 ended the Anglo-Persian War between Britain and Qajar Iran, which had begun after Iranian forces took the Afghan city of Herat in 1856. Iran agreed to withdraw from Herat and to renounce all claims to Afghan territory, while Britain…

taihe-code.s: The Taihe Code was the legal code of the Jurchen Jin dynasty, issued in 1201 under the emperor Zhangzong and named after the Taihe reign period. Closely modelled on the Tang Code, it marked the height of the Jin adoption of Chinese government institutions.

tuhfat-al-nafis.s: The Tuhfat al-Nafis ('The Precious Gift') is a Malay history of the kingdoms of Johor, Riau, Siak and the Bugis written in the nineteenth century, completed by Raja Ali Haji of Riau-Lingga around 1865 from an earlier draft by his father. It traces the Malay rulers and the…

temenggong-abdul-rahman.s: Abdul Rahman was the temenggong, a senior Malay chief, of Johor who settled on the island of Singapore around 1811. On 6 February 1819 he and Hussein Shah signed the treaty with Stamford Raffles that allowed the British East India Company to found a settlement on the island.

temenggong-daeng-ibrahim.s: Daeng Ibrahim was the temenggong of Johor from 1841 to 1862 and the son of Temenggong Abdul Rahman. Enriched by Singapore's trade and by gambier and pepper planting by Chinese settlers in Johor, he became the real power in the state, and in 1855 Sultan Ali ceded him the…

taejong-of-joseon.s: Taejong, born Yi Bang-won, was the third king of Joseon, ruling from 1400 to 1418. A son of the founder Taejo, he killed rival princes and the chief minister Jeong Do-jeon in 1398 before taking the throne.

tiramakhan-traore.s: Tiramakhan Traore was a general of Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire, in the thirteenth century. According to Mandinka oral tradition he led a western campaign that conquered lands in the Gambia and Casamance regions, where his followers settled as rulers of frontier…

tauekel-khan.s: Tauekel Khan was khan of the Kazakhs in the late sixteenth century, ruling until 1598. A son of Shigai Khan, he took advantage of the death of Abdullah Khan II of Bukhara to seize Tashkent, Turkistan and other towns of the Syr Darya from the Shaybanids in 1598.

tzitzak.s: Tzitzak was a Khazar princess, a daughter of the khagan Bihar, who in 732 married the future Byzantine emperor Constantine V and was baptised as Irene. The marriage sealed an alliance between Byzantium and the Khazars against the Umayyad Caliphate.

ta-prohm.s: Ta Prohm is a temple at Angkor in Cambodia, founded by Jayavarman VII in 1186 as a Buddhist monastery dedicated to his mother. Its foundation inscription lists thousands of villages and tens of thousands of people who supplied and served it, a measure of the economic weight of…

terken-khatun-wife-of-tekish.s: Terken Khatun was the wife of the Khwarazmshah Ala ad-Din Tekish and mother of Ala ad-Din Muhammad II. A princess of the Qangli Turks, she kept her own court at Gurganj, and her kinsmen held key military commands, giving her power that rivalled her son's.

tui.s: Tui is a town in the province of Pontevedra in Galicia, on the Miño river opposite Valença in Portugal. A Roman town and the seat of a bishop from the sixth century, it was destroyed in the Muslim conquest and resettled under Ordoño I of Asturias in the ninth century.

tristan-und-isolde.s: Tristan und Isolde is an opera by Richard Wagner, composed between 1857 and 1859 on the medieval legend of the lovers Tristan and Isolde. It was first performed in Munich on 10 June 1865 under the patronage of Ludwig II of Bavaria.

treaty-of-ried.s: The Treaty of Ried was signed on 8 October 1813 at Ried im Innkreis between Bavaria and Austria. Bavaria left the Confederation of the Rhine and joined the Allies against Napoleon, in return for a guarantee of its sovereignty and of compensation for any lands it had to return…

treaty-of-munich-1816.s: The Treaty of Munich was signed on 14 April 1816 between Bavaria and Austria, completing the territorial settlement after the Napoleonic Wars. Bavaria returned Salzburg, the Innviertel and the Hausruckviertel to Austria, and in exchange received the Palatinate on the left bank…

ten-days-campaign.s: The Ten Days' Campaign was the Dutch invasion of Belgium in August 1831, an attempt by King William I of the Netherlands to reverse the Belgian Revolution. Dutch forces defeated the Belgian armies at Hasselt and Leuven, but withdrew when a French army entered Belgium to…

tito-winyi-iv.s: Tito Winyi IV was omukama of Bunyoro from 1924 until 1967. Under the Bunyoro Agreement of 1933 he gained formal recognition for the kingdom within the Uganda Protectorate, and in 1964 a referendum returned two of the lost counties, Buyaga and Bugangaizi.

teresa-of-portugal-queen-of-leon.n: Teresa of Portugal, Queen of León
teresa-of-portugal-queen-of-leon.s: Teresa of Portugal was a daughter of Sancho I of Portugal who married her cousin Alfonso IX of León in 1191. The marriage was annulled on grounds of kinship, and she later retired to the monastery of Lorvão.

tambor-de-mina.s: Tambor de Mina is an Afro-Brazilian religion centred on São Luís in the state of Maranhão, Brazil. Its oldest temple, the Casa das Minas, was founded in the nineteenth century by Africans from Dahomey and worships the vodun of the Fon royal family.

tegbesu.s: Tegbesu was king of Dahomey from 1740 to 1774, succeeding his father Agaja after a disputed succession. He consolidated royal control over the port of Ouidah and the slave trade, which became a royal monopoly and the main source of the kingdom's revenue, while Dahomey…

thyra.s: Thyra was the wife of King Gorm the Old of Denmark and mother of Harald Bluetooth, who lived in the tenth century. Gorm raised the smaller Jelling runestone in her memory, calling her "Denmark's adornment", one of the earliest inscriptions to name Denmark.

treaty-of-copenhagen-1660.s: The Treaty of Copenhagen was signed on 27 May 1660 between Denmark-Norway and Sweden, ending the war that Charles X Gustav had renewed in 1658. Concluded after his death, it returned Bornholm and Trøndelag to Denmark-Norway, while Scania, Halland, Blekinge and Bohuslän…

treaty-of-vienna-1864.s: The Treaty of Vienna was signed on 30 October 1864 between Denmark and the victors of the Second Schleswig War, Prussia and Austria. Denmark ceded the duchies of Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg to joint Prussian and Austrian administration.

tycho-brahe.s: Tycho Brahe was a Danish nobleman and astronomer. His observation of a new star in 1572 challenged the belief that the heavens were unchangeable.

the-anarchy.s: The Anarchy was a civil war in England and Normandy between King Stephen and Empress Matilda, daughter of Henry I, over the succession to the English throne. Fighting, sieges and the breakdown of royal authority lasted from 1138 until the Treaty of Wallingford of 1153, which…

the-canterbury-tales.s: The Canterbury Tales is a collection of stories in Middle English verse and prose by Geoffrey Chaucer, written in the late fourteenth century and left unfinished at his death in 1400. It presents a group of pilgrims travelling from Southwark to the shrine of Thomas Becket at…

treaty-of-troyes.s: The Treaty of Troyes was agreed on 21 May 1420 between Henry V of England and Charles VI of France, backed by the Duke of Burgundy. It disinherited the Dauphin Charles and made Henry heir to the French throne, and Henry married Charles's daughter Catherine of Valois.

thomas-cranmer.s: Thomas Cranmer was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1533 to 1555 and a leader of the English Reformation. He annulled Henry VIII's marriage to Catherine of Aragon, and under Edward VI he wrote the Book of Common Prayer and gave the Church of England a Protestant doctrine.

thomas-cromwell.s: Thomas Cromwell was chief minister to Henry VIII from about 1532 to 1540. He steered through Parliament the laws that broke with Rome and made the king head of the Church, organised the dissolution of the monasteries and reformed royal administration and finance.

thomas-hobbes.s: Thomas Hobbes was an English philosopher whose Leviathan of 1651 is a founding work of modern political thought. Writing during the English Civil War, he argued that without a sovereign power life would be a war of all against all, and that people agree to a social contract…

the-fronde.s: The Fronde was a series of revolts in France between 1648 and 1653 during the minority of Louis XIV. It began with the Parlement of Paris resisting new taxes imposed by Cardinal Mazarin and grew into a rebellion of great nobles led by princes such as Condé.

toulon.s: Toulon is a port city on the Mediterranean coast of Provence, France, with one of the finest natural harbours in Europe. Its arsenal was developed under Louis XIV by Colbert and Vauban, and it became the chief base of the French Mediterranean fleet.

the-spectator-1711.s: The Spectator was a daily periodical published in London in 1711 and 1712, founded by Joseph Addison and Richard Steele. Its essays, written in the voice of a fictional club of observers, commented on manners, morals, literature and fashion for a middle-class readership in the…

thomas-clarkson.s: Thomas Clarkson was an English campaigner against the slave trade. After winning a Cambridge essay prize on slavery in 1785, he helped found the Society for Effecting the Abolition of the Slave Trade in 1787 and travelled widely gathering evidence from sailors and ports.

the-wealth-of-nations.s: The Wealth of Nations, in full An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, is a book by Adam Smith published in London in 1776. It argued that wealth comes from labour and the division of labour, and that free competition, guided as if by an invisible hand,…

truman-doctrine.s: The Truman Doctrine was a United States foreign policy announced by President Harry S. Truman on 12 March 1947, pledging support to countries threatened by communist subversion or outside pressure. It was prompted by Britain's withdrawal of aid to Greece during its civil war…

treaty-of-aberconwy.s: The Treaty of Aberconwy was the settlement imposed by Edward I of England on Llywelyn ap Gruffudd in November 1277, ending their first war. Llywelyn kept the title of Prince of Wales but lost the homage of most Welsh lords and was confined to Gwynedd west of the River Conwy,…

treaty-of-woodstock.s: The Treaty of Woodstock was an agreement of April 1247 between Henry III of England and the brothers Owain and Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, made after the death of their uncle Dafydd ap Llywelyn. It confined the rulers of Gwynedd to the lands west of the River Conwy, leaving the…

treaty-of-worcester.s: The Treaty of Worcester was the agreement of 1218 by which the minority government of Henry III of England recognised the dominance of Llywelyn the Great in Wales. Llywelyn did homage to the young king and was allowed to keep the castles and lands he had taken, including…

transylvanian-saxons.s: The Transylvanian Saxons are a German-speaking people settled in southern and north-eastern Transylvania from the mid-twelfth century, first under King Géza II. The Andreanum of 1224 granted them collective self-government, and their towns, such as Hermannstadt (Sibiu) and…

treaty-of-pressburg-1491.s: The Treaty of Pressburg was signed on 7 November 1491 between Vladislaus II of Hungary and Bohemia and Emperor Frederick III and his son Maximilian. It ended Maximilian's war for the Hungarian throne after the death of Matthias Corvinus and provided that the Habsburgs would…

tripartitum.s: The Tripartitum is the compilation of the customary law of the Kingdom of Hungary made by István Werbőczy and presented to the diet in 1514. Though never formally promulgated, it was printed in Vienna in 1517 and used by the courts as the basic law book, confirming the equal…

treaty-of-elaznauri.s: The Treaty of Elaznauri was signed in April 1804 by Solomon II of Imereti, under Russian military pressure, at Elaznauri in Imereti. He accepted the protection of the Russian Empire while keeping his throne, but disputes over its terms continued, and in 1810 Russia deposed…

thomas-fitzgerald-10th-earl-of-kildare.s: Thomas FitzGerald, 10th Earl of Kildare, known as Silken Thomas, led a rebellion against Henry VIII in 1534 after rumours that his father, the imprisoned lord deputy, had been executed in London. His forces besieged Dublin and killed Archbishop John Alen, but the rising was…

theobald-wolfe-tone.s: Theobald Wolfe Tone was an Irish revolutionary, a Protestant lawyer who helped found the Society of United Irishmen in 1791. In France he persuaded the Directory to send an expedition to Ireland, which reached Bantry Bay in 1796 but could not land.

treaty-of-limerick.s: The Treaty of Limerick was signed on 3 October 1691, ending the siege of Limerick and the Williamite War in Ireland. Its military articles allowed the Jacobite soldiers to sail to France, the 'Flight of the Wild Geese', while its civil articles promised Catholics the religious…

treaty-of-mellifont.s: The Treaty of Mellifont was the submission of Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone, to Lord Mountjoy at Mellifont in County Louth in March 1603, ending the Nine Years' War. O'Neill renounced his Gaelic title and accepted English law but kept most of his lands; he had not been told…

trinity-college-dublin.s: Trinity College Dublin is the college founded in 1592 by a charter of Elizabeth I on the site of a dissolved monastery in Dublin. For centuries the intellectual centre of the Protestant Ascendancy, it educated Jonathan Swift, George Berkeley, Oliver Goldsmith and Edmund Burke,…

tirzah.s: Tirzah was an ancient city in the northern hills of Samaria, usually identified with Tell el-Far'ah (North) near Nablus in the West Bank. According to the Bible it served as a royal residence and the capital of the Kingdom of Israel from the late 10th century BCE until Omri…

tisha-bav.s: Tisha B'Av, the ninth day of the Hebrew month of Av, is the annual fast day in Judaism that mourns the destruction of the First Temple by the Babylonians in 587 or 586 BCE and of the Second Temple by the Romans in 70 CE. Other disasters of Jewish history are also remembered on…

tormes.s: The Tormes is a river of western Spain that rises in the Sierra de Gredos and flows north-west through Salamanca to join the Duero on the Portuguese border. After Ramiro II's victory at Simancas in 939, the Kingdom of León resettled its valley around Salamanca.

treaty-of-zamora.s: The Treaty of Zamora was the agreement of October 1143 by which Alfonso VII of León and Castile recognised his cousin Afonso Henriques as King of Portugal. It was concluded at Zamora in the presence of the papal legate, Cardinal Guido de Vico.

third-anglo-mysore-war.s: The Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790–1792) was provoked by Tipu Sultan's attack on the lines of Travancore, an ally of the British East India Company, in 1789. Governor-General Lord Cornwallis, allied with the Marathas and the Nizam of Hyderabad, took Bangalore in 1791 and…

tipus-tiger.s: Tipu's Tiger is a wooden automaton made for Tipu Sultan of Mysore around 1795, showing a life-sized tiger mauling a European soldier. A small pipe organ inside imitates the growls of the tiger and the cries of its victim.

treaty-of-madras.s: The Treaty of Madras was concluded on 4 April 1769 between Hyder Ali of Mysore and the British East India Company, ending the First Anglo-Mysore War after Hyder's cavalry appeared near Madras. Both sides restored their conquests and promised to aid each other if attacked.

treaty-of-mangalore.s: The Treaty of Mangalore was signed on 11 March 1784 between Tipu Sultan of Mysore and the British East India Company, ending the Second Anglo-Mysore War. Each side gave back the territory it had taken and released its prisoners.

treaty-of-seringapatam.s: The Treaty of Seringapatam was signed in March 1792 by Tipu Sultan of Mysore with the British East India Company and its allies, the Marathas and the Nizam of Hyderabad, ending the Third Anglo-Mysore War. With Cornwallis's army outside Srirangapatna, Tipu ceded about half of…

teatro-di-san-carlo.s: The Teatro di San Carlo is the opera house of Naples, opened on 4 November 1737 by Charles of Bourbon next to the royal palace. It is the oldest opera house in Europe still in continuous use and was a leading centre of Italian opera, with works by Rossini and Donizetti…

the-dream-of-the-rood.s: The Dream of the Rood is an Old English poem in which the poet dreams of the Cross, which speaks of its part in Christ's crucifixion as a loyal retainer of a heroic lord. The full text survives in the Vercelli Book of the late tenth century, but lines related to it were carved…

treaty-of-dardanos.s: The Treaty of Dardanos ended the First Mithridatic War in 85 BCE. Meeting Sulla at Dardanos in the Troad, Mithridates VI of Pontus agreed to give up his conquests in the province of Asia, Bithynia and Cappadocia, surrender part of his fleet and pay an indemnity, in return for…

treaty-of-alcanices.s: The Treaty of Alcañices was signed on 12 September 1297 at Alcañices in León between King Denis of Portugal and Ferdinand IV of Castile. Portugal gained the Riba-Côa district and other border towns, giving up claims elsewhere, and the two crowns agreed peace and royal marriages.

treaty-of-windsor-1386.s: The Treaty of Windsor was signed on 9 May 1386 between Richard II of England and John I of Portugal, renewing the alliance of 1373 after English archers had fought for Portugal at Aljubarrota. It pledged perpetual friendship and mutual support, and John's marriage to Philippa…

treaty-of-kalisz-1813.s: The Treaty of Kalisz (Kalisch) was signed on 28 February 1813 between Russia and Prussia after Napoleon's disastrous retreat from Moscow. Prussia abandoned its forced alliance with France and joined Russia in war against Napoleon, and Russia promised to restore Prussia to its…

treaty-of-london-1718.s: The Quadruple Alliance was formed in 1718 by Britain, France and Austria, with the Dutch Republic expected to join, to uphold the Peace of Utrecht against Spain, which had seized Sardinia and Sicily. After the War of the Quadruple Alliance, the Treaty of The Hague of 1720 gave…

treaty-of-zurich.s: The Treaty of Zürich, signed on 10 November 1859 by Austria, France and the Kingdom of Sardinia, ended the Second Italian War of Independence. It confirmed the preliminary peace of Villafranca: Austria ceded most of Lombardy to France, which passed it to Sardinia, while…

the-brus.s: The Brus is a long narrative poem in Scots by John Barbour, archdeacon of Aberdeen, completed around 1375. In some 13,000 lines it tells the story of Robert the Bruce and his companion James Douglas in the Wars of Independence, culminating in Bannockburn, and celebrates…

treaty-of-edinburgh-northampton.s: The Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton, agreed at Edinburgh in March 1328 and ratified by the English parliament at Northampton in May, ended the First War of Scottish Independence. England recognised Robert I as king of an independent Scotland and gave up its claim to…

treaty-of-edinburgh-1560.s: The Treaty of Edinburgh of 6 July 1560 was agreed between England and France after English forces helped the Scottish Protestant lords besiege the French garrison at Leith. Both French and English troops withdrew from Scotland, ending French domination and opening the way for…

treaty-of-falaise.s: The Treaty of Falaise was imposed in December 1174 on William the Lion, King of Scots, who had been captured at Alnwick while invading England. William accepted Henry II of England as his feudal overlord and handed over the castles of Roxburgh, Berwick, Jedburgh, Edinburgh and…

tabula-rogeriana.s: The Tabula Rogeriana, or Book of Roger, is the great work of geography that Muhammad al-Idrisi completed in 1154 for Roger II of Sicily. Written in Arabic and drawing on earlier geographers and travellers' reports gathered at the Palermo court, it describes the known world…

tancred-king-of-sicily.s: Tancred of Lecce was King of Sicily from 1189 to 1194, an illegitimate grandson of Roger II. On the death of William II the Sicilian barons and officials chose him rather than Roger II's daughter Constance, wife of the future emperor Henry VI.

treaty-of-mignano.s: The Treaty of Mignano was concluded on 25 July 1139 between Roger II of Sicily and Pope Innocent II, who had been captured by Roger's forces at Galluccio three days earlier. The pope recognised Roger as King of Sicily, Duke of Apulia and Prince of Capua, legitimising the royal…

torgils-knutsson.s: Torgils Knutsson was Lord High Constable of Sweden and the leading figure of the regency for the young King Birger Magnusson in the 1290s. In 1293 he led the expedition into Karelia known as the third Swedish crusade and founded Vyborg Castle.

theo-van-gogh-film-director.s: Theo van Gogh was a Dutch film director, writer and provocative columnist, a great-grandson of Theo van Gogh, brother of the painter Vincent. In 2004 he made the short film Submission with Ayaan Hirsi Ali, criticising the treatment of women in Islam.

toprakkale.s: Toprakkale is the site of a Urartian citadel on a hill east of Van in eastern Turkey, identified with Rusahinili, founded in the seventh century BCE as a new royal centre near the old capital Tushpa. It contained a major temple of the god Haldi.

teisheba.s: Teisheba was the storm and war god of Urartu, second in the state pantheon after Haldi. A form of the Hurrian storm god Teshub, he was often shown standing on a bull, and the fortress-city of Teishebaini, now Karmir Blur near Yerevan, was named after him.

the-consolation-of-philosophy.s: The Consolation of Philosophy is a Latin work by the Roman statesman Boethius, written around 524 while he awaited execution after falling from favour with the Ostrogothic king Theoderic. In alternating prose and verse, Lady Philosophy consoles the prisoner by showing that…

the-solent.s: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and the mainland of southern England, a sheltered waterway leading to the harbours of Southampton and Portsmouth. In the early Anglo-Saxon period its coasts were settled by Jutes and Saxons whose lands became part of the…

the-life-of-jesus-critically-examined.n: The Life of Jesus, Critically Examined
the-life-of-jesus-critically-examined.s: The Life of Jesus, Critically Examined is a work by the German theologian David Friedrich Strauss, published in 1835–1836. It argued that the gospel accounts of miracles were myths produced by the early Christian community, rather than history or misunderstood natural events.

treaty-of-fulda.s: The Treaty of Fulda was concluded on 2 November 1813 between Austria and the Kingdom of Württemberg after the Battle of Leipzig. King Frederick I abandoned his alliance with Napoleon and joined the coalition against him, and in return his sovereignty and territorial…

tubingen.s: Tübingen is a university town on the River Neckar in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, south of Stuttgart. Its university, founded in 1477, and the Protestant seminary known as the Stift trained generations of Württemberg clergy and officials, including Hegel, Hölderlin and Schelling.

tylissos.s: Tylissos is an archaeological site and village in north-central Crete, west of Heraklion, with the remains of three large Minoan houses of the sixteenth and fifteenth centuries BCE. In the Greek period it was a small independent city, and a treaty of about 450 BCE between…

termez.s: Termez is a city in southern Uzbekistan on the Amu Darya, at an ancient crossing between Bactria and the lands to the north. Under the Kushans it was a flourishing Buddhist centre, with the monasteries of Kara Tepe and Fayaz Tepe.

tantamani.s: Tantamani was the last king of the Kushite 25th Dynasty to rule Egypt. Succeeding Taharqa in 664 BCE, he briefly reconquered Memphis, but the Assyrian army of Ashurbanipal drove him south and sacked Thebes in 663 BCE.

temple-of-literature-hanoi.s: The Temple of Literature in Hanoi was founded in 1070 as a temple to Confucius and became the seat of Vietnam's first national academy. From 1484 the names of successful doctoral candidates were carved on stone stelae resting on tortoises; 82 stelae survive, covering…

tran-cao.s: Trần Cảo was the leader of a major revolt in northern Vietnam in 1516, provoked by the heavy labour demands and palace building of the Lê emperor Lê Tương Dực. Claiming descent from the Trần dynasty, he briefly seized the capital Thăng Long before being driven out, and the…

telugu-cholas.s: The Telugu Cholas, or Telugu Chodas, were families of chiefs in the Telugu country who claimed descent from the Tamil Chola kings. The most important line ruled from Nellore in the 12th and 13th centuries, acting at times as feudatories of the Cholas and Kakatiyas; its ruler…

tomb-of-the-princess-of-chen.n: Tomb of the Princess of Chen
tomb-of-the-princess-of-chen.s: The Tomb of the Princess of Chen is a Liao dynasty burial in Inner Mongolia, China, of a Khitan princess and her husband, who were interred in 1018. Excavated undisturbed in 1986, it contained the couple dressed in silver-wire burial suits with gold face masks, along with…

temple-of-diana-merida.s: The Temple of Diana is a Roman temple at Mérida in Spain, ancient Emerita Augusta, capital of Lusitania. Built in the late 1st century BCE in the city's municipal forum, it was probably dedicated to the imperial cult, and its traditional name is a mistaken attribution.

torre-de-palma.s: Torre de Palma is the site of a large Roman villa near Monforte in the Alentejo region of Portugal, occupied from the 1st century CE into late antiquity. It is known for its 4th-century mosaics, among them the Mosaic of the Muses and a mosaic of named horses, now in the…

turan-shah-ibn-ayyub.s: Turan-Shah ibn Ayyub, called Shams al-Dawla, was an elder brother of Saladin and a leading Ayyubid commander. In 1172–1173, after a Nubian attack on Aswan, he led an army south into Nubia and sacked Qasr Ibrim.

tulunid-dynasty.s: The Tulunid dynasty ruled Egypt and Syria from 868 to 905, the first dynasty to make Egypt effectively independent of the Abbasid caliphate. Its founder, Ahmad ibn Tulun, a Turkish officer sent as governor, built a new capital, al-Qata'i, with the great Mosque of Ibn Tulun.

treaty-of-basel-1499.s: The Treaty of Basel of 22 September 1499 ended the Swabian War between the Old Swiss Confederacy and Emperor Maximilian I with the Swabian League. It freed the Confederates in practice from the jurisdiction of the imperial courts and the imperial taxes of the reform of 1495,…

teltow.s: The Teltow is a plateau region of Brandenburg, Germany, south of Berlin, between the Spree, Havel and Dahme rivers. In the 13th century the Ascanian margraves John I and Otto III won it in rivalry with the margraves of Meissen and settled it with German colonists.

treaty-of-furstenwalde.s: The Treaty of Fürstenwalde of 1373 transferred the Margraviate of Brandenburg from Otto V of the House of Wittelsbach to Emperor Charles IV of the House of Luxembourg. After a brief war, Otto surrendered the Mark in return for money and lands, and Charles granted it to his…

tegal.s: Tegal is a port city on the north coast of Central Java, Indonesia, between Cirebon and Semarang. In 1629 Sultan Agung of Mataram gathered rice stores there and at Cirebon for his second siege of Batavia, and their destruction by Dutch ships contributed to the siege's failure.

tuban.s: Tuban is a town on the north coast of East Java, Indonesia, and one of the oldest ports of Java. Chinese and Javanese sources record it as a major harbour in the Majapahit period, trading with China and the spice islands, and it later became a Muslim coastal state.

tantara-ny-andriana.s: The Tantara ny Andriana eto Madagasikara ('History of the kings of Madagascar') is a collection of Merina oral traditions about the kings and customs of Imerina. Recorded from Malagasy informants and published between 1873 and 1881 by the French Jesuit François Callet, it is…

tomas-mejia.s: Tomás Mejía was a Mexican general of Otomí origin from the Sierra Gorda of Querétaro and a leading conservative commander in the Reform War and the French intervention. He fought for Emperor Maximilian to the end and was captured with him at Querétaro.

treaty-of-tlatelolco.s: The Treaty of Tlatelolco, signed in Mexico City on 14 February 1967, created a nuclear-weapon-free zone in Latin America and the Caribbean, the first in a populated region. Promoted by Mexico after the Cuban Missile Crisis and negotiated under Alfonso García Robles, it bans…

tale-of-the-eloquent-peasant.s: The Tale of the Eloquent Peasant is an ancient Egyptian literary work of the Middle Kingdom. It tells of a peasant robbed of his goods by an official's servant, who appeals for justice in nine eloquent petitions, recorded at the king's wish before justice is finally done.

tale-of-the-shipwrecked-sailor.s: The Tale of the Shipwrecked Sailor is an ancient Egyptian story of the Middle Kingdom, preserved on a single papyrus in St Petersburg. A sailor tells how, shipwrecked on a magical island, he was welcomed by a great serpent who foretold his rescue and sent him home laden with…

tod-egypt.s: Tod is a village and archaeological site on the east bank of the Nile south of Luxor, in Upper Egypt, ancient Djerty, with a temple of the war god Montu. In 1936 excavators found beneath the temple the Tod Treasure, four bronze chests inscribed for Amenemhat II containing…

the-capture-of-miletus.s: The Capture of Miletus was a tragedy by the Athenian dramatist Phrynichus about the Persian sack of Miletus in 494 BCE at the end of the Ionian Revolt. According to Herodotus the audience burst into tears, and the Athenians fined Phrynichus a thousand drachmas for reminding…

tadukhipa.s: Tadukhipa was a Mitanni princess, daughter of King Tushratta, who was sent to Egypt with a rich dowry to marry the ageing Pharaoh Amenhotep III near the end of his reign. Her marriage and dowry are recorded in the Amarna letters.

todar-mal.s: Todar Mal was the finance minister of the Mughal emperor Akbar and one of the leading nobles of his court. He reorganised land revenue through the zabt system, which assessed taxes in cash from measured land and average yields and prices, and his methods long shaped revenue…

than-shwe.s: Than Shwe is a Myanmar general who led the country's military government from 1992 to 2011 as chairman of the State Law and Order Restoration Council and its successor, the State Peace and Development Council. He kept Aung San Suu Kyi under house arrest, crushed the Saffron…

tatmadaw.s: The Tatmadaw is the name of Myanmar's armed forces. Tracing their origin to the Burma Independence Army of 1941, they have fought ethnic and communist insurgencies almost without pause since independence in 1948 and have dominated politics, ruling directly or through a…

thein-sein.s: Thein Sein is a Myanmar general and politician who was prime minister from 2007 and president from 2011 to 2016. Leading the first nominally civilian government after decades of military rule, he released political prisoners, relaxed censorship, allowed Aung San Suu Kyi's…

treblinka-extermination-camp.s: Treblinka was a Nazi extermination camp north-east of Warsaw in German-occupied Poland, built as part of Operation Reinhard. Between July 1942 and October 1943 some 700,000 to 900,000 Jews, most of them from the Warsaw Ghetto, were murdered there in gas chambers, more than at…

treaty-of-saint-germain-en-laye-1632.s: The Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye, signed on 29 March 1632, returned Quebec and Acadia to France. English privateers under the Kirke brothers had taken Quebec in 1629, after peace between England and France had already been agreed, and Charles I gave the colonies back in…

troupes-de-la-marine.s: The Troupes de la Marine were independent companies of infantry under the French Ministry of the Marine, raised to defend France's colonies and naval ports. From 1683 they formed the regular garrison of New France, and many of their officers were Canadian-born men skilled in…

tenzing-norgay.s: Tenzing Norgay was a Sherpa mountaineer who, with Edmund Hillary, made the first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest on 29 May 1953, as a member of a British expedition led by John Hunt. He had taken part in several earlier Everest expeditions.

think-big.s: Think Big was a programme of large state-backed industrial projects launched by Robert Muldoon's National government in New Zealand from 1979 to reduce dependence on imported oil. It used the country's natural gas to build a synthetic petrol plant, a methanol plant and an…

tokelau.s: Tokelau is a group of three coral atolls in the South Pacific, north of Samoa, that is a dependent territory of New Zealand. It was annexed by Britain in 1916 as part of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony and placed under New Zealand administration in 1926, becoming part of…

treaty-of-waitangi-act-1975.s: The Treaty of Waitangi Act 1975 was a New Zealand law that created the Waitangi Tribunal to hear Māori claims that the Crown had breached the principles of the Treaty of Waitangi. At first limited to claims arising after 1975, its scope was extended by an amendment in 1985…

treaty-principles-bill.s: The Treaty Principles Bill was a bill introduced in the New Zealand Parliament in November 2024 by ACT New Zealand to define the principles of the Treaty of Waitangi in law. Critics argued that it would reduce Māori rights under the Treaty, and it provoked one of the largest…

the-tale-of-kieu.s: The Tale of Kieu, or Truyện Kiều, is an epic poem by Nguyễn Du, written in the early nineteenth century in chữ Nôm script and in the six-eight lục bát verse form. Adapted from a Chinese novel, it tells of Thúy Kiều, a young woman who sells herself to save her family and…

treaty-of-saigon-1874.s: The Treaty of Saigon of 15 March 1874, negotiated by the French official Paul-Louis-Félix Philastre after Francis Garnier's seizure of Hanoi, recognised French sovereignty over all six provinces of Cochinchina. In return France withdrew its forces from Tonkin.

thieu-tri.s: Thiệu Trị was the third emperor of the Nguyen dynasty of Vietnam, ruling from 1841 to 1847 after his father Minh Mạng. Faced with revolt in Cambodia, he withdrew Vietnamese forces from much of the country, accepting shared influence with Siam.

ton-that-thuyet.s: Tôn Thất Thuyết was a Vietnamese mandarin and regent of the Nguyen court who led resistance to French rule. On 5 July 1885 he launched an attack on the French garrison at Huế, and after its failure fled with the boy emperor Hàm Nghi and issued the Cần Vương edict calling on…

tran-tay-province.s: Trấn Tây was the province into which Emperor Minh Mạng of Vietnam organised much of Cambodia after 1834, ruling through Vietnamese officials and the puppet queen Ang Mey. Vietnamese administrative and cultural measures provoked a Cambodian uprising in 1840, and after renewed…

treaty-of-tientsin-1885.s: The Treaty of Tientsin of 9 June 1885 was signed by Li Hongzhang for the Qing dynasty and the French envoy Jules Patenôtre, ending the Sino-French War. China recognised the French protectorates over Annam and Tonkin, giving up its claim to suzerainty over Vietnam, and France…

treaty-of-bolotovo.s: The Treaty of Bolotovo was an agreement, traditionally dated to 1348, by which the Novgorod Republic recognised the independence of Pskov, until then its dependent town. Pskov gained the right to elect its own officials and its own bishop's representative.

theophanes-the-greek.s: Theophanes the Greek was a Byzantine painter of icons and frescoes who worked in the Russian lands from about the 1370s. His frescoes of 1378 in the Church of the Transfiguration on Ilyina Street in Novgorod are his only surviving securely attributed murals.

treaty-of-korostyn.s: The Treaty of Korostyn was concluded in August 1471 between Ivan III of Moscow and the Novgorod Republic after Novgorod's defeat at the Battle of Shelon. Novgorod paid a large indemnity, renounced any alliance with Lithuania and accepted limits on its self-government,…

treaty-of-yazhelbitsy.s: The Treaty of Yazhelbitsy was imposed on the Novgorod Republic by Vasily II of Moscow in 1456, after his army defeated the Novgorodians at Staraya Russa. Novgorod paid an indemnity, promised not to shelter the grand prince's enemies and lost the right to conduct its own…

thracia.s: Thracia was a province of the Roman Empire created by the emperor Claudius in 46 CE after the murder of the client king Rhoemetalces III, covering much of present-day southern Bulgaria, north-eastern Greece and European Turkey. Its main cities included Philippopolis and…

tundzha.s: The Tundzha, ancient Tonzos, is a river of about 390 kilometres in south-eastern Bulgaria and European Turkey. Rising in the Balkan Mountains, it flows east through the Kazanlak Valley, then south past Yambol to join the Maritsa at Edirne.

ten-thousand.s: The Ten Thousand were Greek mercenaries hired by the Persian prince Cyrus the Younger in 401 BCE to seize the throne from his brother Artaxerxes II. After Cyrus fell at Cunaxa and their generals were treacherously killed, they fought their way north through Mesopotamia and…

treaty-of-thaba-bosiu.s: The Treaty of Thaba Bosiu was signed in April 1866 between Moshoeshoe I of the Basotho and the Orange Free State, ending the war of 1865–1866. Moshoeshoe ceded much of the fertile land west of the Caledon River to the Free State, but fighting resumed in 1867, and Moshoeshoe's…

thatbyinnyu-temple.s: The Thatbyinnyu Temple is the tallest temple of Pagan (Bagan) in central Myanmar, rising about 61 metres. It was built in the mid-twelfth century under King Alaungsithu and marks the transition to a taller, two-storeyed style of temple with its main shrine on the upper floor.

taranatha.s: Taranatha was a Tibetan Buddhist lama and scholar of the Jonang school. His History of Buddhism in India, completed in 1608, collects Indian and Tibetan traditions about the Buddhist teachers and kings of India, including the Pala dynasty, and remains an important if late source.

tiruvalangadu-copper-plates.s: The Tiruvalangadu copper plates are a set of inscribed copper plates issued in the reign of the Chola king Rajendra I and found at Tiruvalangadu in Tamil Nadu. Written in Sanskrit and Tamil, they record a royal grant and give a long genealogy of the Chola dynasty, including…

takua-pa.s: Takua Pa is a town and district in Phang Nga Province on the Andaman Sea coast of southern Thailand. In the first millennium CE the area, especially the island of Ko Kho Khao, was a port on the route across the Malay Peninsula.

thirumangai-alvar.s: Thirumangai Alvar was a Tamil poet-saint devoted to Vishnu, traditionally the last of the twelve Alvars, who lived in the eighth or ninth century. Said to have been a local chieftain before his conversion, he visited many Vishnu temples and contributed more hymns than any…

tondaimandalam.s: Tondaimandalam is a historical region of northern Tamil Nadu and southern Andhra Pradesh, centred on Kanchipuram and including the area of present-day Chennai and Vellore. It was the heartland of the Pallava dynasty from the fourth to the ninth century and was annexed by the…

theophylact-i-count-of-tusculum.s: Theophylact I, Count of Tusculum, was a Roman nobleman who dominated Rome and the papacy in the early tenth century. Holding the offices of vestararius, magister militum and senator, he and his wife Theodora controlled papal appointments, and their daughter Marozia continued…

tiananmen.s: Tiananmen, the Gate of Heavenly Peace, is the monumental gate at the southern entrance to the Imperial City of Beijing, first built in 1420 under the Ming dynasty and rebuilt in 1651. From its rostrum Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China on 1 October 1949, and…

third-plenum-of-the-11th-central-committ.n: Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee
third-plenum-of-the-11th-central-committ.s: The Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, held in Beijing in December 1978, confirmed Deng Xiaoping as China's leading figure. It shifted the party's priority from class struggle to economic modernisation and is regarded as the start of the…

treaty-of-viterbo-1267.s: The Treaty of Viterbo was concluded in May 1267 between Charles of Anjou, the deposed Latin emperor Baldwin II and William II of Villehardouin of Achaea, under the auspices of Pope Clement IV. William accepted Charles as suzerain, and his daughter Isabella married Charles's…

tirant-lo-blanc.s: Tirant lo Blanc is a chivalric romance in Catalan by the Valencian knight Joanot Martorell, completed after his death by Martí Joan de Galba and printed in Valencia in 1490. Realistic and humorous, it tells of a knight who saves the Byzantine Empire, and it was praised by…

taula-de-canvi.s: The Taula de Canvi ('exchange table') of Barcelona was a public bank founded by the city council in 1401 to hold deposits, make payments and manage the city's debt. One of the first public banks in Europe, it lasted in various forms until the nineteenth century.

treaty-of-corbeil-1258.s: The Treaty of Corbeil was signed in May 1258 between Louis IX of France and James I of Aragon. Louis renounced the French crown's claims to suzerainty over the Catalan counties, and James gave up most of his claims in Languedoc and Provence, fixing the border roughly along the…

treaty-of-bucharest-1812.s: The Treaty of Bucharest, signed on 28 May 1812, ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1806–1812. The Ottoman Empire ceded to Russia the eastern half of the Principality of Moldavia between the Prut and the Dniester, which became the Russian province of Bessarabia, and Serbia gained…

tekyeh-dowlat.s: The Tekyeh Dowlat was a royal theatre built in Tehran by Naser al-Din Shah in 1868 near the Golestan Palace for performances of the ta'zieh, the passion plays that commemorate the martyrdom of Imam Husayn at Karbala. A large circular building seating thousands of spectators,…

talha-ibn-ubayd-allah.s: Talha ibn Ubayd Allah was an early companion of Muhammad from the Quraysh of Mecca, one of the ten promised paradise in Sunni tradition and a member of the council that chose Uthman as caliph in 644. After Uthman's murder he joined Aisha and al-Zubayr in opposing the new…

tulayha-ibn-khuwaylid.s: Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid was a chief of the Banu Asad of north-central Arabia who claimed to be a prophet in Muhammad's last years. During the Ridda Wars his followers were defeated by Khalid ibn al-Walid at the Battle of Buzakha in 632 and he fled to Syria.

thongchai-winichakul.s: Thongchai Winichakul is a Thai historian, long a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. In Siam Mapped: A History of the Geo-Body of a Nation (1994) he argued that modern mapping and the boundary treaties of the late nineteenth century created the idea of Siam as a…

trinitarians.s: The Trinitarians, the Order of the Most Holy Trinity and of the Captives, are a Catholic religious order founded in France in 1198 by John of Matha and approved by Pope Innocent III. Its original mission was to ransom Christians held captive by Muslims, and for centuries its…

treaty-of-petropolis.s: The Treaty of Petrópolis, signed on 17 November 1903, ended the dispute between Bolivia and Brazil over Acre, a rubber-rich Amazon territory settled by Brazilian rubber tappers who had rebelled against Bolivian rule. Bolivia ceded Acre to Brazil in return for a payment of two…

tarapaca.s: Tarapacá is a desert region in the far north of Chile, with its capital at Iquique. Formerly a Peruvian province rich in nitrates, it was conquered by Chile in the War of the Pacific and ceded under the Treaty of Ancón of 1883.

tacna.s: Tacna is a city in the far south of Peru, near the Chilean border. Occupied by Chile during the War of the Pacific in 1880, it remained under Chilean administration for nearly fifty years because the plebiscite promised by the Treaty of Ancón was never held.

tierra-del-fuego.s: Tierra del Fuego is an archipelago at the southern tip of South America, separated from the mainland by the Strait of Magellan. Named by Ferdinand Magellan's expedition in 1520, it was home to the Selk'nam, Yaghan and other peoples.

treaty-of-ancon.s: The Treaty of Ancón, signed on 20 October 1883, ended the war between Chile and Peru in the War of the Pacific. Peru ceded the nitrate province of Tarapacá to Chile, while Tacna and Arica were to remain under Chilean control for ten years, followed by a plebiscite.

treaty-of-lima-1929.s: The Treaty of Lima, signed on 3 June 1929 with the mediation of the United States, settled the Tacna–Arica dispute left by the War of the Pacific. Tacna was returned to Peru and Arica remained with Chile, which paid Peru compensation and agreed to provide port facilities.

three-principles-of-the-people.s: The Three Principles of the People, nationalism, democracy and the people's livelihood, form the political philosophy of Sun Yat-sen, developed from the early 1900s and set out in lectures of 1924. They became the official doctrine of the Kuomintang and of the Republic of…

taiwan-relations-act.s: The Taiwan Relations Act is a law passed by the United States Congress in April 1979, after Washington switched diplomatic recognition from the Republic of China to the People's Republic. It maintained commercial, cultural and other ties with Taiwan through the American…

taiwan-semiconductor-manufacturing-compa.s: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is a Taiwanese chipmaker founded in 1987 by Morris Chang with backing from the government. It pioneered the 'foundry' model of making chips designed by other companies and became the world's largest contract chipmaker,…

taiwan-strait.s: The Taiwan Strait is the arm of the sea, about 130 to 180 kilometres wide, that separates Taiwan from the Chinese province of Fujian. Since 1949 it has divided the Republic of China from the People's Republic and has been the scene of crises in 1954–1955, 1958 and 1995–1996.

third-taiwan-strait-crisis.s: The Third Taiwan Strait Crisis was a period of military tension in 1995–1996, triggered by Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui's visit to the United States in June 1995. The People's Republic of China fired missiles into waters near Taiwan and held exercises before Taiwan's first…

tongmenghui.s: The Tongmenghui, or Revolutionary Alliance, was a secret society founded in Tokyo in August 1905 by Sun Yat-sen and other Chinese revolutionaries to overthrow the Qing dynasty. It united several revolutionary groups and organised a series of uprisings in southern China.

tsai-ing-wen.s: Tsai Ing-wen is a Taiwanese politician and former law professor who led the Democratic Progressive Party and served as president of the Republic of China from 2016 to 2024, the first woman to hold the office. Her government legalised same-sex marriage in 2019, the first in…

temporary-provisions-against-the-communi.n: Temporary Provisions against the Communist Rebellion
temporary-provisions-against-the-communi.s: The Temporary Provisions against the Communist Rebellion were amendments attached to the constitution of the Republic of China in 1948, during the civil war. They gave the president emergency powers and exempted him from term limits, and on Taiwan they underpinned martial law…

trans-ecuadorian-oil-pipeline-system.s: The Trans-Ecuadorian Oil Pipeline System is the main oil pipeline of Ecuador, running about 500 kilometres from Lago Agrio in the Amazon across the Andes to the Pacific port of Esmeraldas. Opened in 1972, it made oil Ecuador's leading export and the main source of state revenue.

tapa-estonia.s: Tapa is a small town in Lääne-Viru County in northern Estonia, a railway junction on the line from Tallinn to Narva and Tartu. It has long been an important military base.

tarja-halonen.s: Tarja Halonen (born 1943) is a Finnish Social Democratic politician who served as president of Finland from 2000 to 2012, the first woman to hold the office. A lawyer and former trade union official, she had been foreign minister from 1995 to 2000.

the-prince.s: The Prince is a political treatise by the Florentine Niccolò Machiavelli, written in 1513 after the return of the Medici had cost him his office, and published in 1532. Dedicated to Lorenzo de' Medici, Duke of Urbino, it describes how new princes win and hold power, arguing…

tela.s: Tela is a port town on the Caribbean coast of northern Honduras, in the department of Atlántida. From the early twentieth century it was the headquarters of the Tela Railroad Company, the Honduran subsidiary of the United Fruit Company, whose banana plantations, railways and…

the-emergency-india.s: The Emergency was a period from June 1975 to March 1977 during which Prime Minister Indira Gandhi ruled by decree after a court found her guilty of electoral malpractice. Civil liberties were suspended, the press was censored, opposition leaders were jailed and a forced…
