tashkent-declaration.s: The Tashkent Declaration was the peace agreement signed on 10 January 1966 by Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri of India and President Ayub Khan of Pakistan at Tashkent, with Soviet mediation by Alexei Kosygin. It ended the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965 by committing both sides…

torrijos-carter-treaties.s: The Torrijos–Carter Treaties were two agreements signed on 7 September 1977 by Panama's leader Omar Torrijos and US President Jimmy Carter. The Panama Canal Treaty abolished the Canal Zone in 1979 and provided for joint administration until the canal passed fully to Panama on…

thousand-days-war.s: The Thousand Days' War was a civil war in Colombia from 1899 to 1902 between the governing Conservatives and the Liberals, which killed perhaps 100,000 people. Much of the final fighting took place on the isthmus of Panama, then a Colombian department, and the war ended with…

thomson-urrutia-treaty.s: The Thomson–Urrutia Treaty was signed in Bogotá in April 1914 by the United States and Colombia to settle the dispute caused by Panama's secession in 1903. Ratified by the US Senate only in 1921, after an expression of regret had been removed, it paid Colombia 25 million…

truth-and-reconciliation-commission-peru.s: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Peru was established in 2001, after the fall of Alberto Fujimori, to investigate the internal armed conflict of 1980–2000. Its final report of 2003 estimated that about 69,000 people had been killed or disappeared, attributed more…

truth-and-reconciliation-commission-of-c.n: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada
truth-and-reconciliation-commission-of-c.s: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada was established in 2008 under the settlement of lawsuits by former pupils of Canada's Indian residential schools, church-run boarding schools to which Indigenous children were sent from the nineteenth century until the 1990s.…

truth-and-reconciliation-commission-sout.s: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission of South Africa was set up in 1995 after the end of apartheid to investigate gross human rights violations committed between 1960 and 1994. Chaired by Archbishop Desmond Tutu, it held public hearings from 1996 in which victims testified…

tradiciones-peruanas.s: Tradiciones peruanas is a collection of several hundred short prose pieces by Ricardo Palma, published in series from 1872, mixing history, legend, anecdote and humour and mostly set in colonial Lima. Written in a lively, ironic style, they created a popular literary genre,…

tupac-amaru-revolutionary-movement.s: The Túpac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) was a Marxist–Leninist guerrilla group active in Peru from the early 1980s, smaller than and rival to the Shining Path. It is best known for seizing the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima in December 1996 and holding dozens of…

treaty-of-zadar.s: The Treaty of Zadar was signed on 18 February 1358 between Venice and Louis I of Hungary after a war that Venice had lost. Venice gave up all of Dalmatia, from the Kvarner Gulf to Durazzo, and the doge dropped the title Duke of Dalmatia.

telesom.s: Telesom is a telecommunications company based in Hargeisa, Somaliland, founded in 2002. It is the largest mobile operator in Somaliland, and its ZAAD mobile-money service, launched in 2009, made electronic payments part of everyday life in a territory with little formal banking.

thabo-mbeki.s: Thabo Mbeki is a South African politician who was president of South Africa from 1999 to 2008, succeeding Nelson Mandela. A leading ANC diplomat in exile, he presided over steady economic growth and promoted an "African Renaissance", but his questioning of the scientific…

teatro-san-cassiano.s: The Teatro San Cassiano in Venice was the first public opera house in the world, opened in 1637 by the Tron family, where audiences paid for admission instead of attending by invitation at court. Its success led to many more commercial opera houses in Venice, which became the…

tintoretto.s: Tintoretto was a Venetian painter of the late Renaissance, famed for his speed, dramatic lighting and bold perspective. His greatest cycle fills the Scuola Grande di San Rocco in Venice, and his Paradise in the Doge's Palace is among the largest paintings on canvas.

titian.s: Titian was the greatest painter of 16th-century Venice. His altarpieces such as the Assumption in the Frari, portraits and mythologies won him the patronage of popes, Emperor Charles V and Philip II of Spain.

taninganwe.s: Taninganwe was king of the Restored Toungoo dynasty of Burma from 1714 to 1733. His reign saw the kingdom's decline accelerate: from the 1720s Manipuri cavalry raided the Burmese dry zone, Chiang Mai and other frontier territories broke away, and the court was unable to…

temple-of-athena-lindia.s: The Temple of Athena Lindia stands on the acropolis of Lindos on Rhodes, one of the most famous sanctuaries of the Greek world. The surviving Doric temple was rebuilt in the fourth century BCE after a fire in 392 BCE, within a complex of stairs, a monumental gateway and stoas…

theophilus-i-of-alexandria.s: Theophilus was Patriarch of Alexandria from 385 to 412. With imperial backing he led the campaign against paganism in the city, and in 391 the Serapeum, its greatest temple, was destroyed.

tabennisi.s: Tabennisi was a village on the Nile in Upper Egypt, near Dendera, where Pachomius founded the first Christian communal monastery in the 320s. The community grew quickly, and Pachomius organised a federation of monasteries under a common rule.

thebaid.s: The Thebaid was the southern region of ancient Egypt around Thebes, stretching from about Abydos to the First Cataract at Aswan. Under Roman rule it was an administrative district, the scene of a revolt against Roman taxation soon after the conquest, and from Diocletian's time…

terence.s: Terence, in full Publius Terentius Afer, was a Roman comic playwright, said to have been born in North Africa and brought to Rome as a slave. His six surviving comedies, adapted from Greek New Comedy, are known for refined language and careful characterisation.

tiberius-gracchus.s: Tiberius Gracchus, in full Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus, was a Roman tribune of the plebs in 133 BCE. He passed a law to redistribute public land to poor citizens over the Senate's opposition and then sought a second term.

tambov-rebellion.s: The Tambov Rebellion was a peasant uprising against Bolshevik rule in Tambov province, south-east of Moscow, in 1920–1921. Led by Alexander Antonov and provoked by forced grain requisitioning, it grew to tens of thousands of fighters.

tamagusuku-chokun.s: Tamagusuku Chōkun was a Ryukyuan official and playwright who created kumi odori, the classical dance-drama of Okinawa. As the official in charge of entertaining the Chinese investiture envoys, he staged his first plays for them in 1719.

tamaudun.s: Tamaudun is the royal mausoleum of the Second Shō dynasty of Ryukyu at Shuri on Okinawa, built in 1501 by King Shō Shin to receive the remains of his father Shō En. Cut into the rock and built of stone in imitation of a palace, it held the remains of later kings and queens.

tahmasp-i.s: Tahmasp I was the second shah of Safavid Iran, ruling from 1524 to 1576 after succeeding his father Ismail I as a boy. He survived years of Qizilbash factional strife, fended off repeated Ottoman invasions and agreed the Peace of Amasya with Suleiman the Magnificent in 1555,…

tasmola-culture.s: The Tasmola culture is an early Iron Age archaeological culture of central and northern Kazakhstan, dated to about the eighth to fourth centuries BCE. It is known from burial mounds, some joined to stone ridges known as 'kurgans with moustaches', containing weapons, horse…

tumshuq.s: Tumshuq is an ancient site near modern Tumxuk in the north-western Tarim Basin, Xinjiang. In the first millennium CE it was a Buddhist oasis town whose people wrote a Saka language, known as Tumshuqese, closely related to Khotanese.

tunnel-of-eupalinos.s: The Tunnel of Eupalinos is an aqueduct tunnel 1,036 metres long cut through Mount Kastro on Samos in the sixth century BCE, under the tyrant Polycrates. Dug from both ends at once under the engineer Eupalinos of Megara, it carried water to the ancient city on the site of…

timotheus-general.s: Timotheus was an Athenian general and statesman of the fourth century BCE, son of the admiral Conon. His campaigns expanded the Second Athenian League; he captured Samos from a Persian garrison in 365 BCE after a ten-month siege and took several towns in the northern Aegean.

ter-maharashtra.s: Ter is a village in Dharashiv (Osmanabad) district, Maharashtra, India, on the site of the ancient city of Tagara. In the early centuries CE Tagara was an important inland market of the Satavahana kingdom, named in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea as sending goods to the…

two-ewalds.s: The two Ewalds, called Ewald the Black and Ewald the Fair, were English priests who went as missionaries to the Old Saxons around 695. According to Bede they were killed by Saxons who feared the conversion of their chieftain, and their bodies were thrown into the Rhine.

thor.s: Thor was the Germanic god of thunder, known to the continental Saxons as Thunaer or Donar and to the English as Thunor. Armed with his hammer Mjolnir, he was the protector of gods and men against giants and the most widely worshipped god of the Viking Age in Scandinavia.

theodore-svetoslav.s: Theodore Svetoslav was tsar of Bulgaria from 1300 to 1322, son of George I Terter. Long a hostage of the Mongol warlord Nogai, he seized the throne after Nogai's fall and ended the Golden Horde's domination of Bulgaria.

tetraevangelion-of-ivan-alexander.s: The Tetraevangelion of Ivan Alexander is an illuminated manuscript of the four Gospels made in 1355–1356 for Tsar Ivan Alexander of Bulgaria. Written in Middle Bulgarian by the monk Simeon, it contains several hundred miniatures, including portraits of the tsar and his family,…

theodosius-of-tarnovo.s: Theodosius of Tarnovo was a Bulgarian monk and leading teacher of hesychasm, the Orthodox tradition of contemplative prayer. With the support of Tsar Ivan Alexander he founded the Kilifarevo Monastery near Tarnovo around 1350, which became a centre of learning and book copying.

trapezitsa.s: Trapezitsa is a fortified hill in Veliko Tarnovo, Bulgaria, facing the Tsarevets hill across the Yantra river. With Tsarevets it formed the core of Tarnovo, capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire from the late twelfth century until the Ottoman conquest of 1393.

tang-of-shang.s: Tang of Shang, also called Cheng Tang, was the founder of the Shang dynasty according to Chinese tradition. Histories such as Sima Qian's Shiji relate that he overthrew Jie, the tyrannical last king of the Xia, at the Battle of Mingtiao, with the help of his minister Yi Yin.

tufang.s: The Tufang were a people living to the north or north-west of the Shang state, probably in present-day Shanxi. Oracle-bone inscriptions from the reign of King Wu Ding often record their raids on Shang settlements and the king's campaigns against them, alongside wars with the…

trucial-oman-scouts.s: The Trucial Oman Scouts were a British-officered force raised in 1951 as the Trucial Oman Levies, with headquarters at Sharjah, to keep order in the Trucial States. Renamed in 1956, they took part in the Buraimi dispute and in operations in Oman in the late 1950s.

three-kingdoms-of-korea.s: The Three Kingdoms of Korea were Goguryeo, Baekje and Silla, which competed for control of the Korean peninsula and southern Manchuria from about the first century BCE until the seventh century CE. The Gaya confederacy also existed in the south until Silla absorbed it in 562.

talhae-of-silla.s: Talhae was the fourth ruler of Silla, traditionally reigning from 57 to 80 CE, and the founder of the Seok clan, one of the three lineages that held the Silla throne. Legend says he was born from an egg in a distant land and arrived by boat.

third-indochina-war.s: The Third Indochina War is the name given to the conflicts that followed the Vietnamese invasion of Cambodia in December 1978. Vietnam overthrew the Khmer Rouge regime and occupied the country for a decade, fighting Khmer Rouge and other resistance groups, while China attacked…

to-lam.s: Tô Lâm is a Vietnamese politician and career police officer who became general secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam in August 2024, after the death of Nguyen Phu Trong. As minister of public security from 2016 to 2024 he directed much of the party's anti-corruption…

ton-duc-thang.s: Tôn Đức Thắng was a Vietnamese communist revolutionary who succeeded Ho Chi Minh as president of North Vietnam in 1969 and became the first president of the reunified Socialist Republic of Vietnam in 1976, holding office until his death. A former mechanic and labour organiser,…

tarikh-al-fattash.s: The Tarikh al-Fattash is an Arabic chronicle of the western Sudan written in Timbuktu, traditionally attributed to Mahmud Kati and completed by a descendant, Ibn al-Mukhtar, in the seventeenth century. With the Tarikh al-Sudan it is the main written source for the history of…

thomas-francois-burgers.s: Thomas François Burgers was a Cape-born minister of the Dutch Reformed Church who served as president of the South African Republic from 1872 to 1877. He promoted a railway to Delagoa Bay, secular state schooling and the republic's first gold coins, but his plans outran its…

transvaal.s: The Transvaal is the region of north-eastern South Africa lying between the Vaal and Limpopo rivers. Settled by Voortrekkers from the 1830s, it formed the South African Republic, was annexed by Britain as the Transvaal Colony after the Second Boer War, and became the Transvaal…

treaty-on-the-creation-of-the-ussr.n: Treaty on the Creation of the USSR
treaty-on-the-creation-of-the-ussr.s: The Treaty on the Creation of the USSR, approved on 30 December 1922 by the First All-Union Congress of Soviets, united the Russian SFSR, the Ukrainian SSR, the Byelorussian SSR and the Transcaucasian SFSR into the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. Together with the…

taygetus.s: Taygetus is the highest mountain range of the Peloponnese in Greece, rising to 2,404 metres at Profitis Ilias. It runs north to south between Laconia and Messenia and towers over the site of ancient Sparta to the west.

tyrtaeus.s: Tyrtaeus was a Greek elegiac poet who lived in Sparta in the mid-seventh century BCE, during the Second Messenian War. His surviving poems exhort Spartan citizens to stand firm in the battle line and die for their city, and one, the Eunomia, praises the Spartan order given by…

telaga-batu-inscription.s: The Telaga Batu inscription is a large stone found at Telaga Batu in Palembang, Sumatra, inscribed in Old Malay in the late seventh century during the early Srivijaya period. Crowned by seven cobra heads and with a spout for water, it carries a long oath of loyalty with curses…

tonglushan.s: Tonglüshan is an ancient copper mine near Daye in Hubei, China, worked from about the late second millennium BCE to the Han dynasty. Discovered in 1973, it preserves shafts, timber supports, tools and smelting furnaces, and the slag heaps suggest that tens of thousands of…

tsinghua-bamboo-slips.s: The Tsinghua Bamboo Slips are a collection of about 2,500 bamboo strips inscribed in the Chu script in the Warring States period, acquired by Tsinghua University in Beijing in 2008 after being looted from a tomb. Radiocarbon-dated to about 300 BCE, they include lost chapters…

tian-chang.s: Tian Chang, also called Tian Heng or Tian Chengzi, was a minister of the State of Qi from the Tian (or Chen) family. In 481 BCE he killed Duke Jian of Qi, installed Duke Ping and took control of the government, greatly enlarging his family's lands.

treaty-of-melno.s: The Treaty of Melno was signed on 27 September 1422 near Lake Melno between the Teutonic Order and the allied Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania, ending the Gollub War. The Order gave up its claims to Samogitia permanently, and the treaty fixed the border between…

treaty-of-raciaz.s: The Treaty of Raciąż was signed in May 1404 between the Teutonic Order and the Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania. It confirmed the Order's possession of Samogitia, which linked its lands in Prussia and Livonia, and allowed Poland to buy back Dobrzyń Land, which…

treaty-of-soldin.s: The Treaty of Soldin was signed on 12 June 1309 at Soldin, present-day Myślibórz in Poland. The margraves of Brandenburg sold their claims to Pomerelia, with Danzig, Dirschau and Schwetz, to the Teutonic Order for 10,000 marks.

traiphum-phra-ruang.s: The Traiphum Phra Ruang, or Three Worlds According to King Ruang, is a Thai treatise on Buddhist cosmology traditionally attributed to King Li Thai of Sukhothai and dated to 1345. Drawing on Pali sources, it describes the realms of existence, the workings of karma and the…

tausug.s: The Tausug are a Muslim people of the Sulu archipelago in the southern Philippines, with communities also in Sabah and other parts of Mindanao. Their name means people of the current.

tawi-tawi.s: Tawi-Tawi is the southernmost province of the Philippines, a group of islands at the south-western end of the Sulu archipelago, close to Borneo. Its main island is Tawi-Tawi and its capital Bongao.

tangerang.s: Tangerang is a large city in Banten province, Indonesia, on the Cisadane River immediately west of Jakarta and part of the Greater Jakarta metropolitan area. In the early sixteenth century it was one of the ports of the Sunda Kingdom listed by Tomé Pires.

thandile.s: Thandile, known as LaZidze, was a daughter of the Ndwandwe king Zwide who married Sobhuza I, founder of the Swazi Kingdom, sealing peace with her father's people. As mother of Mswati II she became queen mother on her husband's death and acted as a powerful regent during her…

treaty-of-stolbovo.s: The Treaty of Stolbovo, signed on 27 February 1617, ended the Ingrian War between Sweden and Russia. Sweden returned Novgorod, which it had occupied, but kept Ingria and Kexholm, cutting Russia off from the Baltic Sea.

tanzania-zambia-railway.s: The Tanzania–Zambia Railway is a railway of about 1,860 kilometres from Dar es Salaam to Kapiri Mposhi in Zambia, built between 1970 and 1975 with an interest-free loan, engineers and workers from China. It gave landlocked Zambia an outlet to the sea that avoided white-ruled…

the-merchant-of-venice.s: The Merchant of Venice is a play by William Shakespeare, written in the late 1590s. It tells of the Venetian merchant Antonio, who borrows money from the Jewish moneylender Shylock on the bond of a pound of his flesh, and of Portia, who saves him in court.

tanganyika-rifles.s: The Tanganyika Rifles was the army of newly independent Tanganyika, formed from battalions of the British colonial King's African Rifles. In January 1964 its soldiers mutinied over pay and the slow replacement of their British officers by Africans, and President Julius Nyerere…

tanzania-peoples-defence-force.s: The Tanzania People's Defence Force is the armed forces of Tanzania, created in 1964 after the mutiny of the Tanganyika Rifles to replace the old colonial-style army with a force loyal to the ruling party. It supported liberation movements in southern Africa, defeated Idi…

temple-of-the-feathered-serpent.s: The Feathered Serpent Pyramid is the third-largest pyramid at Teotihuacan, built around 200 to 250 CE inside the Ciudadela. Its facades bear sculpted heads of feathered serpents alternating with headdress motifs.

tepantitla.s: Tepantitla is an apartment compound at Teotihuacan, east of the Pyramid of the Sun, famous for its well-preserved murals. Its paintings show a storm god or goddess with priests and a lively scene of small figures playing, swimming and singing in a watery landscape, often…

tetitla.s: Tetitla is an elite apartment compound on the western side of Teotihuacan, notable for its many rooms decorated with murals. Its paintings include figures of the female deity often called the Great Goddess, jaguars, priests casting offerings and some motifs in a Maya style.

thin-orange-ware.s: Thin Orange ware is a fine, thin-walled orange pottery produced in southern Puebla, in central Mexico, during the Classic period, roughly the third to the sixth centuries CE. Distributed through Teotihuacan's exchange networks, it is found throughout the city and as far away…

tlaloc.s: Tlaloc was the Aztec god of rain, storms and agricultural fertility, recognisable by his goggle eyes and fangs. A storm god with similar features was already worshipped at Teotihuacan in the first centuries CE, and at Tenochtitlan Tlaloc shared the Templo Mayor with the war…

takdra-lukhong.s: Takdra Lukhong was a Tibetan minister and general under the emperor Trisong Detsen. He is commemorated by the Zhol pillar in Lhasa, one of the oldest surviving inscribed pillars in Tibet, which records his services, including the Tibetan campaign that briefly captured the Tang…

thonmi-sambhota.s: Thonmi Sambhota was, according to Tibetan tradition, a minister of the emperor Songtsen Gampo who was sent to India in the seventh century and devised the Tibetan script on the model of an Indian alphabet, as well as the first Tibetan grammar. Some modern scholars doubt his…

thrimalo.s: Thrimalö was the wife of the Tibetan emperor Mangsong Mangtsen and one of the most powerful women of imperial Tibet. As queen mother and grandmother of emperors she dominated the court for decades, and after the death of her son Tridu Songtsen in 704 she governed as regent for…

tridu-songtsen.s: Tridu Songtsen was emperor of Tibet from 676 to 704. Coming to the throne as an infant, he grew up under the domination of the Gar clan, which he destroyed in 698 and 699, restoring royal power.

tomsk.s: Tomsk is a city on the Tom River in western Siberia, founded as a fortress in 1604 by order of Tsar Boris Godunov. It grew as a trading and administrative centre on the route across Siberia and became known as the 'Siberian Athens' after Tomsk University, the first in Siberia,…

treaty-of-nerchinsk.s: The Treaty of Nerchinsk, signed on 27 August 1689 at Nerchinsk in eastern Siberia, was the first treaty between Russia and Qing China. Following clashes over the Amur, including the Qing sieges of Albazin, it fixed the frontier along the Argun River and the Stanovoy Range,…

truce-of-yam-zapolsky.s: The Truce of Yam-Zapolsky was signed on 15 January 1582 between Russia and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, ending their part in the Livonian War after Stephen Báthory's campaigns and siege of Pskov. Ivan IV gave up his conquests in Livonia and Polotsk, while…

tito-okello.s: Tito Okello was a Ugandan army officer who became head of state after the coup of July 1985 that ousted Milton Obote. An Acholi who had served in the King's African Rifles, he had commanded Ugandan exile forces in the war against Idi Amin and later headed Obote's army.

third-fitna.s: The Third Fitna was a series of civil wars in the Umayyad Caliphate that began in 744 with the overthrow and killing of al-Walid II by his cousin Yazid III. Successive caliphs fell or died within months, revolts broke out across Syria, Iraq and the east, and Marwan II restored…

trucial-states.s: The Trucial States were the sheikhdoms of the southern Persian Gulf coast that signed maritime truces with Britain from 1820 onwards, culminating in the Perpetual Maritime Truce of 1853 and the Exclusive Agreement of 1892, which made them British protectorates in all but name.…

the-beatles.s: The Beatles were an English rock band formed in Liverpool in 1960, with John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and, from 1962, Ringo Starr. Their records and the Beatlemania of the mid-1960s made them the best-selling musical act in history and a symbol of Britain's…

the-blitz.s: The Blitz was the German bombing campaign against British cities from September 1940 to May 1941. London was bombed on 57 consecutive nights at its start, and ports and industrial centres such as Coventry, Liverpool and Plymouth were heavily hit; more than 40,000 civilians…

tony-blair.s: Tony Blair is a British Labour politician who was prime minister of the United Kingdom from 1997 to 2007, the party's longest-serving holder of the office. Leading New Labour to three election victories, he introduced devolution for Scotland and Wales, helped secure the Good…

the-crystal-palace.s: The Crystal Palace was a building of cast iron and glass designed by Joseph Paxton to house the Great Exhibition in Hyde Park, London, in 1851. After the exhibition it was rebuilt in enlarged form at Sydenham in south London, where it served for exhibitions and entertainment…

twenty-sixth-amendment-of-the-constituti.n: Twenty-sixth Amendment of the Constitution of India
twenty-sixth-amendment-of-the-constituti.s: The Twenty-sixth Amendment of the Constitution of India, enacted in December 1971 under Indira Gandhi, abolished the privy purses paid to the former rulers of the princely states and ended the official recognition of their titles and privileges. These guarantees had been given…

townshend-acts.s: The Townshend Acts were a series of laws passed by the British Parliament in 1767 and 1768, named after the chancellor of the exchequer Charles Townshend, that imposed duties on glass, lead, paint, paper and tea imported into the American colonies. Colonial boycotts led to the…

tachira.s: Táchira is a state in the Andes of western Venezuela, on the border with Colombia, with its capital at San Cristóbal. A coffee-growing region, it produced the Andean leaders who dominated Venezuela from 1899 to 1958, among them Cipriano Castro, Juan Vicente Gómez, Eleazar…

trienio-adeco.s: The Trienio Adeco was the three-year period from October 1945 to November 1948 when Venezuela was governed by Democratic Action (AD), whose members were known as adecos. Brought to power by a civilian–military coup against Isaías Medina Angarita, the party introduced universal…

treaty-of-coche.s: The Treaty of Coche was the agreement signed in April 1863 at the Coche estate near Caracas that ended the Federal War in Venezuela. Negotiated between representatives of José Antonio Páez's government and of the federalist leader Juan Crisóstomo Falcón, it handed power to a…

third-council-of-lima.s: The Third Council of Lima was a church council held in Lima in 1582–1583 under Archbishop Toribio de Mogrovejo. It set the rules of the Catholic Church in South America for centuries, requiring that indigenous people be taught in their own languages, and commissioned a…

tirumala-deva-raya.s: Tirumala Deva Raya was the brother of Aliya Rama Raya and founder of the Aravidu dynasty, the last ruling house of the Vijayanagara Empire. After the defeat at Talikota in 1565 he withdrew with the treasury and the nominal emperor Sadashiva Raya to Penukonda, and around 1570…

tungabhadra-river.s: The Tungabhadra is a river of southern India, formed by the junction of the Tunga and Bhadra rivers in Karnataka, that flows north-east for about 530 km to join the Krishna in Andhra Pradesh. Vijayanagara (Hampi), the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, was built on its…

tretyakov-gallery.s: The Tretyakov Gallery is an art museum in Moscow holding the world's foremost collection of Russian art. It grew from the collection of the merchant Pavel Tretyakov, who began buying works in 1856 and gave the gallery to the city of Moscow in 1892.

tuoba.s: The Tuoba were a clan of the Xianbei people who founded the Northern Wei dynasty, which ruled northern China from 386 to 534. Moving south from the Greater Khingan region, they established the state of Dai in the fourth century and reunified northern China by 439.

tian-yu.s: Tian Yu was a Chinese general and frontier official of the Cao Wei state during the Three Kingdoms period. As an officer on the northern frontier he dealt with the Wuhuan and Xianbei, and he is remembered for setting rival Xianbei chiefs against one another to contain the…

tonghui-canal.s: The Tonghui Canal was a canal designed by the engineer Guo Shoujing and completed in 1293, linking the Yuan capital Dadu (Beijing) with Tongzhou and the northern end of the Grand Canal. By supplying it with spring water from the western hills, Guo allowed grain barges to sail…

tillya-tepe.s: Tillya Tepe is an archaeological site in Jowzjan province, northern Afghanistan, where Viktor Sarianidi excavated six rich graves in 1978–1979. They held some 20,000 gold objects, the 'Bactrian Gold', mixing steppe, Greek, Iranian and Indian styles, probably belonging to nomad…

tanah-datar.s: Tanah Datar is a regency in the highlands of West Sumatra, Indonesia, with its seat at Batusangkar. It is one of the three original heartlands (luhak) of the Minangkabau and contains Pagaruyung, the seat of the Minangkabau kings, and many traditional villages.

trans-iranian-railway.s: The Trans-Iranian Railway is a railway built between 1927 and 1938 under Reza Shah, linking the Caspian Sea with the Persian Gulf by way of Tehran. Financed by taxes on tea and sugar rather than foreign loans, it crosses the Alborz and Zagros mountains on hundreds of bridges…

taman-siswa.s: Taman Siswa ('Garden of Pupils') is an Indonesian school movement founded by Ki Hajar Dewantara in Yogyakarta on 3 July 1922. Combining Javanese culture with modern teaching methods and refusing Dutch subsidies, it trained a generation of nationalists and spread across the…

tenagino-probus.s: Tenagino Probus was the Roman prefect of Egypt in 270. When Zenobia of Palmyra sent her general Zabdas into Egypt, Probus, returning from operations against pirates, fought the Palmyrenes and at first drove them back, but was defeated near Babylon (Old Cairo) and took his own…

tivaradeva.s: Tivaradeva was a king of the Panduvamshi dynasty of Dakshina Kosala, in modern Chhattisgarh, who reigned in the late 6th century. Known from his copper-plate grants, he united the region, styled himself lord of all Kosala and made Shripura, modern Sirpur, his capital.

thewa.s: Thewa is a jewellery technique from Pratapgarh in Rajasthan, India, in which finely worked sheet gold is fused onto coloured glass. The gold is engraved with openwork scenes of hunting, mythology or court life, and the glass beneath is usually green, red or blue.

tarikh-al-sudan.s: The Tarikh al-Sudan is a chronicle of West Africa written in Arabic at Timbuktu by Abd al-Rahman al-Sadi and completed around 1655. It records the history of the Songhai Empire, the Moroccan conquest of 1591 and the rule of the pashas, as well as the lives of the scholars of…

tepelene.s: Tepelenë is a town in southern Albania on the Vjosa river, in Gjirokastër County. It was the birthplace and family seat of Ali Pasha, who ruled much of the western Balkans from Ioannina and rebuilt its castle.

trikala.s: Trikala is a city in western Thessaly in Greece, on the Lithaios river. It stands on the site of ancient Trikke, famed as an early cult centre of Asclepius.

taita.s: Taita was a king of Palistin, a Neo-Hittite kingdom of northern Syria, in the 11th or 10th century BCE. He is known from Luwian hieroglyphic inscriptions, among them one in the temple of the storm god on the citadel of Aleppo, which name him as hero and king of Palistin.

treaty-of-lircay.s: The Treaty of Lircay was signed on 3 May 1814 on the banks of the Lircay river near Talca between the Chilean patriot government and the royalist commander Gabino Gaínza, with the British naval officer James Hillyar as mediator. It provided for the withdrawal of royalist…

theodora-wife-of-theophilos.s: Theodora was a Byzantine empress, wife of Emperor Theophilos, who ruled as regent for their young son Michael III from 842 to 856. In 843 she restored the veneration of icons, ending the period of Iconoclasm, an event the Orthodox Church celebrates as the Triumph of Orthodoxy.

theodora-wife-of-justinian-i.s: Theodora was a Byzantine empress, wife of Emperor Justinian I and one of the most influential women in Byzantine history. A former actress, she married Justinian around 525 and became empress in 527; during the Nika riots of 532 she is said to have persuaded him not to flee.

thulare-i.s: Thulare was king of the Pedi in the north-east of present-day South Africa in the late 18th and early 19th centuries. Through conquest and alliances he made the Pedi the paramount power over many smaller chiefdoms of the Steelpoort and Olifants valleys.

tome-pires.s: Tomé Pires was a Portuguese apothecary and writer who lived at Malacca from 1512 to 1515. His Suma Oriental, written there, is the most detailed European account of the trade and ports of maritime Asia in the early 16th century, describing lands from the Red Sea to Japan.

theodoros-kolokotronis.s: Theodoros Kolokotronis was the leading military commander of the Greek War of Independence in the Peloponnese. A former klepht who had served with British forces in the Ionian Islands, he directed the siege and capture of Tripolitsa in 1821 and destroyed the Ottoman army of…

tripoli-greece.s: Tripoli, known in Ottoman times as Tripolitsa, is a city in the central Peloponnese of Greece and the capital of Arcadia. Under Ottoman rule it was the seat of the pasha of the Morea.

todor-zhivkov.s: Todor Zhivkov was the communist leader of Bulgaria for 35 years, first secretary of the Bulgarian Communist Party from 1954 to 1989 and head of state from 1971. He kept Bulgaria the most loyal Soviet ally in Eastern Europe, oversaw rapid industrialisation and in the 1980s led…

tatobem.s: Tatobem was the grand sachem of the Pequot in the early 17th century, when the nation dominated the wampum trade of southern New England and traded with the Dutch on the Connecticut River. After a quarrel over trade at the Dutch post, the Dutch seized and killed him around…

treaty-of-hartford-1638.s: The Treaty of Hartford was signed in September 1638 by the Connecticut colony and the Mohegan and Narragansett sachems after the Pequot War. It declared the Pequot nation dissolved, divided the surviving captives between the Mohegan and the Narragansett, and forbade the use of…

tuanku-syed-sirajuddin.s: Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin is the Raja of Perlis, a Malaysian state ruled by the Jamalullail family, who succeeded his father Tuanku Syed Putra in 2000. Under Malaysia's system of rotating monarchy he was elected by the Conference of Rulers and served as the twelfth Yang…

treaty-of-nvarsak.s: The Treaty of Nvarsak was concluded in 484 between the Armenian leader Vahan Mamikonian and the Sasanian Empire after years of Armenian revolt. It granted the Armenians freedom to practise Christianity, removed Zoroastrian fire temples from Armenia and allowed the nobility to…

tour-de-vesone.s: The Tour de Vésone is the surviving round cella of a Gallo-Roman temple in Périgueux, France, built in the 2nd century CE in the Roman town of Vesunna. About 24 metres high, it was dedicated to the town's tutelary goddess Vesunna.

tsongkhapa.s: Tsongkhapa was a Tibetan Buddhist monk and scholar from Amdo whose teaching founded the Gelug school. He stressed monastic discipline and systematic study of philosophy, began the Great Prayer Festival in Lhasa in 1409 and in the same year founded Ganden Monastery.

talos.s: Talos is a bronze giant of Greek mythology who guarded Crete, striding around the island three times a day and hurling stones at approaching ships. In the story of the Argonauts he was killed when Medea caused the single vein that held his life to be opened at the ankle.

thepphiphit.s: Thepphiphit was a Siamese prince, a son of King Borommakot of Ayutthaya, who was exiled to Ceylon after involvement in court intrigue. He later returned to Siam, and after the fall of Ayutthaya in 1767 he set himself up as ruler at Phimai on the Khorat Plateau.

tatiana-proskouriakoff.s: Tatiana Proskouriakoff was a Russian-born American archaeologist and architectural artist who transformed the study of Maya writing. In a paper of 1960 she showed that the dated monuments of Piedras Negras recorded the births, accessions and deaths of rulers, proving that Maya…

truso.s: Truso was a Viking Age trading settlement on the shore of Lake Drużno near Elbląg in northern Poland, active from the 8th to the 10th century. The traveller Wulfstan, whose voyage from Hedeby is recorded in the Old English Orosius, described sailing there around 890.

temple-of-athena-paestum.s: The Temple of Athena at Paestum in southern Italy is a Doric temple built around 500 BCE in the Greek colony of Poseidonia. Long misnamed the Temple of Ceres, it stands on high ground in the north of the city and combines a Doric exterior with Ionic columns in its porch.

tomb-of-the-diver.s: The Tomb of the Diver is a Greek stone cist grave of about 470 BCE found in 1968 near Paestum in southern Italy. Its five painted slabs show a symposium on the walls and, on the lid, a young man diving into water, a rare surviving example of Greek painting from the Classical…

treaty-of-middle-plantation.s: The Treaty of Middle Plantation of 1677 was concluded between the English Crown and Native peoples of Virginia, among them the Pamunkey under Cockacoeske, after the violence of Bacon's Rebellion. It made the tribes subjects of the Crown with guaranteed land rights and laid the…

the-mountain-wreath.s: The Mountain Wreath is a verse drama by Petar II Petrović-Njegoš, prince-bishop of Montenegro, published in Vienna in 1847. Set around 1700, it depicts the Montenegrin struggle against the Ottomans and the killing of local converts to Islam, and it is regarded as a masterpiece…

trentino.s: Trentino is a mountainous region of northern Italy in the upper Adige valley, with Trento as its capital, today an autonomous province. For most of the Middle Ages and early modern period much of it was ruled by the prince-bishops of Trent.

thopia-family.s: The Thopia were an Albanian noble family of central Albania in the late Middle Ages. Its best-known member, Karl Thopia, took Durrës from the Angevins in 1368 and ruled as Prince of Albania until 1388.

tughshada.s: Tughshada was the Bukhar Khudah, the local ruler of Bukhara, in the early 8th century. After the Arab general Qutayba ibn Muslim took Bukhara in 709 he installed the young Tughshada as a vassal prince.

tashkent.s: Tashkent is the capital and largest city of Uzbekistan, in an oasis watered by the Chirchiq river. Known in the early Middle Ages as Chach or Shash, it was a trading city between the farmland of Transoxiana and the steppe.

transfiguration-cathedral-chernihiv.s: The Transfiguration Cathedral in Chernihiv, Ukraine, is one of the oldest surviving churches of Kievan Rus'. It was begun in the 1030s by Prince Mstislav of Chernigov, the brother of Yaroslav the Wise, who was buried there in 1036.

transfiguration-cathedral-pereslavl-zale.s: The Transfiguration Cathedral in Pereslavl-Zalessky, Russia, was begun in 1152 by Prince Yuri Dolgoruky and completed in 1157 by his son Andrei Bogolyubsky. A simple single-domed church of white limestone, it is one of the oldest surviving buildings in north-eastern Russia and…

trevoux.s: Trévoux is a small town on the Saône in the Ain department of eastern France, north of Lyon. It was the capital of the sovereign principality of Dombes, where the princes kept a mint, and its parliament moved there in 1696.

terebovlia.s: Terebovlia is a town in Ternopil Oblast, western Ukraine, on the Hnizna river. First mentioned in 1097, it was the seat of Prince Vasylko Rostyslavych, whose blinding that year is one of the best-known stories of the Primary Chronicle.

taksony.s: Taksony was Grand Prince of the Hungarians from about 955 to about 970, the period after the defeat at the Lechfeld that ended the Magyar raids on western Europe. A grandson of Árpád, he is said to have settled Pecheneg and Muslim groups in Hungary and asked the papacy for a…

telavi.s: Telavi is a town in eastern Georgia, the main centre of Kakheti, on the slopes above the Alazani valley. It was a seat of the kings of Kakheti-Hereti in the 11th century and later of the Kingdom of Kakheti, and the palace of King Erekle II, built in the 18th century, survives…

tusheti.s: Tusheti is a remote mountain region of north-eastern Georgia on the northern slopes of the Greater Caucasus, bordering Chechnya and Dagestan. Its people, the Tush, lived from sheep herding, moving their flocks between summer pastures and the lowlands of Kakheti, and built…

tartu.s: Tartu is the second-largest city of Estonia, on the Emajõgi river. An Estonian hillfort there was taken by Yaroslav the Wise around 1030 and named Yuryev, and in 1224 the German crusaders captured it, making it the seat of the Bishopric of Dorpat.

trubizh.s: The Trubizh is a river in Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine, a left tributary of the Dnieper about 110 km long. The medieval town of Pereyaslavl, modern Pereiaslav, stood on it, and the Primary Chronicle sets at its ford the tale of the young Rus' champion who defeated a Pecheneg warrior…

themistoklis-sofoulis.s: Themistoklis Sofoulis was a Greek politician from Samos. An archaeologist by training, he led the rising on Samos in 1912 that expelled the last Ottoman garrison and brought the island's union with Greece.

theresienstadt-ghetto.s: The Theresienstadt Ghetto was a Nazi ghetto and concentration camp in the fortress town of Terezín in northern Bohemia, in use from November 1941 to May 1945. Presented in propaganda as a model Jewish settlement, it held about 140,000 Jews, mainly from Bohemia, Moravia,…

thinis.s: Thinis was an ancient Egyptian city in Upper Egypt near Abydos, whose exact site has not been found, though it probably lay near modern Girga. Egyptian tradition, reported by Manetho, made it the home of the first kings who unified Egypt, and it was the capital of the eighth…

tomb-u-j.s: Tomb U-j is a Predynastic royal tomb in Cemetery U at Abydos in Upper Egypt, excavated by Günter Dreyer in 1988 and dated to about 3320 BCE. Its twelve chambers held hundreds of jars, many of them wine jars imported from the Levant, and many small bone and ivory labels incised…

tomochichi.s: Tomochichi was the leader of the Yamacraw, a small Creek-affiliated band living on a bluff above the Savannah River. He welcomed James Oglethorpe in 1733, allowing the founding of Savannah, and helped negotiate a treaty with the Lower Creek.

trustees-for-the-establishment-of-the-co.n: Trustees for the Establishment of the Colony of Georgia in America
trustees-for-the-establishment-of-the-co.s: The Trustees for the Establishment of the Colony of Georgia in America were the board, led by James Oglethorpe, that received a royal charter from George II in 1732 to found and govern Georgia. They aimed to settle the deserving poor and to shield South Carolina from Spanish…

thomas-gage.s: Thomas Gage was a British army officer who served as commander-in-chief in North America from 1763 to 1775 and as the last royal governor of Massachusetts from 1774. His attempt to seize colonial military stores at Concord led to the Battles of Lexington and Concord in April…

torrens-title.s: Torrens title is a system of land registration in which the state keeps a central register of land ownership and guarantees the title of the registered owner. It was introduced in South Australia in 1858 by Robert Torrens, replacing the complex old system of tracing chains of…

trinidad.s: Trinidad is the larger of the two main islands of Trinidad and Tobago, lying just off the Orinoco delta of Venezuela. Sighted by Columbus in 1498, it remained a thinly settled Spanish colony until French Catholic planters arrived after 1783, and Britain captured it in 1797.

thomas-scott-orangeman.s: Thomas Scott was an Irish-born Protestant labourer and member of the Orange Order who opposed Louis Riel's provisional government at Red River. Captured during an armed counter-movement, he was tried by a Métis tribunal and executed by firing squad on 4 March 1870.

theodore-roosevelt.s: Theodore Roosevelt was the 26th president of the United States, from 1901 to 1909. A hero of the Spanish–American War, he pursued an assertive 'big stick' policy in the Americas, backing Panama's secession from Colombia in 1903 to build the Panama Canal and claiming a right to…

titus.s: Titus was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 CE, the elder son of Vespasian and the second emperor of the Flavian dynasty. In 70 he captured Jerusalem after a long siege, destroying the city and the Second Temple, an event commemorated by the Arch of Titus in Rome.

titus-saint.s: Saint Titus was an early Christian missionary and companion of the apostle Paul, to whom the New Testament Letter to Titus is addressed. According to tradition he became the first bishop of Crete, and he is the island's patron saint.

tianjin.s: Tianjin is a major port city in northern China, about 120 km south-east of Beijing near the Bohai Sea. After the Treaties of Tianjin of 1858 and the Convention of Peking of 1860 it became a treaty port, with concessions held by several foreign powers.

trinity-cathedral-pskov.s: The Trinity Cathedral in Pskov, Russia, is the city's main Orthodox church, standing inside the Krom citadel. Tradition places the first church on the site in the 10th century, and the present building dates from the 1680s and 1690s.

thondaiman-dynasty.s: The Thondaiman dynasty ruled Pudukkottai in Tamil Nadu from the late 17th century until the state joined India in 1948. Raghunatha Raya Thondaiman founded the principality around 1686, and the family's support for the British in the Carnatic wars kept it independent of…

tzintzuntzan.s: Tzintzuntzan was the capital of the Purépecha (Tarascan) state on the north-eastern shore of Lake Pátzcuaro in Michoacán, western Mexico. By the 15th century it had become the political and religious centre of the kingdom, with tens of thousands of inhabitants and monumental…

tabaristan.s: Tabaristan was the medieval name of the Caspian province of northern Iran, roughly modern Mazandaran, a land of forested mountains and coastal lowlands. Shielded by the Alborz, it kept Zoroastrian rulers such as the Dabuyids for over a century after the Arab conquest, and…

teelhunu.s: Te'elhunu was a queen and priestess of the Arabs of Qedar in the early 7th century BCE. Her forces were defeated by Sennacherib of Assyria, who around 690 BCE seized the oasis of Adummatu and carried her, together with the images of the Arab gods, to Nineveh.

tianshui.s: Tianshui is a city in south-eastern Gansu, China, in the valley of the Wei River. It lies close to the region where the State of Qin had its origins, and was later a frontier prefecture on the roads to the west, briefly the capital of Xue Ju's Qin state in 617–618.

treaty-of-lal-dhang.s: The Treaty of Lal Dhang was concluded in October 1774 between Shuja-ud-Daula, Nawab of Awadh, and the Rohilla chief Faizullah Khan at the end of the First Rohilla War. After Awadh and East India Company troops had defeated the Rohillas at Miranpur Katra, Faizullah Khan, who…

tangata-manu.s: The Tangata manu ('bird man') was the winner of a yearly competition on Rapa Nui (Easter Island), centred on the ceremonial village of Orongo. Each spring men representing rival chiefs swam to the islet of Motu Nui to wait for the first sooty tern egg; the chief whose man…

toompea.s: Toompea is a limestone hill in the centre of Tallinn, Estonia, rising above the medieval Lower Town. An Estonian stronghold stood there before the Danish conquest of 1219, when Valdemar II built a castle on it.

thomas-douglas-5th-earl-of-selkirk.s: Thomas Douglas, 5th Earl of Selkirk, was a Scottish peer who sponsored settlements of emigrant Highlanders in British North America. In 1811 he obtained a huge land grant from the Hudson's Bay Company and founded the Red River Colony, which brought him into violent conflict…

tabula-amalphitana.s: The Tabula Amalphitana is a medieval code of maritime law compiled in the Republic of Amalfi, probably between the 11th and 13th centuries. Its chapters regulate relations between shipowners, merchants and sailors, including shares in profits and liability for losses.

two-towers-bologna.s: The Two Towers, the Asinelli and the Garisenda, are medieval towers in the centre of Bologna, Italy, and the city's best-known landmarks. Built in the early 12th century by noble families, they are survivors of the many towers raised in the commune.

tirana.s: Tirana is the capital and largest city of Albania, in the centre of the country. Traditionally founded as a town by the Ottoman notable Sulejman Pasha in 1614, it was chosen as the capital by the Congress of Lushnjë in 1920.

tomas-guardia-gutierrez.s: Tomás Guardia Gutiérrez was a Costa Rican general who seized power in a coup in 1870 and dominated the country until his death in 1882. He issued the long-lasting constitution of 1871, abolished the death penalty in 1882 and began the railway to the Caribbean port of Limón.

taucheira.s: Taucheira was an ancient Greek city on the coast of Cyrenaica in eastern Libya, founded in the 7th or 6th century BCE. One of the cities of the Pentapolis, it was renamed Arsinoe under the Ptolemies and was later refortified under Justinian.

theodorus-of-cyrene.s: Theodorus of Cyrene was a Greek mathematician of the 5th century BCE, a teacher of Plato and of Theaetetus. In Plato's dialogue Theaetetus he is credited with showing that the square roots of the non-square numbers from 3 to 17 are irrational.

theodorus-of-samos.s: Theodorus of Samos was a Greek architect, sculptor and metalworker of the 6th century BCE. Ancient writers credit him, with Rhoecus, with the great temple of Hera on Samos and with pioneering the casting of bronze statues, and Herodotus names him as the maker of the ring of…

thibron.s: Thibron was a Spartan mercenary commander who, after murdering Harpalus in Crete in 324 BCE, took over his mercenary army and crossed to Cyrenaica. He fought Cyrene and its neighbours for control of the region until Ophellas, sent by Ptolemy I, defeated him in 322 BCE.

treaty-of-shimonoseki.s: The Treaty of Shimonoseki, signed on 17 April 1895, ended the First Sino-Japanese War. China recognised the independence of Korea, ceded Taiwan, the Penghu Islands and the Liaodong Peninsula to Japan and paid a large indemnity, though the Triple Intervention of Russia, Germany…

tonton-macoute.s: The Tonton Macoute was a paramilitary force created by François Duvalier in Haiti in 1959, officially named the Volunteers for National Security from 1962. Answerable only to the president, its members terrorised opponents through murder, torture and extortion under both…

treaty-of-tartu-finland-russia.s: The Treaty of Tartu between Finland and Soviet Russia, signed on 14 October 1920 in the Estonian town of Tartu, fixed the border between the two states after the Finnish Civil War and the volunteer expeditions into Russian territory. Finland gained the Petsamo area on the…

transkei.s: Transkei was a Bantustan, or homeland, for Xhosa-speaking people in the Eastern Cape region of South Africa, with its capital at Umtata (Mthatha). It received self-government in 1963 and in 1976 became the first homeland declared independent under apartheid, a status no other…

tarnobrzeg.s: Tarnobrzeg is a town in south-eastern Poland on the Vistula, in the Subcarpathian Voivodeship. Founded in the late 16th century by the Tarnowski family, it lay in Austrian Galicia from 1772 to 1918.

texan-santa-fe-expedition.s: The Texan Santa Fe Expedition was a commercial and military venture sent by President Mirabeau B. Lamar of the Republic of Texas in 1841 to bring the Santa Fe trade and eastern New Mexico, which Texas claimed, under Texan control. About 320 men crossed the plains, suffered…

thomas-upington.s: Sir Thomas Upington was an Irish-born lawyer and politician who was Prime Minister of the Cape Colony from 1884 to 1886. He later served as attorney general and as a judge of the Cape Supreme Court.

thalun.s: Thalun was king of Burma's Restored Toungoo dynasty from 1629 to 1648. He moved the capital from Pegu back to Ava in 1635, ordered a great revenue inquest of the kingdom and organised royal service groups to supply soldiers and labour.

tyrifjorden.s: Tyrifjorden is a large lake in Buskerud, eastern Norway, north-west of Oslo. Despite its name it is a freshwater lake, not a fjord.

tsang.s: Tsang is a historical region of west-central Tibet along the Yarlung Tsangpo river, with Shigatse and Gyantse as its main towns. Together with Ü to the east it formed the heartland of central Tibet.

treaty-of-ponche-verde.s: The Treaty of Ponche Verde, agreed on 1 March 1845, ended the Ragamuffin War between the Empire of Brazil and the rebel Riograndense Republic. Negotiated with the imperial commander Luís Alves de Lima e Silva, it reincorporated Rio Grande do Sul into the empire, granted the…

todai-ji.s: Tōdai-ji is a Buddhist temple in Nara, Japan, built on the orders of Emperor Shōmu as the head of the state temples of the provinces. Its Great Buddha Hall houses a colossal bronze statue of the Buddha Vairocana, dedicated in 752.

thagaste.s: Thagaste was a Roman town in Numidia, on the site of modern Souk Ahras in north-eastern Algeria. It is best known as the birthplace of Augustine of Hippo in 354, who returned there after his conversion to found a religious community before becoming bishop of Hippo.

timgad.s: Timgad, the Roman Thamugadi, is a ruined city in north-eastern Algeria, founded by Trajan around 100 CE as a colony for veterans of the Third Augustan Legion. Its almost perfect grid plan, forum, theatre, library and arch of Trajan make it one of the best-preserved Roman…

twelve-tables.s: The Twelve Tables were the earliest written code of Roman law, drawn up by a board of ten men, the decemviri, in 451–450 BCE in response to plebeian demands. They covered legal procedure, debt, family, property and crime.

tlingit.s: The Tlingit are an Indigenous people of the Pacific Northwest coast, living in south-east Alaska and neighbouring British Columbia. Organised in clans and known for their carving and potlatches, they resisted Russian expansion, destroying the fort at Sitka in 1802 before being…

tharapita.s: Tharapita is a god of the pre-Christian Estonians named in the Livonian Chronicle of Henry, written in the 1220s. Henry describes him as the great god of the Oeselians, born on a wooded hill in Virumaa, from where he flew to Saaremaa.

titus-tatius.s: Titus Tatius was, in Roman legend, the king of the Sabine town of Cures who made war on Rome after the abduction of the Sabine women. When the women intervened to end the fighting, he and Romulus agreed to rule jointly over a united people.

toki-yorinari.s: Toki Yorinari was the last of the Toki family to hold the office of military governor (shugo) of Mino province in Japan. Raised to power with the help of his retainer Saito Dosan, he was driven out by Dosan around 1542, and after a brief return with outside help he was finally…

tumshuqese-language.s: Tumshuqese is an extinct Eastern Iranian language of the Saka group, known from documents of about the 7th to 10th centuries found at Tumshuq on the northern edge of the Tarim Basin, in Xinjiang. It was written in a form of the Brahmi script and is closely related to…

takeno-joo.s: Takeno Jōō was a wealthy merchant of Sakai and one of the founders of the wabi style of the Japanese tea ceremony. Building on the ideas of Murata Jukō, he favoured small, simple rooms and plain, often Japanese-made utensils over costly Chinese pieces.

tournai.s: Tournai is a city in the province of Hainaut in western Belgium, on the Scheldt, and one of the oldest towns in the country. As Roman Tornacum it became the seat of the Salian Frankish kings in the 5th century; the tomb of Childeric I, father of Clovis, was found there in 1653.

tarom.s: Tarom is a mountainous district of Zanjan province in north-western Iran, in the valley of the Qezel Ozan river. In the 10th century it was the home of the Daylamite Sallarid dynasty, also called the Musafirids, whose fortress of Shamiran stood there and who for a time ruled…

tepsi-minaret.s: The Tepsi Minaret is a medieval minaret in the citadel of Erzurum in north-eastern Turkey, generally attributed to the Saltukid period of the 12th century. Built of brick on a stone base, it was later converted into a clock tower in the Ottoman period and remains a landmark of…

tercan.s: Tercan is a town in Erzincan province in eastern Turkey, on the road between Erzincan and Erzurum. In the 12th century it belonged to the Saltukids of Erzurum, and its best-known monument is the tomb of Mama Hatun, a Saltukid ruler, built around 1200 within an unusual circular…

teutomalius.s: Teutomalius was a king of the Salyes, a Celto-Ligurian people of lower Provence, in the 120s BCE. After Roman forces destroyed the Salyan stronghold of Entremont he fled to the Allobroges.

tewa.s: The Tewa are a group of Pueblo peoples of northern New Mexico who speak the Tewa language, a member of the Tanoan family. Their communities along the Rio Grande include Ohkay Owingeh, Santa Clara, San Ildefonso, Pojoaque, Nambé and Tesuque, and a Tewa community also lives at…

togha-temur.s: Togha Temür was a Mongol prince descended from Chinggis Khan's brother Jochi Qasar who claimed the throne of the Ilkhanate after the death of Abu Sa'id in 1335. Based in Gurgan and Mazandaran, he controlled much of Khorasan and was recognised as overlord for a time by the…

temwen-island.s: Temwen Island is a small island off the eastern coast of Pohnpei in the Federated States of Micronesia. On the reef beside it lies Nan Madol, a complex of nearly a hundred artificial islets built of basalt columns and coral, which served as the ceremonial and political centre…

tovsta-mohyla.s: Tovsta Mohyla is a Scythian royal burial mound of the 4th century BCE near the town of Pokrov in Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine. Excavated by Borys Mozolevsky in 1971, it yielded a gold pectoral decorated with scenes of Scythian daily life and of animals in combat, one of the…

tell-khaiber.s: Tell Khaiber is an archaeological site in southern Iraq, about 20 kilometres north-west of Ur, excavated from 2013 by the Ur Region Archaeology Project. Its principal building, a large fortified administrative complex, yielded an archive of cuneiform tablets from the First…

tsarevets.s: Tsarevets is a fortified hill in Veliko Tarnovo, Bulgaria, enclosed by a loop of the Yantra river, which served as the main citadel of the Second Bulgarian Empire from the late 12th century to 1393. Within its walls stood the royal palace and the patriarchal church, as well as…

theodoros-pangalos.s: Theodoros Pangalos was a Greek general who seized power in a coup in June 1925 and ruled the Second Hellenic Republic as dictator until August 1926. His regime suspended the constitution, made him president in 1926 and provoked a brief border clash with Bulgaria, the Incident…

trimontium.s: Trimontium was a Roman fort at Newstead, near Melrose in the Scottish Borders, named after the three peaks of the Eildon Hills. Founded around 80 CE during Agricola's campaigns, it was occupied in several phases until the late 2nd century and served as a key base on Dere Street.

tancred-prince-of-galilee.s: Tancred was an Italo-Norman leader of the First Crusade and a nephew of Bohemond of Taranto. After the capture of Jerusalem in 1099 he took Tiberias and Galilee and styled himself prince there.

tiz.s: Tiz was a medieval port on the Makran coast of south-eastern Iran, near modern Chabahar. From the 10th to the 13th century it served as a harbour for ships trading between the Persian Gulf, India and East Africa, linked by caravan routes to Kerman and Khurasan.

tervete-hillfort.s: Tērvete hillfort is an earthwork stronghold in southern Latvia, one of the main centres of the Semigallians in the 13th century. It was the seat of Semigallian rulers resisting the Livonian Order, and in 1281 the defenders burned and abandoned it.

tonawanda-band-of-seneca.s: The Tonawanda Band of Seneca is a federally recognised Seneca nation with a reservation near Akron in western New York. Unlike the Seneca Nation of Indians, which became an elected republic in 1848, it kept government by traditional hereditary chiefs.

treaty-of-big-tree.s: The Treaty of Big Tree was signed in 1797 at Geneseo, New York, between the Seneca and the financier Robert Morris. The Seneca sold their rights to most of their land west of the Genesee River for 100,000 dollars, keeping only a number of reservations.

thessaly.s: Thessaly is a region of central Greece, a broad fertile plain ringed by mountains, including Olympus and Pelion. In antiquity it was famed for its horses and cavalry, and its cities, among them Larissa and Pherae, formed the Thessalian League.

theophanes-the-confessor.s: Theophanes the Confessor was a Byzantine monk and chronicler whose Chronographia covers the history of the empire from 284 to 813. It is a key source for the 7th and 8th centuries, including the rise of Islam and the arrival of the Bulgars.

tilaurakot.s: Tilaurakot is an archaeological site in Kapilvastu district of southern Nepal, near Lumbini. Its walled city, with gates, a moat and building remains, is identified by many scholars, especially in Nepal, with ancient Kapilavastu, the home of the Buddha's Shakya clan.

the-bund.s: The Bund is the waterfront promenade along the west bank of the Huangpu River in central Shanghai. Laid out from 1845 as the river frontage of the British settlement, it became lined with the banks, trading houses, hotels and consulates of the foreign community, many in grand…

tuapse.s: Tuapse is a port city on the Black Sea coast of Krasnodar Krai, Russia. A Russian fort was built there in 1838 during the conquest of the Circassian coast, and the town grew after the Circassian expulsions of the 1860s.

tazeroualt.s: Tazeroualt is a region in the western Anti-Atlas of southern Morocco, south of the Sous valley. It holds the shrine of the 16th-century saint Sidi Ahmed ou Moussa, and in the 17th century his descendants made Iligh the capital of a sharifate that controlled caravan routes to…

tanegashima.s: Tanegashima is an island south of Kyushu, Japan, part of Kagoshima Prefecture. Portuguese traders shipwrecked there in 1543 brought the first European firearms to Japan, and the local lord had them copied, so that early Japanese matchlocks were called tanegashima.

tsuruoka.s: Tsuruoka is a city on the Shōnai plain of Yamagata Prefecture, Japan. From 1622 it was the castle town of the Sakai clan, lords of the Shōnai Domain, whose domain school, the Chidōkan, still stands.

tucume.s: Túcume is an archaeological complex in the Lambayeque valley of northern Peru, with 26 large adobe pyramids around a rocky hill. Built from around 1100 as the Late Sicán centre after Batán Grande was abandoned, it was later occupied by the Chimú and the Incas.

tennes.s: Tennes was king of Sidon in the mid-4th century BCE. Around 351 BCE he led the Phoenician cities in revolt against the Persian king Artaxerxes III, with Egyptian help.

thane.s: Thane is a city in Maharashtra, India, on the Thane creek just north-east of Mumbai. Known in medieval inscriptions as Sthanaka, it was a centre of the Silahara kings of the North Konkan and a port visited by Arab traders and Marco Polo.

tell-kazel.s: Tell Kazel is an archaeological mound in the Akkar plain of western Syria, near the Lebanese border and the Mediterranean coast. Excavations since the 1980s have uncovered Bronze and Iron Age levels, and most scholars identify the site with Sumur, the Simyra of classical sources.

treaty-of-concordia.s: The Treaty of Concordia, signed on 23 March 1648, divided the Caribbean island of Saint Martin between France and the Dutch Republic after the Spanish garrison had left. The French received the larger northern part and the Dutch the southern part with its salt ponds.

tai-tham-script.s: The Tai Tham script, also called the Lanna script, is a writing system derived from the Mon script and used since about the 14th century for Northern Thai, Tai Lue, Tai Khün and Lao religious texts. Its name, 'Dharma script', reflects its use for Buddhist scriptures written on…

thomas-jones-missionary.s: Thomas Jones (1810–1849) was a Welsh Calvinistic Methodist missionary who arrived in the Khasi Hills of north-east India in 1841. Working from Sohra (Cherrapunji), he wrote the Khasi language in the Latin alphabet, prepared the first Khasi reading books and translations, and…

transitional-federal-government.s: The Transitional Federal Government was the internationally recognised government of Somalia from 2004 to 2012. Formed at peace talks in Kenya, with a parliament chosen by clan quotas, it struggled to control even Mogadishu and depended on Ethiopian troops and then on the…

transitional-national-government.s: The Transitional National Government was an interim government of Somalia formed in 2000 at a peace conference at Arta in Djibouti, the first attempt at a national government since the state collapsed in 1991. Led by President Abdiqasim Salad Hassan, it controlled only parts…

tel-river.s: The Tel is a river of western Odisha in eastern India and one of the main southern tributaries of the Mahanadi. Its basin covers much of the Kalahandi and Balangir districts, and it joins the Mahanadi at Sonepur, a temple town that grew up at the confluence.

thatta.s: Thatta is a historic city in Sindh, Pakistan, near the Indus delta about 100 km east of Karachi. It was the capital of lower Sindh under the Samma, Arghun and Tarkhan dynasties from the 14th to the 17th century, and a centre of trade and learning.

tellumpoccoe.s: The Tellumpoccoe ('three powers') was an alliance of the Bugis kingdoms of Bone, Wajo and Soppeng in South Sulawesi, sworn in 1582 at Timurung to resist the expansion of the Makassar kingdom of Gowa. Bone was recognised as the eldest brother, Wajo the middle and Soppeng the…

thesprotia.s: Thesprotia is a region of Epirus in north-western Greece, on the Ionian coast opposite Corfu, today a regional unit with its capital at Igoumenitsa. In antiquity it was the land of the Thesprotians, with the oracle of the dead (Necromanteion) on the Acheron river.

tufa-poqiang.s: Tufa Poqiang was a prince of the Southern Liang, a Xianbei kingdom in Qinghai, and the son of its last ruler Tufa Rutan. After Western Qin destroyed Southern Liang in 414 he fled to the Northern Wei, whose Tuoba rulers shared his clan's origins; they gave him the name Yuan He,…

treaty-of-shaoxing.s: The Treaty of Shaoxing of 1141 ended the wars between the Southern Song dynasty and the Jurchen Jin dynasty. It fixed the frontier along the Huai River, made the Song emperor a vassal of the Jin and obliged the Song to pay an annual tribute of silver and silk.

tinian.s: Tinian is one of the three main islands of the Northern Mariana Islands in the western Pacific, just south-west of Saipan. Under Japanese rule it was covered with sugar plantations.

turkish-armenian-war.s: The Turkish–Armenian War was fought from September to December 1920 between the Turkish nationalist forces of the Grand National Assembly and the First Republic of Armenia. Turkish troops under Kâzım Karabekir took Kars and Alexandropol, and Armenia was forced to sign the…

terentii-shtykov.s: Terentii Shtykov (1907–1964) was a Soviet colonel general and party official who directed the Soviet occupation of northern Korea from 1945. As the senior political officer of the occupying forces he supervised the Soviet Civil Administration, the rise of Kim Il Sung and the…

tamsui.s: Tamsui is a coastal district of New Taipei at the mouth of the Tamsui River in northern Taiwan. The Spanish built Fort Santo Domingo there in 1628, later rebuilt by the Dutch, whose Fort Antonio still stands.

third-treaty-of-san-ildefonso.s: The Third Treaty of San Ildefonso was a secret agreement signed on 1 October 1800 by which Spain returned Louisiana to France. In exchange Napoleon promised a kingdom in Italy, Etruria, for the son-in-law of King Charles IV of Spain.

tarfaya.s: Tarfaya is a small town on the Atlantic coast of southern Morocco, beside Cape Juby. Under the name Villa Bens it was the centre of the southern zone of the Spanish protectorate, the Tarfaya Strip between the Draa River and the 27th parallel.

thirty-comrades.s: The Thirty Comrades were young Burmese nationalists, led by Aung San, who received secret military training from the Japanese on Hainan in 1941. In December 1941 they founded the Burma Independence Army in Bangkok and entered Burma with the Japanese invasion of 1942.

tennessee.s: Tennessee is a state in the south-eastern United States, with its capital at Nashville. Settled west of the Appalachians from the 1760s, the region was ceded by North Carolina to the federal government in 1790 and admitted as the sixteenth state in 1796, with John Sevier as…

tegucigalpa.s: Tegucigalpa is the capital and largest city of Honduras, in a highland valley of the south-centre. It grew from a silver-mining settlement founded in 1578, and after independence it rivalled Comayagua as the seat of government until it became the permanent capital in 1880.

tianma-qucun-site.s: The Tianma-Qucun site is a large archaeological site in southern Shanxi province, China, between the villages of Tianma and Qucun near Houma. Excavations since the 1960s, and especially of the Beizhao cemetery from 1992, revealed the tombs of the early marquises of Jin and…

three-huan.s: The Three Huan were the Jisun, Mengsun and Shusun, three ministerial families of the State of Lu descended from sons of Duke Huan of Lu. From the sixth century BCE they controlled most of Lu's land and armies, dividing the state's forces among themselves and reducing the dukes…

tamim-bin-hamad-al-thani.s: Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani (born 1980) has been emir of Qatar since June 2013, when his father, Hamad bin Khalifa, abdicated in his favour. Educated at Sandhurst, he led the country through the blockade imposed by Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Egypt from…

toribio-montes.s: Toribio Montes was a Spanish general sent by the viceroy of Peru to put down the autonomous government of Quito. His forces took Quito in November 1812 and destroyed the last patriot army at Ibarra in December.

talamone.s: Talamone is a small coastal village in southern Tuscany, in the comune of Orbetello. Near it the Romans destroyed a large Gallic army at the Battle of Telamon in 225 BCE.

taihang-mountains.s: The Taihang Mountains are a range in northern China running about 400 km north to south between the Shanxi plateau and the North China Plain of Hebei and Henan. Their passes controlled the routes between plateau and plain, and in the Zhou period the uplands were home to the Di…

tengzhou.s: Tengzhou is a county-level city in southern Shandong, in Zaozhuang prefecture. It lies on the sites of the Zhou-period states of Teng and Xue, whose old city walls survive nearby.

temple-of-mencius.s: The Temple of Mencius is a temple complex in Zoucheng, Shandong, dedicated to the philosopher Mencius. First built under the Song dynasty in the 11th century and later moved to its present site, it is a large group of halls and courtyards modelled on the Temple of Confucius at…

tsarevo.s: Tsarevo is a town on the Black Sea coast of south-eastern Bulgaria, in Burgas Province near the Strandzha mountains. As Vasiliko it was a centre of the Strandzha Commune during the Preobrazhenie Uprising of 1903, and it passed to Bulgaria after the Balkan Wars.

tayyibi-ismailism.s: Tayyibi Isma'ilism is the branch of Musta'li Isma'ili Shi'ism that recognises al-Tayyib, the infant son of the Fatimid caliph al-Amir, as imam after 1130. Backed by the Sulayhid queen Arwa in Yemen, it holds that the imam went into concealment and is represented by a da'i…

tenes.s: Ténès is a port town on the Mediterranean coast of Algeria, in Chlef Province west of Algiers. Founded by the Phoenicians as Cartennae, it became a Roman colony, and in the 9th and 10th centuries it was held by princes of the Sulaymanid branch of the Idrisid family.

tegama.s: Tegama was sultan of Agadez in the Aïr region of present-day Niger in the early 20th century. In 1916–1917 he joined the Tuareg revolt led by Kaocen against French rule, during which the French garrison of Agadez was besieged for months.

tanimoune.s: Tanimoune dan Souleymane was sultan of Damagaram, with its capital at Zinder, in the mid and later 19th century, until 1884. He threw off the overlordship of Bornu, built up an army with firearms and locally made cannon, and enlarged the sultanate by conquest.

tsingoni.s: Tsingoni is a town on the west coast of Mayotte in the Comoros archipelago and the former seat of its sultans. Its Friday mosque, dated by an inscription to 1538, is among the oldest mosques still in use in the region and was later restored.

thuwaini-bin-said.s: Thuwaini bin Said was sultan of Muscat and Oman from 1856 to 1866. The eldest surviving son of Said ibn Sultan, he inherited the Arabian lands while his brother Majid took Zanzibar; a planned expedition against Zanzibar was halted by Britain, and the Canning Award of 1861…

treaty-of-seeb.s: The Treaty of Seeb was an agreement concluded in 1920, through British mediation, between the Sultan of Muscat and the tribal leaders of the Ibadi Imamate of Oman in the interior. It ended the fighting that had begun with the imamate's rising in 1913 and left the interior…

tarusbawa.s: Tarusbawa is remembered in later Sundanese tradition as the founder of the Sunda Kingdom of western Java. According to texts such as the Carita Parahyangan tradition, in 669 he took the western part of the former Tarumanagara lands, while the eastern part beyond the Citarum…

treaty-of-stockholm-1813.s: The Treaty of Stockholm of 3 March 1813 was an alliance between Britain and Sweden against Napoleon. Sweden, led by Crown Prince Charles John, agreed to send an army to fight in Germany, and Britain promised subsidies, supported Swedish ambitions to acquire Norway and ceded…

truce-of-plussa.s: The Truce of Plussa was signed in August 1583 on the Plyussa River between Sweden and Russia, ending the fighting between them in the Livonian War. Sweden kept its conquests in Estonia, including Narva, and the Ingrian fortresses of Ivangorod, Yam and Koporye.

treaty-of-malmo-1803.s: The Treaty of Malmö of 1803 was an agreement by which Sweden pawned the city of Wismar, with the island of Poel and the district of Neukloster, to the Duke of Mecklenburg-Schwerin for 1,250,000 riksdaler for 100 years. Sweden never redeemed the pledge, and in 1903 it formally…

ticino.s: Ticino is the southernmost canton of Switzerland and its main Italian-speaking region, with Bellinzona as its capital and Lugano and Locarno as its largest towns. Its valleys were conquered from Milan by the Swiss cantons between the 15th and 16th centuries and ruled as…

ticino-river.s: The Ticino is a river that rises in the Swiss Alps, flows through the canton of Ticino and Lake Maggiore, and then runs south through Lombardy to join the Po just below Pavia. Its lower course formed a frontier between Lombardy and Piedmont, and in 218 BCE Hannibal defeated…

telys.s: Telys was a popular leader of the Greek city of Sybaris in southern Italy who, around 510 BCE, persuaded the citizens to expel the wealthiest men and confiscate their property. The exiles fled to Croton, which refused to give them up.

tuwati.s: Tuwati was a king of Tabal in south-central Anatolia in the 8th century BCE, named in Luwian hieroglyphic inscriptions and in Assyrian records of Tiglath-Pileser III, to whom he paid tribute in 738 BCE. He appears as a leading ruler among the many kings of Tabal, and his son…

tagalog-language.s: Tagalog is an Austronesian language of the central Philippines, spoken natively around Manila and in southern Luzon. It was the language of the Katipunan and the revolution of 1896.

tejeros-convention.s: The Tejeros Convention was a meeting of Filipino revolutionaries held at Tejeros in Cavite on 22 March 1897 to settle the rivalry between the Magdalo and Magdiwang factions of the Katipunan. It elected Emilio Aguinaldo president of a revolutionary government in place of Andrés…

treaty-of-alcaraz.s: The Treaty of Alcaraz of 1243 placed the Muslim kingdom of Murcia under the protection of Castile. Its ruler Muhammad ibn Hud, under pressure from Granada and Aragon, agreed with the infante Alfonso, the future Alfonso X, to accept Castilian garrisons and pay tribute while…

treaty-of-capdepera.s: The Treaty of Capdepera of 1231 made Muslim Menorca a tributary of James I of Aragon. Agreed at Capdepera on Majorca after the Aragonese conquest of that island, it let Menorca's Muslims keep their own rulers, law and religion in return for recognising James as overlord and…

tavira.s: Tavira is a town on the Gilão river near the Ria Formosa lagoon in the eastern Algarve, southern Portugal. Under Muslim rule it was a fortified port and briefly an independent taifa in the 1140s, and in 1242 the Order of Santiago under Paio Peres Correia took it for Portugal.

toledan-tables.s: The Toledan Tables were astronomical tables compiled in Toledo in the later 11th century by scholars led by al-Zarqali (Arzachel) under the patronage of al-Mamun. Used to predict the positions of the Sun, Moon and planets, they were translated into Latin in the 12th century…

tay-bac-autonomous-region.s: The Tây Bắc Autonomous Region was an autonomous region of North Vietnam covering the mountainous north-west, home to Tai, Hmong and other minority peoples. Created in 1955 as the Thái–Mèo Autonomous Region after the Geneva Accords gave the area to North Vietnam, it was renamed…

taipei.s: Taipei is the capital and largest city of Taiwan, in the Taipei Basin in the north of the island. It grew in the 18th and 19th centuries from Han Chinese settlements and was walled by the Qing in the 1880s.

tursunzoda.s: Tursunzoda is a city in western Tajikistan near the Uzbek border, west of Dushanbe. It grew around a large aluminium smelter opened in the 1970s, now run by the state company TALCO and one of the country's main exporters.

takamatsu.s: Takamatsu is a port city on the Seto Inland Sea, capital of Kagawa Prefecture on the island of Shikoku, Japan. It grew around a sea castle begun by Ikoma Chikamasa in 1588, whose moats were fed by seawater, and was the seat of the Matsudaira lords of the Takamatsu Domain…

tsutsujigasaki-castle.s: Tsutsujigasaki was the fortified residence of the Takeda clan in Kai Province, Japan, built by Takeda Nobutora in 1519 in what became the town of Kōfu. It was the seat of Takeda Shingen and was abandoned after his son Katsuyori moved to the new Shinpu Castle in 1581.

talivaldis.s: Tālivaldis (died 1215) was the ruler of Tālava, a Latgalian principality in north-eastern Latvia, known from the chronicle of Henry of Livonia. Formerly a tributary of Pskov, he accepted Latin baptism with his sons around 1208 and allied with the German crusaders against the…

talysh.s: Talysh is a historical region on the south-western shore of the Caspian Sea, divided between south-eastern Azerbaijan and Iran's Gilan and Ardabil provinces. Home of the Talysh people, who speak a north-western Iranian language, it has humid forested mountains and fertile…
